No good deed will go unpunished, no milestone reached undone, and no time spent having fun. I'm not understanding how this game can be enjoyable given the prevalence of script-kiddies and KoS insanity. This on top of the clunky combat system that makes targetting an opponent a game of risk/barely a reward. Until this game's mechanics, and especially the ability to kick out hackers, are improved, I can't recommend this. Get it when it's finished, if it has improved by then.
EDIT: I wrote this review about a year ago, and really nothing has changed. The game has good potential to be an interesting dynamic community building game. But there is just no moderation, even STILL. I paid 20 dollars for this in pre-release and I regret it. Valve's lackluster refund policy is the only reason I haven't demanded one yet. I've sunk too many hours in for my own good to only have my progress undone by hackers ganking away all of my progress. Every. Single. Time.
Absolutely stay away from this trash.

This game... it's like trying to run a Ferrari on Potato fuel.
First of all, the game posses a wide variety of soundtrack and BGM, each unique and changes depending on what map or battles you were in. This shows that the Developer (or atleast the original Developers a.k.a Koreans) had a vast access to manpower and tools in order to generate all of these beautifully composed musics. They're an essential if you were to indulge yourself fully into each of the gameplay.
Now, the art part. Majestic, beautiful and gives a nostalgic vibe for veteran MMORPG players who missed the Ragnarok days. The sheer pixel of each everything, varying from backgrounds to mobs' heads, you won't find anything that does not fit anywhere, other than also allowing you to appreciate how detailed the surrounding really are.
But that's where all the kisses and praises ends.
As far as I have went into the gameplay itself, I could say of one thing. Their server runs on potato. There are major lags hopping on you everywhere, you can't hide from them. You'd get disconnected at times for no reason, failing to enter your specific server etc. etc. This drastically affect the whole gameplay itself since it interrupts your playing experience.
Now, this is one thing that I hate the most. Token users. Seriously? I mean, if it's extra exp buff, movement speeds and things as such, I'd probably find myself unfazed and let it slip past by. But to be a token user so that you can trade between players (OH and not to mention the 30 times limit and the fact that you can only trade between Token users?) Come on, what in the heck is MMORPG when you can't trade between players?
The commission for using the Market is also neck-choking. 30% of your sale price is a pretty big bite out of nowhere, just to end up turning into useless codes. Again, this may be decreased to half if you were a Token user, thus leading me to believe it's there just to be another 'fish-bob' for players to buy Tokens.
There are more flaws than I could handle to mention, but as the Developers are actively doing their best to fix the game to be a better day for everyone, I can't help but to give them another chance. Thumbs up for them, and hopefully, for the better future of the game. I'd hate to let go of this game, not when it reminds me so much of Ragnarok.
I will edit this review as time passes by, so do your best Developers, don't fail our hopes and hypes.
23/4/2016 EDIT:-
Seriously Developers? Raising the price of the Early Access Packages, other than also getting the 3rd one out of the shelves? After looking at the prices of these DLCs, they're like 3x times the previous price! Trying to cover it all up with a 50% sale? What a disgrace, I'm utterly disappointed. If this is an attempt to stop bot from spreading, then I rather say this is an attempt to get more money from Early Access Users.
OH AND LOOK AT THAT, PUSHING THE F2P RELEASE DATE? Lame, Developers. Lame. You may say that this is to provide more time for bug fixing and calibrating, but what I see here is yet another attempt to squeeze more money from future DLC buyers.
But guess what? With all these 'good' reviews exploding, your future seem bleak, my friends. It was such a great game, but sadly, it fell into the hands of stupid devils.

Alien: Isolation is such a great game.  I don't understand why it didn't sell better.  It isn't perfect, but it has a little something for everyone.  The story is partly a re-hash of the first few movies, but hey it worked for Star Wars: The Force Awekens.  It can be scary.  It can be exciting.  It is just really fun being an actual part of the Alien universe.  There is a lot more to it than hiding from the alien.  There are creepy robots and untrustworthy humans.  You can sneak.  You can plan attacks.  You can go in guns blazing.  You can throw a noise maker at a group of bad guys and the alien might just take care of them for you.  It is a very clever game.  If it gets too tough or scary you can turn the difficulty down so far that when the alien sees you he basically just walks up to you and hands you a beer.
It has elements of all my favorite recent horror games: Dead Space, The Evil Within, Outlast, and SOMA.
Oh, and if you haven't played SOMA, shame on you!  Go do that right now!  It could be described as a walking simulator, but it is a great sci-fi "horror" experience.  Don't read about it, just get it.  Or at least put it on your wish list for when it is on sale.
And get Alien: Isolation too.

I play video games for stories like this; it weaves a tale that may retread familiar territory but by allowing us play through the point of view of a lead with almost choral narration is spectacular for anyone who happens to enjoy the odd and reticent storyline. Through the silent protagonist we get to understand the world through her actions and gleam most of the interesting backstory through what we stop and take the time to reflect upon. It is easy to skim through this game and just write it off as a decent attempt to fuse art, narrative and gameplay. However it would be a disservice to the audience/ player to do so. Is the gameplay as absolutely refined as it could be? No, it is unique with the tactical options yet the world and the abilities you are offered are sometimes not intuitive to initiate in every battle sequence. Yet again this is only a minor quibble the animation is great yet the backgrounds are sometimes too static which is a shame; yet it runs beautifully on my PC. The soundtrack is another major selling point stop whatever it is you are doing go find it listen to it if nothing else. In summation this is a game I would recommend to anyone.
It's a great game. Period.

STORY:
I'm more than a little dissapointed with this game. I loved their last game Bastion and like Bastion, Transistor tells an interesting story through neration. The problem is that the naration doesn't come close to telling as much story as well as Bastion did and the rest of the story you have to peice together yourself from reading unrelated text blocks that are attached to your weapon upgrades. If you're not playing close attention to the cryptic neration, and read all the text boxes from upgrades, and read all the text boxes from the news stands, you'll have no idea what's going on. I liked what little story there was but half a story wasn't doing it for me.
GAMEPLAY:
Also unlike Bastion the combat isn't skillful, fast-paced, or even fun. Transistor has this silly turn-based element where you press spacebar and go around planning an attack that half the time doesn't even kill one enemy and that's the only way to play the game because it's the only way to avoid taking damage and your attacks take so damn long to wind up and they so little dammage.
CONCLUTION: I just couldn't finish this game because their wasn't enough story for me to care much about what everthe hell was going on and the gameplay was boaring and unsatisfying.

I purchased Transistor without having played Bastion.  I was drawn in by the art style and potentially unique experience and story.
The game utilizes a very clean and clever skill system where you can combine the skills you unlock in more than one function, much like Diablo 3.  The game is broken into stages for combat with directed storytelling but each component of the story is very interesting.  Additionally, each skill has storylines of the "functions" you absorb, unveiling side stories as you progress through the main one.
I was blown away by this game, there is so much more to go on for what you get in a $20 package.  From the art style, effects, to the voice acting and perfectly (literally perfect) timed sequences, I give Transistor a 10/10.  The only drawback is that the game is relatively short, coming in around 4 hours average to complete.  You can replay the game in Recurse mode, which increases the inherent difficulty of the enemies as you continue your character progression.
Transistor is one of the finest examples of creativity in the video game medium.
A game has never tugged more at my emotions. Play it.

I have thousand hours in this game, I know what I'm talking, so here's my final review.
Dark Souls is very known for being a difficult game. Not because it forces you to be pixel perfect or have insane fast reaction time. It just doesn't tell you how things work, and you have to figure out about things by yourself. So if you like to explore and learn by trial, it's a great game.
There are two things that got the fans of the series disappointed. One of them is the E3 footage they showed us. Where they promissed a really, really good looking game with a lot of atmosfere and interesting level design. The final product had different graphics, level design was dumbed down and it♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off people. And now they promise they will deliver better graphics and multiplayer if we pay for it. Great!
Second thing is that a lot of people complain the game isn't very hard as the previous ones. It's partially true. While the game won't feel as much difficult if you had played a previous Souls game, most of the bosses were really lazy and you could beat them by doing the same tactics over and over.
Here comes a spoiler about how to beat bosses and most enemies, so you better skip this paragraph... You can just run to their back and hit after they attack combo. That's it! The bosses are oversized enemies just to scare you, and they lack AoE attacks to keep players away from their backs!
About the DLC, it's the only good part of the game, really. Level design is great! You can see places you will reach or have passed by, while you progress. You look behind and see that bonfired you rested at, you look forward and see an area that you will reach later (or not, some of them are hidden areas).
Most bosses are great and challenging, because they have a large variety of attacks, and attacks that can get you offguard if you try to use that tactic I mentioned before.
You will have fun playing it, that's for sure! Just don't close your eyes to the problems this game has, and to the fact the developers suddenly decided to change a lot of things they showed us, without saying a word about it.

This game can be put in the Action-RPG genre.
But a category has its limits. So let's describe it a bit more precisely.
Dark Souls 2 puts you in the role of a lone adventurer thrown in a dark-fantasy world where dealing with pitfalls and enemies demand skill and reasoning. Combat is both stats-based and skill-based. Stats are leveled up with the same curency that weapons are bought and repaired with : souls dropped from monsters.
The skill needed in combat and in navigating the terrain is one reason the game is regarded as a difficult one. The other is the punishing loss of all souls after an unsuccessful retrieval attempt.
While enemies are usually tough and the world is at times tricky to navigate, the game does a good job of connecting you with hints and warnings of dangerous zones left by players who experience the same challenges in their parallel world. One can also stumble upon signs offering help for tough fights when certain conditions are met. The player who offered his help is then loaded into the host's world and can assist in the difficult boss fight.
The game world is beautifully designed. Enemies and friendly characters are numerous and varied. They are believeable. The challenges are great. This is clearly an atmospheric game.
There is also different player-vs-player features in the game. Fun challenges as they may be, these challenges can be alleviated with in-game choices.

Elder Scrolls Online is, as of 2017, an excellent MMO with an Elder Scrolls theme. The game encourages exploration, combat is enjoyable, the amount of available content is staggering and most of it is doable both alone and with friends. Though the game is ultimately an MMO, it is a good one.
It gets a lot of the Elder Scrolls feel right. It might not be a single player Elder Scrolls RPG, but it is good in it's own right and I would recommend it.
- Voice acting for every NPC and quest,
- Quests are good, barely any of the usual MMO stuff,
(game's better than most of Skyrim there)
- Combat is varied. Light and heavy attacks, with blocking and dodging,
- Player freedom. Content is leveled to player level,
- Thievery, assassination and player housing make feel less like an MMO.
- Little to no instancing. Players can run about killing bosses,
- No explanation for most things. Somewhat obscure without Wiki,
- User interface. Get add-ons
,
- Cash shop. Not the worst, but for example: you can train your horse to run faster up to 60 times, but training is limited to once a day. And it is not shared across characters. Or, you could max training for cash in a day.
Overall as far as MMOs go, it's a very enjoyable one. A lot of systems such as thievery and allowing murdering NPCs make the game feel more unique and make good use of the Elder Scrolls theme. It isn't perfect, but it is a good one none the less.

Great game.  Mostly it was emotional.  Everything that Supergiant got right with Bastion was multiplied times ten.  The voice acting is amazing, so much more personal than Bastion, and continues to immerse.  The OST is not as diverse, but overall better themed and works more to the feel of the game.  The songs with vocals are phenomenal, and normally vocals turn me right off.
Now the combat, which is what makes up the vast majority of the game is really neat.  Supergiant opted to experiment and hit the ball right out of the park.  Only four abilites can be on your bar at once, but extra abilities can be used to fill either buff slots to the active abilities or as passives on your character, and with 16 abilities, this leads to lots and lots of customization that the game encourages you to play around with, as having the ability in each function unlocks codex entries about the people in town.  And then the Turn() system is pretty cool.  It's a way of mixing up the whole idea of turn-based vs real-time combat.  Basically, you can either run around, using abilities in real-time, which puts you at a disadvantage, or you pause, queue up a bunch of abilities, use them with super speed, but then are extremely vulnerable for a few seconds afterwards.  The goal is to destroy enemies before you go vulnerable.  It works really well, and gets incredibly fun when the game starts throwing large groups of enemies that all require different strategies to take down.
Anyways, the gameplay is innovative and fun, the story insanely emotional, for $20 there is zero reason not to play this game (yes I know it will be cheap on sale at some point, ♥♥♥♥ off).

I purchased Transistor without having played Bastion.  I was drawn in by the art style and potentially unique experience and story.
The game utilizes a very clean and clever skill system where you can combine the skills you unlock in more than one function, much like Diablo 3.  The game is broken into stages for combat with directed storytelling but each component of the story is very interesting.  Additionally, each skill has storylines of the "functions" you absorb, unveiling side stories as you progress through the main one.
I was blown away by this game, there is so much more to go on for what you get in a $20 package.  From the art style, effects, to the voice acting and perfectly (literally perfect) timed sequences, I give Transistor a 10/10.  The only drawback is that the game is relatively short, coming in around 4 hours average to complete.  You can replay the game in Recurse mode, which increases the inherent difficulty of the enemies as you continue your character progression.
Transistor is one of the finest examples of creativity in the video game medium.

This game can be put in the Action-RPG genre.
But a category has its limits. So let's describe it a bit more precisely.
Dark Souls 2 puts you in the role of a lone adventurer thrown in a dark-fantasy world where dealing with pitfalls and enemies demand skill and reasoning. Combat is both stats-based and skill-based. Stats are leveled up with the same curency that weapons are bought and repaired with : souls dropped from monsters.
The skill needed in combat and in navigating the terrain is one reason the game is regarded as a difficult one. The other is the punishing loss of all souls after an unsuccessful retrieval attempt.
While enemies are usually tough and the world is at times tricky to navigate, the game does a good job of connecting you with hints and warnings of dangerous zones left by players who experience the same challenges in their parallel world. One can also stumble upon signs offering help for tough fights when certain conditions are met. The player who offered his help is then loaded into the host's world and can assist in the difficult boss fight.
The game world is beautifully designed. Enemies and friendly characters are numerous and varied. They are believeable. The challenges are great. This is clearly an atmospheric game.
There is also different player-vs-player features in the game. Fun challenges as they may be, these challenges can be alleviated with in-game choices.

People can say whatever they want about 3D Sonic games, but one thing's for sure. I'll always love them.

I wanted to believe there could be another decent Sonic game coming out. I played Sonic Colors and Generations. I played the old Adventure games back in the day and I've played them again on Steam to remind me of those times. So I bought the game on release, something I don't normally do.
Most of the levels are straight forward "Hold boost to win." They are not challenging at all and the wisp weapons only serve to make them way too easy to navigate. You can basically go through all of them just holding boost and hitting homing attack when you see the cursor pop up. They are mostly unmemorable and finish in the blink of an eye if the game doesn't kill you for one reason or another.
The story cuts to Eggman taking over the world with a screen of text. The story becomes rather forgettable and none of the writing really stands out. The main bad guy doesn't get fleshed out at all.
Perhaps the only things this game has is Sonic characters and a decent soundtrack. I like the Sonic characters. But if this wasn't a Sonic game, the game would be really bland.
After taking the 4 hours it does it takes to beat the game there really isn't anything that makes me want to play it again.
All that said, Sonic Forces isn't a terrible, broken mess. The presentation is good at least. The gameplay, not so much.
But I paid the same price for Persona 5, and got over 100 hours out of that.

Sonic and Autism
A Synopsis
What I aim to do in this case study is to show the link between the famous video game character Sonic the Hedgehog and children diagnosed with autism.
First let me go into the research I found so there is a better understanding of what I'm saying, some may take this as a joke and That's fine but I am dead serious. Let take a look at Sonic’s color palette, it consists of blue, red, white, black, gold, and green it's a set of colors that could only attract an autistic child. “There is certainly a general consensus that TD children have a preference for primary colors (such as red and blue) rather than secondary colors (such as pink and orange). As the possible functional significance of such color-preference, moreover, the need to discriminate subtle changes in skin color of other persons due to their emotional states (e.g., an angry face is reddish and a sad face is blue) has been argued (Changizi et al., 2006).” The colors that make up Sonic are many primary ones so this could be one explanation with autistic children liking the blue blur.
Second I would like to talk about sonic's ability to easily relate to the autistic children due to his simple black and white character design. I think it's best put in Kongregate user DeathAndSyntaxes words, “Black-and-white morality is so easy to understand that even an autist can follow what’s going on. He can place himself on the hero’s side, watch the hero win, and feel joy at seeing his side win. There’s no need for subtlety, which is necessary for almost every good book, show, movie, or play, but the autist can digest it.” It's an easy character to understand there is no complex story nor crazy character development, sonic is simple so it is easy For the child with low mental capacity to grasp and enjoy.
Third it’s the hedgehog’s personality that may attract the children, sonic tries to be the cool video game character and if he's cool the children may think that liking him would make them cool. Kiwi farms user Henry Bemis said “Sonic's popularity among the socially challenged - be they autistic or just plain dim - might be because liking him allows them to be "cool" by proxy. One of the most consistent factors of "coolness" being a sense of rebellion, coloring outside the lines, that sort of thing, something that is undoubtedly hard to comprehend if your brain is rigidly wired (or, again, just plain dim). Sonic goes fast and thumbs his tiny nose at bumbling fools and utmost evils and saves the world and gets the girl, so he's cool.” I think this best gets at what I'm talking about liking something they think is cool to be cool, and sonic makes these children feel cool.
In conclusion I hope my evidence is good enough to convince that not only is Sonic a video game icon but comforting tool for those less fortunate in cognitive sense in our world today.

This gives a nice feature as the game environment changes as he tells his story, for example, Greaves mentions he was surrounded by appaches, one of the men in the bar asks, what apaches? what happened to the cowboys? then the gunfight turn aroudn as your now surrounded by cowboys, claiming they attacked you APACHE STYLE.
The gameplay is pretty basic run and gun, with Concentration mode which slows down time and marks enemies red, as we know from previous Call of Juarez games.
The graphics are pretty nice to look at and also not too demanding as I'm playing this on my faster outdating rig and are Borderlands style with those edges, which certainly serves the game right. Blood and headshots are quite satisfying to see too.
A leveling system is also implemented which can unlock dual wielding, super fast reloads, a Crusader armor like Ray McCal had in Bound in Blood and legendary weapons which are gold/silver and boost damage, accuracy or lower recoil. I give this game an 8/10 and a really nice reboot of Call of Juarez for the sharp price of €15

This game is great. While the graphics are definitely not perfect, they aren't bad either. They give a more than good enough view of the landscape and surroundings, but I'm not here to just talk about that. The feel of this game is spot on for the lore that they are trying to give. The firefights are tense and challenging, and extremely rewarding when you come out on top, especially in the beginning when they hand you trash and tell you to take out groups of bandits. This feeling does fade some when you move to more effective equipment, but its still a rush to get into shooting matches with enemies. The mechanics are really good as well. They work well, and while this game is not necessarily a first point survival game, the elements are worked in very well, such as hunger, bleeding, and radiation. Overall, this is a very good game, which I would recommend to anyone that likes challenges in shooters, or at least not having running and gunning to be the best strategy. You have to play smart to live through these fights. One thing I would like to point out though, is that to really make this game stellar, the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Complete mod should be installed. It just takes everything, and makes it feel more finished than it already is. Slightly smoothed and adjusted textures, adjusted names from game names to real names for weapons, items and the like. Stuff like that. It just makes an already good game great.

I waited since this was announced in 2013 overseas. I purchased the $49.99 pack, I have played more than 65 hours listed and the betas. I love Ragnarok Online very much and this game was made from essentially the same Executive and Creative persons, so it is HEAVILY influenced in gameplay.  All my opinions are my own and are from the April 3,2016 version. There will be differences of opinions of what I list.  Take it as you will before you dive into this very, very big game.
Pros:
1. It has an enjoyable class system where you pick a base class and advance from there (Archer, Swordsman, Cleric, Wizard) Very reminiscent to Ragnarok Online.
2. The storage system the game gives you is very ample and have yet to run out of room.
3. The music in this game is varied and superb.
4. There is an item collection system in place which will give you a listed passive buff when completed.
5. The art style is pleasing to the eye and the environments are very diverse when travelling.  The monsters I've seen thus far compliment this and am pleased so far.
6. The aspects of this game when "subscribed" is very helpful as for the items it hands you.
Now for the Cons.  They will be listed as such they will compliment the Pro numbers first and so on because there are ADDITIONAL CONS.
TP POINTS = REAL MONEY
1. Picking between the four classes is easy.  Class advancement is not.  There are over 80 CHARACTER CLASSES. Advancement to the next is permanent! NO RESET ON ADVANCEMENT! Choose carefully or else you will need to reroll your character. If you put a point into a skill you did not want and hit Accept, you are stuck with it unless you pay TP for skill reset potion. I seriously recommend a skill simulator to plan out your advancement and skill progression or else you will need to reroll your character or spend real money.
2. The Item storage is ample, but every time you place or take an item out of storage, it charges you 30 silver (Even for Premium users).  This may seem like a small amount, but it adds up.  The item storage is character specific and trade between characters is almost non-existant.  You have one space to trade gear between characters and even then, it penalizes you by reducing the Potential by one (a whole other aspect I won't get into, Wiki it if you want to learn more, but a very important number when upgrading equipment!)
3. Music is great, but this is a grindy game by nature...hearing a specific dungeon song for 30+ times when in an area grinds your teeth.
4. Item collection sets. You have to be in town and talk to a very specific NPC to add a collection Tome and/or items to a set you are in progress of collecting.  This is very inconvenient and not at all user friendly.  I am not in town very often so I had to force myself to remember this when returning to do my daily chores of repairing, skill advancement, item storage.
5.  No con to this
6. Differences of F2P and Premium users of this game is VERY SEVERE. Only going to list the two biggest.
Want to trade between users in this game? NOT ALLOWED between F2P and a Premie. Only between Premies and only 30 per MONTH. Want to trade in the market?  that will be 30% market commission for a F2P and 10% for Premie. I take it that these measures are in place to get money and to stave off scam sites selling gold but at this point in time...the spam hasn't slowed.
7. The websites selling in game currency spam...OH GOD, THE SPAM. The game hasn't even released to the public yet and they are in full force! This game has an item called a Megaphone, it costs 1 TP in the TP shop per megaphone.  This essentially is a consumable item that allows the user to say something to the whole server. THE. WHOLE. SERVER.  It also scrolls it on the top of your screen (you can disable that in options but come on...)  Initially it was not character length restricted...then IMC reduced it to 40 characters last hotfix thinking it would reduce it...nope, they just use more Megaphones (roll that TP in, IMC. good market strategy)  Now my game chat is constantly bombarded by Megaphone spam while the top of my screen, looks like a friggin C-SPAN stock market ticker tape saying the same darn thing over and over and over again. It is a constant battle of me hitting the block button for every guy spamming their gold selling site  i.e.   \/\/ .\/\/ .\/\/ . |\/| |\/| |\/| |\/| . C 0 |\/|   times that by 100 ticking SLOWLY ACROSS MY GAME SCREEN.
8. Game latency.  Due to the game being a recent release and an MMO, there are release issues.  Latency Issues more specifically.  I have to change game channels constantly for the game to become responsive again for me.  There are at times where loot just sits on the ground "rotting". A few minutes later, my screen is bombarded by items picked up in that time-span very fast until it catches up.  This is very frustrating at times when you are doing a quest to obtain a certain number of items from a very specific mob.  For example, you kill 8 like it asks where each drop the quest item.  No registration...until your 40th...  Clicking on a quest item not working?  Latency issue most likely, switch channels and try again.  I am forgiving this since it's recent release, but not for long...
9. The hate against "BR" players.  29% of the player-base is Latin-America and 30% North America, This is by no means a CON, but I've come across a couple of people who are very vocal about it... just block them from chat. You'll be happier.  English is the default language in this game, and they understand it. Be nice and understanding, they are great people to play with too!
10. So you sold something in the Market, GOOD JOB! Now wait 2 DAYS + for the money to unlock. (Even for a Premie) Yes, the Market has a timer to give you your money for the item you sold. This is clearly put in place to limit the gold spammer sites to trade money in the game but this is a very punishing system to legitimately use the Market.  I have over 1 Million Silver waiting on different timers in the Market. This limitation has me up the walls since I like to craft and sell my goods.
All in all the Pro's outweigh the Cons for me.  If you decide to dive in,  Expect a friendly community and a lot of people who played Ragnarok Online.  See you in game!

Years ago I played Rome: Total Wars for weeks straight so I was super excited to see a second part to be released. Unfortunately I can't each and every feature of the first part. Therefore I won't compare the two but rather point out what I found especially awesome about the game.
Because of a lot of negative reviews concerning the day one version I waited multiple months until most of the heavy bugs seemed to have been removed.
Of course the first thing for me to play was the campaign. The first thing I was positively surprised about was the new economical system. You can really specialize your territories depending on what you need them for: Economy, Fleet, Infantry etc.
The diplomatic possibilities are still vast: Find allies who you later betray, poison your foes with agents, block harbors and more. I always felt like I had multiple options to capture cities. Straight out attack it or silently slaughter them using my special agents over weeks.
The combat feels very smooth in my opinion. Especially interesting is the combination of land forces and fleets to conquer cities as the opponent can't just sit behind his walls but must also protect his haven.
I never encountered obvious mistakes by the AI. To me the combats felt challenging and the heavy impact of morale can always still turn the outcome of battles even when you thought you were already the sure winner.
I purchased the game for less than 30€ and already played 37 hours and will definitely start a second campaign in some months. I fully enjoyed the game and was never annoyed by it.
100% recommendation by me!

I love playing this game.
It took me around 4 hours each for the first and seconds playtrough, I liked it even more the second time. The story is unique, fascinating and thrilling. Summary: Disappointing as an RPG. The gameplay is interesting and noteworthy, but the story is wasted.
Start with the good stuff: Gameplay. The combat system sounds interesting at first, but ends up being a bit dull for a while. By the time you're 2-3 hours in, and have a good variety of abilities to choose from, things turn around and it gets pretty fun. I'm sure there are people who specced completely different from me, and it's interesting to play around with all the skills to see what you can get away with. In this respect, Transistor reminds me of games like Valkyrie Profile and Resonance Of Fate, other RPGs with combat systems that seem kind of awkward and disjointed at first, but reward you greatly as you get the hang of it and learn their intricacies (though Transistor is not as deep as either of those games).
Now the bad: The game completely lost me on the story, though. It seems a bit open to interpretation, and things are never clearly explained to you. This *can* be done in an interesting way (I love a good mystery as much as anyone), but I had no emotional investment or attachment to anyone or anything that occurred in this game in the slightest. There's no character development whatsoever, just a couple random details about people, most of whom are pretty inconsequential. That leaves you with a disjointed, unexplained, and irrelevant world. I was never given a reason to care about the fate of the city, Red, or the Transistor.
The music didn't really strike me, either. It's not bad, but having recently played through Child Of Light and To The Moon, two games that definitely made me take notice of their music, I'm disappointed with Transistor's soundtrack, especially considering the praise that other reviews have been lauding upon it.
I feel like I'm missing something, because everyone else seems to love this game. I went in expecting to love it, but ended up waiting for a revelation that never came.
Oh these guys-- know how to make an impactful story, that leaves a lasting impression without it having to be 200 hours long. Gorgeous game, great sound, great gameplay.

After the great Bound in Blood, Call of Juarez 3 was a mighty disappointment. Can a lower budget new game, released for $15, Make Call of Juarez Great Again? Yes.
Now, the low budget can be seen, the game certainly doesn't push any graphical boundaries, it doesn't chase mo-capped Gary Oldmans, or ads during the Superbowl. It is not a long game, you can be done with the campaign in something around 4 hours. There are no cut scenes, the story is told by narration while you play, plus drawn comic-book-style frames.
It is, however, really fun to play. The guns all feel loud and powerful and the game works nice with the concept of the levels being recollections of an old bounty hunter, sort of a Wild West Forrest Gump full of♥♥♥♥♥♥ so often things change in front of your eyes as he either misremembers, or is called on his ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t by others. At one point you approach a bank robbery in three different ways, as different listeners heard a different version of the tale.
Unlike the previous Call of Juarez games, Gunslinger also takes a much more arcadey approach - score points pop out of enemies as you strive for the highest combo, and so on. If the short campaign is not enough for you, there's a NG+ and an arcade mode.
I'd welcome more games like this, cheaper made and sold, where developers might try some new ideas without risking a hundred million dud.
I really recommend this game, it is a blast to play, and can be picked up for just a couple of bucks. One of my favorite FPS games for sure.

Papers, Please, a bare 30 meg download on Steam that turned out to be one of the most strangely absorbing experiences I've had with indie games lately, and like a mysterious rash, I've been taking every opportunity to get people to look at it. The elevator pitch would probably have turned off all but investors with the least amount of ♥♥♥♥s to give.
Basically, it's a bureacracy-'em-up. You play a border-control guard in a communist country and your job is to check the paperwork of incoming travelers, interrogating them over discrepencies and making the final decision of red stamp or green stamp, except there's some kind of secondary invisible checkpoint that instantly spots ♥♥♥♥-ups and fines you if you missed them, so one wonders why we're even here.
More layers of bureacracy are added to the process over time: passports, permission to travel, permission to work, permission to♥♥♥♥♥♥ permission to use run-on sentences, until immigrants are handing you entire scrapbooking projects and if they spell their name with a different vowel once, then it's off to talk to the nice men with guns in the building that people go into a lot but don't seem to come out of so much. But you get paid by how many you processed in a day, so it's hard to sympathize when you have to put Spotty McBumble♥♥♥♥ through the X-ray machine 'cos his passport says he's a girl and the last precious seconds of the day trickle out as you examine a picture of his hairy balls. Hey, you know who'd love to see your hairy balls? These nice men with guns!
That's the beauty of Papers, Please; it presents us constant moral choices, but makes it really hard to be a good person. Virtually all your money goes to rent and food, so while you could waive the rules to reunite a couple or turn away someone with hairy balls so catastrophic they might level the city, you do it at the expense of your own family.
You're a pivotal part of a thousand stories - some small, some big - and you have to decide if you want to create a better world or just look after you and yours. You're gazing up at a big complex state of affairs funneled down and glimpsed through the filter of your tiny little world of passport numbers and hairy ball sacks, the effect of which being that admitting someone that seemed legit and hearing the sound of the obnoxious printer giving me a citation seized my heart more than any number of dead mums.
Yeah, I got quibbles. There's a lot of telling without showing and the booth upgrades are about as much use as a Wi-Fi connection in the Auschwitz prison showers, but the important thing is that a genuinely engaging paperwork simulator is far worthier of your time than the seventy thousand slightly engaging gunfight. EA would never make something like this. For one thing, it would remind them too much of their customer support services.

So I have been playing Transistor lately...just ya know ten hours for just the first play through.
Have to say this game is gaming PERFECTION!!!
Combat is a mix between real time and turn base. You can use any skill you have equipped whilst in real time, but you can also press a button to trigger TURN. Doing this STOPS time, allows you to set up a turn so to speak.
While in TURN you have a bar, each action you do takes some of this bar away. Things like walking, buffs, debuffs etc etc.  Best part of this system was how free you are to play with TURNs. You can use up 99% of the bar and still use something that would take more than what of the bar is left. Making for some majorly epic TURNs.
On top of combat you have a story driven so deeply I seriously teared up at some parts. The world and environment is such a beautiful mix. Imagine TRON, and SecondLife somewhat mixed together. The Users are still themselves, but whilst in this world they consist as a program. This leads to some very, very interesting scifi, and imagination when it comes to the actual world in its self.
Narration is done so powerfully at times I was at a lost of what to even say to myself! The main character Red, actually loses her voice in the actions that lead to the start of the story, so the entire thing is all narrated by your weapon the Transistor. This does not mean you have a silent heroine though. Throughout the world you can use monitors, most of these ask you really simple things like what weather you like. Some of these allow Red to talk to the Transistor. So look out for these they add so much depth with so little dialog it...gah I just I feel I need NEW words just to describe how much I love this game.
It was also made by the same people that made Bastion. So it includes a lot of the ideas that Bastion held. Things like game changers that make it harder, this allows the player to make the gamer harder or just keep it normal without ever asking "easy, normal, or hard?" Which I feel is a prefect way to add difficulty to a game since again it is all up to the player, on top of making the game feel like it has changed in more ways that just "enemy does more damage on higher difficulty!"
If you put these things that make the game harder you get more EXP from fights by a set %. Which is cool because the EXP is based on a percentage system. Unlike other RPGs this game just says you are 0% through 100% to a level up so you actually level up at a great pace.
Leveling up is also a perfect thing in this game! Almost EVERY level up offers YOU the CHOICE of what YOU want. When you start off the lower stuff will be like getting a new skill which can bounce off baddies, or maybe you want the thing that allows you to turn a baddy into an ally for a bit? Up to YOU!
Music is beautiful. I won't even try to go into this, will say this though. It has emotion! Also if you hold down one of the buttons Red will hum, offering you extra sounds to the song currently playing which pretty much doubles the songs in a way!
After your first big boss, you get a place that lets you do challenges. Some are a bit puzzle based where you have to kill all the baddies in one TURN. Others pit you against enemies with a pre-set skill selection making you have to figure out the uses effectively to win! They don't add a TON to the game, but they do offer extra EXP! :D
Last thing I will say, the game has difficulty. By no means did I win without a few deaths, but even in DEATH they made this game so perfect. Instead of dying and having to start all over from your last save spot, you actually LOSE one of your skills, get full health back, and get to keep fighting. You then can get the skills back by going to a save spot. BEWARE I never allowed myself to lose a skill...I always retried, which in my opinion was more fun. Mainly due to the fact when I did retry I got to go back into the fight with a whole new set up and try new things!

This is my first contact with this series,and I've got to say,I'm really impressed.
Alien : Isolation is a horror game that stands out from the rest,because it manages the unthinkable : it presents you with an enemy that you fear really much at the beginning of the game,but as deaths start to stack up on your part,you are just really angry that there is no way to stop the endless deaths that the Alien causes.Your weapons against him?Flares,noisemakers,a motion tracker that is kind of confusing(at least for me) and a few other things that don't even work on him.And a flamethrower,which needs to be used wisely.Spoiler here:
Enough with my complaining because I suck at avoiding enemies in this game,let's get to my real thoughts.
I can say this game is kind of an evolved Outlast.Same suspense,same objective:escape from the horror place you acidentally got into.Your best bet there was to hide.Here you have different approaches,distractions,and there are enemies you can kill,of course.
My favourite part about this game is the save mechanic.There are emergency telephones all across the station that let you save the game when you come across them (of course,you have to wait a few seconds before you save so in case someone is after you they can kill you easily).I truly loved the suspense moments after you play a lot of time without saving,knowing that at any moment,without any warning,you will be facebited by the Alien,knocked out by an Android or just shot by a struggling survivor.You have to plan every move you make,think ahead of your enemies and use hiding spots to your advantage.
I can say that this is one of my favourite horror games,very inovative and chill-giving (is that even a word?) which manages to keep you glued to it to see what happens next.I will never forget the moments when I was scared because I was hearing the Alien coming towards my direction,while looking at the motion tracker and seeing a green dot that moved very quickly.Truly a masterpiece.10/10.
Pro tip:If you have found a way to cause the Alien to retreat,don't use it often.Don't use the flamethrower often,because it will become imune to it;don't hide very often because he will start to search lockers more often.You get my point.I did this mistake and the game became harder from that point forward.
Enjoy this awesome game! It is really worth playing it until the end.

I love playing this game.
It took me around 4 hours each for the first and seconds playtrough, I liked it even more the second time. The story is unique, fascinating and thrilling. The combat feels smooth and is fun, the combinations of skills are near endless. Darren Korb gives me shivers again, the music is brilliant and creates an absolutely authentic gaming experience, I rarely felt as much emotions of characters in a game as I did in Transistor, which makes it overall a near perfect game.
However, it has some negative aspects, too.
Challenges and Achievements  are a bit easy.
For example 2k damage in a single turn is way to low to be worth an Achievement. 20k or even 50k are not only possible, but quite easy to reach. Performance Tests are nice and difficult, the rest of the tests might be a good introduction to the mechanics, but do not constitute a real challenge.
After reaching a certain level of practice or skill, the whole game gets pretty easy. Once you can deal gigantic amounts of damage in a single Turn, if becomes more and more a Hit'n'Run type of combat. Using one combination, waiting for Turn to come back up, rinse and repeat. To crank up the diffuculty in the normal gameplay, one can do combat without using Turn, something like this would be a nice achievement to have.
All in all, as I mentioned at the beginning, I love this game, despite the little difficulty issues. I enjoyed every single minute, it is well worth more than its cost, and I'm sure I'll spend another 5 or 6 hours playing it.

Summary: Disappointing as an RPG. The gameplay is interesting and noteworthy, but the story is wasted.
Start with the good stuff: Gameplay. The combat system sounds interesting at first, but ends up being a bit dull for a while. By the time you're 2-3 hours in, and have a good variety of abilities to choose from, things turn around and it gets pretty fun. I'm sure there are people who specced completely different from me, and it's interesting to play around with all the skills to see what you can get away with. In this respect, Transistor reminds me of games like Valkyrie Profile and Resonance Of Fate, other RPGs with combat systems that seem kind of awkward and disjointed at first, but reward you greatly as you get the hang of it and learn their intricacies (though Transistor is not as deep as either of those games).
Now the bad: The game completely lost me on the story, though. It seems a bit open to interpretation, and things are never clearly explained to you. This *can* be done in an interesting way (I love a good mystery as much as anyone), but I had no emotional investment or attachment to anyone or anything that occurred in this game in the slightest. There's no character development whatsoever, just a couple random details about people, most of whom are pretty inconsequential. That leaves you with a disjointed, unexplained, and irrelevant world. I was never given a reason to care about the fate of the city, Red, or the Transistor.
The music didn't really strike me, either. It's not bad, but having recently played through Child Of Light and To The Moon, two games that definitely made me take notice of their music, I'm disappointed with Transistor's soundtrack, especially considering the praise that other reviews have been lauding upon it.
I feel like I'm missing something, because everyone else seems to love this game. I went in expecting to love it, but ended up waiting for a revelation that never came.

I absolutely love this game. CONS
- The game is very buggy. I've escaped most of it due to being on the EU server, but I've had problems like not being able to log in until after a few tried, the game freezing during a dungeon (and losing me a daily run)/when someone tries to enter my lobby, etc. Nothing that makes it unplayable, but you WILL encounter bugs as it stands
- Trading: you can't trade unless you buy a Token, and even then only 30 times. I have one but I don't know how I feel about this
- The Market: you can only put up 1 item as a free user and 5 as a VIP, but this seriously screws with the economy because it's not worth putting cheaper items on the TH. I don't see how any crafting classes could earn money
Now, onto the...
PROS
+ The game is actually FUN. As in, if I was playing it, I would enjoy it in the same way I enjoy gameboy releases of Zelda or Secret of Mana... and that means everything for me.
+ A lot of great ideas have been implemented, like bonuses from collections, varied secret quests with great rewards, prizes from adventuring achievements (incl 100% map completion), chests hidden in random places, etc... it's GREAT
I won't make this any longer but the fun factor just makes the whole game worthwhile. I'd play it even if it was offline. So this gets a thumbs up from me.

WARNING THIS REVIEW MAY BE SEEN AS SPOILDERS!!!
Sonic Forces is definitely something different.  It's the first Sonic game ever where Sonic gets defeated for once and you can make a custom character, play as them, and see them in cutscenes.
The customization for the custom hero is disappointing because the options are ridiculously limited, there's no options for separate muzzles or ears or tails, just 3 preset heads, eyes, and color options.  There are some fur patterns and haircuts but they're in the clothing section, and all the clothing only comes in 3 color schemes instead of being tintable.  thankfully there are enough options to make some interesting and fun custom avatars.
The gameplay is pretty fun but it could definitely be better.  The game uses the boost formula once again meaning all the levels are super liner and consist of "get from point A to point B in the quickest time."  This sucks because the background for all the levels are so beautiful and detailed that it makes me wanna explore EVERYTHING.  The levels are still fun but a lot of it feels automated just to make it look cool instead of letting you do cool things yourself.  Modern Sonics is fun and entertaining but his Boost is overused, in fact some of his levels feel like you just boost to win. Classic Sonics game play is somewhat fun as well but it can be frustrating because there's no actual physics in this game, only forces physics to give the illusion that there's physics, and that's bad for Classic Sonic because it means he doesn't play like he should.  The Custom Character plays similar to Modern Sonic.  The weapons are fun to use even the special attacks for the weapons.  My biggest complaint about the custom hero's weapons are that they run on wisps.
I'm personally sick of wisps now, they were fun in sonic colors, cute in lost world, and now it's just annoying.  They wisps aren't even mentioned at all, they're just there.  I'd rather have the Chao garden back instead of the stupid wisps.
I actually like the story for this game because Sonic gets defeated for once, Dr. Eggman is an actual threat for once and not played off as a stereotypical Saturday morning cartoon villain.  Infinite is a cool new character as well and I hope he comes back in the next game.  The only problem is the story has plot holes.  Like why is tails afraid of Chaos 0 when he's fought Chaos 4, a stronger version of Chaos, as well as the Egg Walker at the end of his story in Sonic Adventure.  Sonic was also supposedly tortured yet he looks nothing happened, what the heck?  And the game says Eggman invented the Phantom Ruby when Sonic Mania and the comic "Rise of Infinite" says it was FOUND.  Finally there's the fact that the potential for the Phantom Ruby goes unused.  The Phantom Ruby can essentially make anything.  So why didn't Infinite and Eggman make a bunch of Marias to mess with shadow, or played one of those funny "who's the fake" bit.  They could have even made Modern Sonic and the Custom Hero fight Phantom Copies of themselves, there's so much potential!
I really do like this game and I want to love it, but the game was obviously rushed just to make sure it could be sold for the holiday rush.  Thankfully the game is NOWHERE near as bad as other games.
Here's what I think they need to do to make the next sonic game better.  Use the ideas used in Fores.  Abandon the boost formula and give us a proper gameplay style like the Sonic Adventure games and Unleashed.  Abandon the linear level design and 2D segments and give us a 3D environment to freely explore.  Give the custom character a TON of more options so people can make almost anything.  REPLACE THE WISPS WITH A CHAO GARDEN!  And make the game bigger, cause this game did feel short.  But most importantly, delay they next game to make sure it's polished.  Something that Sonic Team never seem to get is that it's better to delay a game to make sure it's better, rather then rush it just to sell it for the holiday rush.
Still despite the problems this game has, I honestly still think it's really fun to play.  I recommend this Game because despite it's flaws, I still had fun with it.  I really do like all the ideas used for this game and wish they'd expand apon them greatly.  This game almost feels like the set up for a Sonic MMO.  I honestly wonder how successful a Sonic MMO would be.
Can't recommend it because I can't get past the moment in the first green hill where sonic calls it sand hill. My game crashes there everytime. Hope Sega fixes the issue soon, looks fun.

The game is... okay.
Story is nothing special, with some things obviously happening for the sole reason of plot convenience, and the whole "power of friendship" fluff feels somewhat tacked-on and out of nowhere. Still, it's okay. Shallow, but reasonably serviceable for the purpose.
Graphics are obviously cartoony (what did you expect?) and remind me somewhat of PS2 era. Poly count might be higher, but frankly it doesn't change all that much. Again, serviceable.
Controls in platforming sections are unbelievably slippery. There are some places where I sent character to its death for dozens of times repeatedly due to slippery controls. There are two problems, from what I can tell: first, controls have noticeable inertia, character doesn't stop the moment you stop input. That would be manageable, if not for the second problem: scale can change almost arbitrarily. This messes with my platformer instincts at least -- it changes timings and what character can or can't do in terms of screen distance. This makes platforming unnecessarily hard. Thankfully, there are not much places where that is actually frustrating, but there are some. For the most part, controls are serviceable.
Music is unremarkable, for the most part. I reasonably enjoyed some of more "edgy" tracks, while those played, but after a day or so I can not remember any of those. So... again, it's fine for what it is, but nothing more.
Customization is rather pointless. It's obviously designed to extend play time, but I literally see no reason to play it more after I finished it once. Same goes for "daily challenges" etc.
Gameplay is, again, fine. Not great. Also, while on topic of gameplay, it's extremely hard to get S ranking in some of the easier levels for some reason (bear in mind I have no trouble getting said rank in about half of the levels, so it's at least weirdly inconsistent)
Main "campaign" is very short. I've beat it in 5 hours, and I bet it could be done in 3 without too much trouble. What I'm trying to say here: it doesn't seem like there's much content here.
All in all, the game's fine. It's not amazing, it's not horrible either. I don't think full asking price is entirely justified, but it's not outrageous.
If Steam had "meh" rating, that would be it. But since it doesn't, I'll recommend it, with a note: it's better to pick this up on a sale.

Sonic Forces was, by all accounts, a dissapointing Sonic game.
The main issue that I, as well as many others, seem to have had with this game is you are paying $40 dollars for 2-3 hours of actual gameplay, and said gameplay is mostly just auto-pilot garbage with enemies that dont even attack you. The game is unenjoyable, the bosses are either a complete joke or have stupid attack patterns, and the plot went from amazing to pure "friendship is magic" trash so fast it'd make Sonics head spin. Even the main selling point, Infinite, the edgiest character to ever grace our eyes, was ultimately a sterotypical and pitiful excuse for a villan.. who wasnt even a threat in the end, I might add.
There are some positives of course. The music is fantastic as always, the main idea behind the game is very good, and I will admit that the "Original Character" levels were some of my favorite in the game

I'd recommend purchasing the game at a later date when its on sale, but as it stands I wouldnt pay full price for it.

Best Sonic game in a long time!
Stability-wise is the game totally fine; it didn't crash even once on me during my playthrough.
There's only a little clipping bug on one of the end-bosses model that makes them a little harder, but nothing serious.
Once the list of items in the character customization system showed the wrong thumbnails. - can be fixed by scolling around.
Graphics-wise the game is not a show-off but it looks gorgeous nonetheless.
In cutscenes you'll see some clone-armies and simplistic animations in the background.
There's also the occasional edge that should be round, but there's really not enough to complain about, the graphics suffice for the chosen art-style.
The sound design is very good.
The background-music adjusts to your gameplay and the cutscenes have decent voiceover.
The custon player character barely ever says anything beyond "Mhm" and "Aaaaah!" however.
The music itself is also high quality - would take it with me on a train ride - a fast one ;D
The levels are occasionally surprisingly detailed.
The world map on the other hand is surprisingly unintuitive and simplistic.
The character customization is very rich, you'll be able to customize your character to quite an extent.
There is also a good arsenal of weapons to choose from that will also become more complex, once you start collecting versions of the weapons you know with different game changing buffs on them - such as: get a ring for every enemy, start the level with a shield, glide longer or sprint after a stomp attack.
The story is fun.
It contains some fan-service and is held deep in the PG area (friendship is magic), but it is not cheesy enough to outstay its welcome that way, actually I wanted to see more of it.
The only downside is that the story was over after 11.5 hours, where I had most missions on S-Rank and done all side missions. However I'm not truly done with the content, since there are still completionist things to do such as collecting all hidden stars in all the levels, get all missions on S-Rank, beat highscores of other players and unlock more character customizations - the game doesn't end after the story is over.
Short but fun.
Overall I'd say it's worth buying especially if you haven't played any of the previous games since the SEGA Mega Drive era and I'd like encourage the developers to take this game as an ideal to start off from for future games.

Is this game worth $40? In a way, yes, but in another, no. There isn't enough to actually do in-game that's different from the rest of the game, particularly where it pertains to the avatar. I consider this game a step in the right direction for several unrelated reasons, but it's just way, way, waaay too narrow. We have the regular levels, not all of which are accessible by the avatar. There are about 30 standard levels. Divided between Sonic, Sanic, and the OC (Donut Steel), or some which have both, this is an already short game which, for all the customizations made available to the avatar, feels... incomplete.
All these clothing options and comparatively so little of the actual stages are avatar-playable, for how long we might overthink poor Donut Steel's appearance. I still recommend this, but good lord, prepare yourself for a drastic sense of underfulfillment after you've completed most of the game. It isn't just Donut Steel, but Sonic and Sanic alike that all feel like they got cut short for available playtime. I'd be pretty happy with a level pack of some sort for the avatar, some more full-length stages for our OC to swing through.
On the earlier point of the game feeling incomplete: I wish to state that, remarkably, it doesn't feel like any of the existing features are missing anything. Everything that exists is rock solid. The sense of incompleteness comes from the game's brevity, and the exclusion of potentially another mode for playing with the avatar. Consider a building; an extremely tall and narrow one is more likely to fall over than an extremely short and wide one. The short and wide one, while stable, just begs to have more built on top. Sonic Forces is that short, wide building.

Despite being rather short and in-game cutscenes...lacking in animation, the actual gameplay is very fun. And introducing a player-made character gives you extra attachment to what is going on. I definately recommend this game, but if you are unsure about aforementioned two points, you might want to wait for some sort of discount.

When it first game out, it tried desperately to be what people wanted, Skyrim Online. It failed this completely. But in the few years it's been out the updates really have made the game into a brilliant MMO. It can be played solo, or with friends (provided you're unlike me and actually have friends that give a sausage about MMORPGs.) Either way it is a brilliant experience.
The graphics are beautiful, not quite Skyrim and there is a bit of pop in when you get close to someone but for the game that it is, it is brilliantly optimised (I say that, I do have a beastly PC) and the colours are far richer than that of any previous Elder Scrolls game which, in my opinion shines out far beyond simple textures. Not to say the textures are bad, because to say that would be a blatant lie, they are again, fantastic.
The writing is also great, the dialogue is familiar to Skyrim players, that is the UI is simple, you are given a few options in each instance and very often a choice that actually impacts how your game plays out. The actual conversations are riddled with jokes and irony, with a lot of people finding some rather humorously named items on their travels as well.
The quests are a lot of fun, they make sense, and the main quest is interesting. Especially when Dumbledore materialises in front of you and tells you to meet him in his secret hideout. The side quests are intriguing and steal you away from whatever you were doing to begin with in true Elder Scrolls fashion. There is the perfect balance of humour, grand adventure and sleuthing in the side quests.
The combat recently recieved a complete overhall and is much richer now, the abilites matter more and are all reasonably balanced, blocking, dodging and interuppting are all perfectly integrated and all prepare you as you go through the game for PvP and the higher difficulty as you level up more and more.
All things considered, with the freedom to explore based on how the enemies scale, the game feels much more Elder Scrolls and while it will never fully accomplish that goal, it is an absoloutely fantastic MMO and I thoroughly recommend it to any MMO fan as well as the majority of Elder Scrolls fans

If anyone wants a pros vs cons:
Pros:
* Bugs are not game breaking USUALLY
* Many different weapon choices
* Many different ways to fight (different swings, blocking etc)
* Infinite sprinting (amazing as this game already takes forever to do things, which is also a pro)
* Half day/night cycle, not too long, not too short
* Lots of life, the game never feels empty (animals, wind, etc always moving)
* Light is very dynamic
* Very realistic light distances (fires seen all the way across the map)
* Raiding is not a chore or boring (never gets old)
* When raided, you are still upset but you still want to play and build up again
* Building is great as you place blocks to make whatever type of building shapes you want
* Tiers for weapons and blocks
* Guilds allows many different approaches to the game (protecting your base/area around from being built etc)
* Guild chat (private chat that only guildies can hear)
* Crafting takes a long time and honestly is still not boring. Good balance with how long stuff takes to build/craft
* I could keep going but I don't want this to go too long
Cons:
* Still no whisper command (unless I'm just stupid and it is in)
* Voice chat breaks a lot in game (relogging helps)
* Weapons sometimes hit strangely (behind you, you swing passed enemy and you still hit, etc)
* Map is a bit small for ~40+ people. And only a couple islands to swim to (please add!)
* Resources are a bit too clustered, kinda reduces desire to live away from main areas (Kind of point of game but still would be nice to see more spread
* People can camp bases on resource nodes, making it impossible for others to get them (another reason I want more spread resources) (But again, the game is about survival of fittest and taking over eachother, so I can deal)
* You can die seriously some stupid deaths
* Mountains are strange to climb. This is good and bad. Really steep areas can be scaled easy, but some areas less steep cannot. Mostly frustating than anything.
* Wells are pointless for most part, need more usefulness
* THERE'S A PLACE TO THE KING'S RIGHT. RIGHT BEFORE YOU GET ON SWORD ON THE LEFT, THERE'S A CLIFF. DO NOT GO DOWN THERE. You get stuck! I had to be roped out xD (Pictures on profile xD)
* Blocks should be stronger(or atleast another teir, like reinforced steel blocks), and trebuchet stones should be 100 stone again. It's too easy to break in to most places, in my opinion.
* Not enough oil spots (bigger map to accomodate)
* Most materials are really easy to get however, don't make much. Or atleast enough to accomodate for how much you can get so quickly. (I'll probably update this as I get more experience)
* Too easy to get to steel armor/weapons in my opinion
* Armor seems to do very little in combat
* NPCs such as bears, wolves, etc do way too much damage. Again, in full steel a bear does around a 1/3rd of your max hp
* NPCs, especially the one's above, often give very little even though they are dangerous
* Again, I'm sure I missed quite a few.
Over all, I rate this game a 9/10 for sheer entertainment. Definitely a new favorite for quite a while.

Fun game, reminds me of RO1.
Pros:
Extremely customizable Job/Skill system
Oldschool MMO Stat point distribution system
Great art style
'Arcade' style mobs of enemies to mow down
Crafting system
Penalties for dying--lose all your gems on your person
Dungeons
PvP Duel System
Controller Support (Xbox 360 and Xbox One with some tweaking)
Cons:
Limited character appearance customizability
Game is focused around combat, little else to do.
Linear questing
End game is not well defined at the moment
AI is not very challenging (as far as I know)
Other considerations:
Tree of Savior had a rough launch week with server instability, however it has gotten leaps and bounds better in the past 2  days as of this review. Many people rate the game negatively because they cannot understand why a game would be laggy in the first two days. Many other games have this same problem on launch *cough cough* Blade and Soul. Also people complain a lot about gold seller spam in the global chat, the developers have noted this and are already taking some steps to curb the problem by limiting megaphone  usage to level 40+. Also there are restrictions on player to player trade which many people don't like. I don't think the game even needs a trade system, since you can just use the marketplace instead. I would personally remove megaphones from the game or make them much more costly or restricted since I think the casual megaphone chat is just as spammy as the gold spammers.
As much as people complain about gold spammers, it was a LOT worse in Blade and Soul. Similarly, the lag issue is much smaller than it was, since April 2nd. I have not been in a login queue since then, and have only had rare bouts of lag that last about 30 seconds at max.
The game is a grindy game, much akin to Maplestory, Ragnorak Online 1, and others... If you like the grind, and  you enjoy being able to find good spots to grind to level, craft good gear, and customize your build to be the best, then you will thoroughly enjoy this game. Overall, I play fairly casually and I have found the community rather chatty and welcoming, I also enjoy taking down large mobs of monsters and map completion so I find the game fun. For those who want challenging AI and heavy PvP and Dungeon focus, this is not the game for you.
My biggest con for the game is the lack of the end game, but it is quite far away from me yet and there is plenty of game play at the moment. Regardless, the developers have said they are working on end game content, I just hope it is interesting/rewarding enough to be worth it.

Sonic Forces... It took a while but it's finally here! ...It didn't turn out as well as I had hoped.
Leading up to Forces, I was decently excited for the game. Mostly because I was interested in messing with the avatar editor and seeing what I could create with it.
The game itself... It became a bit of a mixed bag critically. If you're a TLDR kind of person, I'll just say it now.
7/10.
Want to read on? Cool. Let's begin with the...
STORY 6/10
Of all the stories that Pontac and Graff were involved in, I feel this is probably the strongest one, but that isn't saying much. I did enjoy the darker shift in tone to the concept of a war between Eggman and Sonic's friends. I felt like some things went by too fast like Sonic being considered dead, then revealed to be alive literally a minute later. I feel the inclusion of Classic Sonic was so shoehorned in. He meant nothing to the plot outside of just being the guy to listen to all of Tails's problems. I also felt that a bit too much cheese was inserted into the plot here and there. Overall, it's a cute story, but it's flawed.
GRAPHICS 9/10
Hoo boy. The graphics in this game are so stunning. That work on the Hedgehog Engine 2 really paid off. While the environments aren't as vastly built like the ones in Generations, the effects like grass, reflections, water, etc all look beautiful. One can only begin to think of what a game as detailed as Generations would look like in here. Anyway, they sure made use of the increasae of horsepower modern consoles and PCs have. Too bad it's a bit unoptimized. (That and I have intel graphics, but I've played on a gaming PC too)
Gameplay 7/10
The gameplay was a huge letdown. The stages are all so short with a bunch of style with little substance. The trio of new guys treated automation as their best friend here. As soon as stages get hype, they end within seconds. My first runs of the stages in Generations were full of wonder of what was coming next. That happens here, but it's almost always goal when I question that. Classic is also broken. He's very very broken. He just FEELS shoehorned into the game. The custom hero has a wide variety of different weapons to use. They bring a pretty decent change to the levels depending on which one you equip. Drill is good for speedrunning, Void is overpowered, etc.
Music 9/10
The music is hit or miss for many. For me, I love all of the music. The only misses I get are some of the classic tracks, and only like two of those and one that gives me flashbacks to a level that uses a trope that should NEVER be used in a Sonic game... When it first game out, it tried desperately to be what people wanted, Skyrim Online. It failed this completely. But in the few years it's been out the updates really have made the game into a brilliant MMO. It can be played solo, or with friends (provided you're unlike me and actually have friends that give a sausage about MMORPGs.) Either way it is a brilliant experience.
The graphics are beautiful, not quite Skyrim and there is a bit of pop in when you get close to someone but for the game that it is, it is brilliantly optimised (I say that, I do have a beastly PC) and the colours are far richer than that of any previous Elder Scrolls game which, in my opinion shines out far beyond simple textures. Not to say the textures are bad, because to say that would be a blatant lie, they are again, fantastic.
The writing is also great, the dialogue is familiar to Skyrim players, that is the UI is simple, you are given a few options in each instance and very often a choice that actually impacts how your game plays out. The actual conversations are riddled with jokes and irony, with a lot of people finding some rather humorously named items on their travels as well.
The quests are a lot of fun, they make sense, and the main quest is interesting. Especially when Dumbledore materialises in front of you and tells you to meet him in his secret hideout. The side quests are intriguing and steal you away from whatever you were doing to begin with in true Elder Scrolls fashion. There is the perfect balance of humour, grand adventure and sleuthing in the side quests.
The combat recently recieved a complete overhall and is much richer now, the abilites matter more and are all reasonably balanced, blocking, dodging and interuppting are all perfectly integrated and all prepare you as you go through the game for PvP and the higher difficulty as you level up more and more.
All things considered, with the freedom to explore based on how the enemies scale, the game feels much more Elder Scrolls and while it will never fully accomplish that goal, it is an absoloutely fantastic MMO and I thoroughly recommend it to any MMO fan as well as the majority of Elder Scrolls fans

This game is just amazing, every time we play it's a fresh adventure with a completely new story to tell. Last night (and this morning and afternoon) ended up playing 15 hours straight, haven't got into a game like this for a long long time. I've owned it for 4 days I think and played nearly 40 hours, after a long period of not really gaming more than an hour a day for nearly a year.
It just ticks all boxes:
- Excellent combat system (pretty much just like Chivalry).
- Open world with a sense of land ownership.
- Open PvP, full loot. When you log off, your character sleeps and you can be killed and robbed. Build a base to protect your♥♥♥♥♥♥- Of course that can be broken into, lock picked, or smashed down with seige equipment depending on strength of materials.

Followed by the series of Ragnarok online, Tree of Savior(ToS) served as another nostalgic MMORPG game for old MMO players to regain their childhood or teenage-hood. However, I want to emphasize that this game is a complete different genre than RO main because the game philosophy, mechanism and character is in a totally distinguished realm.
Pro:
-	Quests / Story are somehow interesting (you are destined to save bundle of goddess??).
-	IMC (developer) is doing well in trouble handling such as creating more servers during launch (despite took 24 hours) but still manageable.
-	A lot features to be discovered (Attributes, Classes, Map exploration and Bosses).
-	Game controls are nice touch as there are 3 options available – Keyboard, Keyboard + mouse, controllers.
-	Progression of classes make the game unique to each player and various of options.
-	Solo is optional but party will help you progress level faster.
Cons:
-	Grinding section can be boring and counter intuitive.
-	Classes are somehow not balanced (Cleric has a tough start-up compared to swordman).
-	Some classes are not controller optimised (Archer and Magician).
-	Quests are not linearly synced to player progression level.
-	Controllers are not fully utilized, D-pad and joystick should have separate features.
-	Trading is forbidden in the game unless you are a premium player.
-	Team storage is not accessible unless you are paying for it (token user).
-	Game still in beta stage I believe as more optimization is required.
-       The outfit is very limited as it is bound by classes. Is there anyway to make it more flexible for example corresponding to player equipment.
