I'm not good at reviews, but I felt that I should write something because I loved this game and I love the people behind Supergiant.  <3
Supergiant games did it again!  ^_^
After having fallen in love with Bastion and Supergiant Games, I could not wait for their next release.
The only similarities between Bastion and Transistor, however, are.. obviously the art-style, the immersive narration and story, and yet again the amazing soundtrack.  Woot woot, the same narrator from Bastion!
The difference: the combat system is not quite the same as Bastion's. It's not so much a hack & slash, as much as it is a *tactical* combat-system game.  Ahh how to explain this..? It's quite unique.
There is a 'time-stop' system which allows you to literally -pause- to analyze and plan out your combat moves in advance. Each ability and number of steps you take around the "field" require a certain amount of 'energy' - so you are limited by an energy bar and its refresh system.  Therefore, you have to be efficient in not only the abilities you choose, but your movements across the "combat field", etc.  It's remniscent of other games to me that I had enjoyed very much.. so that was not an issue for me, personally! -- it was quite a delight. :)
What I especially enjoyed was the way that you can experiment with and mix up all the different abilities you pick through leveling up. Each combination results in something different, and you can only have 4 active ones in combat. You can literally mix 2-3 learned abilities together for one unique ability / result - so there are multiple possiblities.  You also have passive ability-slots which you can use those ability cards for, as well, and they play a completely different role.  There is quite a flexible customization system. :)
Also, if / everytime your HP goes to '0' in combat, you lose and are disabled from one of your 4 abilities; which you can only recover at a later time. :o Additionally, if you want to challenge yourself further, you are able to raise the difficulty by implementing an in-game system called "limiters" -- a very similar system to Bastion.  The more limiters you use, the more rewards (more xp). Funfun!
All in all, I loved the game so much that I took my time with it and did not want to rush through it.  I recommend that you don't either to enjoy the narration, soundtrack, and immersiveness for the total experience. Luckily, there is an option for a second playthrough so you can have the opportunity to level up some more and unlock abilities you had missed out on before and try different combinations! :)

Transistor has seriously become one of my favourite games of all time. Supergiant were criticised as a one-hit wonders with Bastion but they have come back with the artistic tour-de force that is Transistor. Through the wonderful handpainted art of Jen Zee and the beautiful tones of Darren Korb's soundtrack, you really get sucked into the abtract city that is Cloudbank and it's atmosphere.
Transistor captures that fleeting moment of Red and The Transistor trying to make it through alive and to get to the bottom of everything. The pacing is on form, some people say its quite short (at 7 hours) but I feel its enough to tell the story that it needed to tell without overstaying its welcome. The world and characters gell so well and all feel completely new, helped by the wonderful narration and chemistry between the characters.
Transistor isnt just all pretty picture, the ability system is quite different and completely customisable and promotes experimentation for completely different playstyles and the punishment for dying in game is one of the most original I've seen and actually adds to the experimentaion of the abilities.
In short, to me Transistor feels like a masterpiece of a painting with a wonderful story, good solid gameplay mechanics and a soundtrack ties it up into one fantastic and intelligently beautiful experience.
Transistor is a game that will stick with me for years to come, and for that Supergiant, thank you.

Don't expect Bastion 2, because this cleary isn't. It has some similarities regarding mechanics and of course the awesome voice of Logan Cunningham, but other than that it feels completely different. In a good way, that is.
Combat is action orientated, but more turn-based like. You can fight in real time, but you won't stand a chance. Utilizing the planning function allows you to plan moves, attacks and so on and then execute them very rapidly. It feels very satisfying to plan the perfect attack and then see it work out flawlessly and the sheer amount of abilities available, which can all be used in 3 entirely different ways is almost too much to handle at first.
But once you get the hang of it, there is no end to experimenting with the possible combinations at hand. The story element is probably what reminds me the most of Bastion, in the sense that it is told while playing with hardly any real cutscenes and it just unfolds as you go, adding bits and pieces of lore and background story. And it is just as well executed as in Bastion.
Although it's an entirely different game, I think if you liked Bastion and the style of it, there is a very, very high chance you will also dig Transistor. It's unique in so many ways.

+ Flawless gameplay. Cool and well implemented skill customization and game mechanics

All around taking the same roots as Bastion, this game is far more polished. If you enjoyed its predecessor, you will absolutely love Transistor, even with those cons (which aren't really something considerable, more like a personal opinion).
I conclude that this game is worth every penny I put on it.

I'm a Sonic fan by heart, especially for the boost gameplay.
For this game, I'll give it a 6.5/10.
Pros:
- It's a Sonic game...you already know the music is going to be amazing.
- The graphics are amazing. This is built with the same graphical engine (but upgraded) used from Sonic Unleashed; Hedgehog Engine.
- The gameplay looks, feels, and of course...plays very smooth and fluid.
- The boost component has gotten a "overhaul" per se, compared to past boosting games and it's really nice.
- Nice and diverse character creation, with countless customization options.
- The story is pretty decent and somewhat intruiging.
- Pretty nice level designs.
- Sega finally added some "action" in cutscenes..a bit of fighting here and there. Something I've been wishing for the longest. We can see what our heroes can truly do aside what we make em do. :p
Cons:
- Levels are kinda short and somewhat linear...due to how this game only had three level designers compared to past boosting games with 7+ designers. Still pretty good but could have been better.
- A couple questionable things in the story...
- Classic Sonic controls are a bit wierd. He falls too fast and cannot maneuver as much in the air, which threw me off a lot.
- Automatic drifting.
More cons: Read at your own risk.

This is a very good western FPS that takes advantage of its storytelling in ways you don't normally see. It's presented as a recollection of a bounty hunter's life told over some drinks, and the gameplay reflects that. If a detail is wrong, the game will rewind and fix itself. If he talks about something coming from "out of nowhere," it might actually fall from the skies. It's all rather clever. There's good mechanics at play here too, with an XP and level up system with different skill trees, a combo and focus meter system, a different take on "down but not out," and one on one duels, there's quite a lot here in this 4 hour game. There's also a combo focused arcade mode and a new game +, so I will definitely check both of those out. For FPS fans, this is a great buy at $15.

Borderlands 2 is a Shooter/ARPG four-player Co-op game developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K Games. This game revolves around killing enemies and getting better loot to kill more enemies. Unlike other shooter games, Borderlands 2 take unique approach by giving players more freedom to build their own character with different skills and playstyle. With tons of weapon and items, I think this game classifies as a simplified RPG.
Handsome Jack, one of the leader of Hyperion and responsible for Pandora's exploration and exploitation, is opening a great, ancient vault that imprison the powerful creature of the old, The Warrior. You, the vault hunter who seek glory, wealth, and fame by opening vaults, must ironically stop Handsome Jack from opening the vault, with the help of ex-vault hunters (=Borderlands (1) main/playable character).
For some people, Borderlands 2's storyline might seems too linear and predictable. You must fight the evil supreme boss to complete the game. That's different for some other gamers though. Borderlands 2 use humor to enchance the game and unconventional character with their mentally-challanged trait and stupid little brain (especially Krieg in the Psycho Pack DLC).
Borderlands 2 use unique gameplay unlike other shooter games (as mentioned above). You simply kill enemies, get guns, kill more enemies. Is it repetitive? Yes. Is it boring? No. With RPG-like customization, you could play the story 10 times and choose different classes and build. Each weapons have their own manufacturer with their own speciality. For example, Jakobs' weapons that fires as fast as you click your mouse, or Tourge's weapons that
shoot slow shiny bullet that explode on impacts, or even Tediore's weapons that shoot exploding bullet magazine when reloading. Totally could get tons of fun with this game. Sadly, quests are repetitive and only fetching items and killing monsters, and of course with some exeptional unique and funny quests.
As seen in the steam's preview, Borderlands 2's graphic use cartoonish texture and the 3D model looks 2D with an outline for  sprites and backgrounds, improvised one from it's predecessor. This style is very unique (if not the first time used) and gives fun atmoshpere with all those obscenity and swearing words. With cartoonish graphic, the weapons looks even more RPG-like, some even looks taken straight out of fantasy with colourful and modern-styled weapons. A great way to deliver the style and a great execution as well.
Personally, I never care about music in games. As such, I could give ordinary rating because there's no outstanding music that I like. I even thought there's no music in here. I recommend music from PAYDAY 2's soundtrack to acompany your gameplay. The sound is different though. The voice acting is really good and really fits into the character. The voice acting didn't reduce or increase how annoying or stupid or weird the character behave. The sound effects are pretty good too, the right sound of what a game needs.
If you prefer story over anything, this game might too average, but if you enjoy humor and shooter gameplay with a mix of RPG and action, you will love this game, especially with a trusted friends that boost the fun.

Just played through BL2 co-op with a friend. Before this we played through BL1.
For me these two games are almost the same game with little differences. BL2 has better graphics and a larger world but that´s about it. The GUIs for shops and inventory are horrible just as in BL2 but BL2 even slightly worse.
BL2 is a straight up FPS that in my opinion lacks finesse. The dialogue and quests are created with humor which probably is what made me play thought it and not quit. The co-op is also very good and slightly better than in BL1 with ammo-sharing. I would NOT have played many hours of this game solo.
The main problem I have is the magazine reloads. Simply put, you shoot like crazy, it empties, your character changes magazine which takes forever and always somehow occurs when you least want it. And it is sooo slow. It feels like a complete weaponcleaning every magchange. So you basically spend all your time screaming AMMO, AMMO!
It doesn´t help that the weapons are randomized, since some weapons which are very good damagewise could have very small magazines, and some weapons alsw fire several bullets at a time so it could take 2 seconds for a mag to empty and 5 seconds to change mag. Superannoying. The game would have been better if they skipped the whole reload-thing.
The last thing I want to mention is the golden keys, which destroyed the whole "pickup weapon". You get the golden keys from webpages through a serialnumber so I ended up with aroound 100 golden keys.
These unlock a specific chest that every time randomizes equipment that always are way better that what you find elsewhere.
On the whole I would say that if you like co-op play then BL2 could be a good choice. If you are a solo player look elsewhere.

Overall, the pros outway the cons by a ton. I highly recommend this game.

POSSIBLE SPOILERS ALERT.
For me, Emily is Away is a "subjective" form of gameplay. I'll try my best to describe the way how this game works for me.
Emily is Away is a game where it takes on a conversation using old instant messaage system such as AOL or MSN type and uses that system to carry the game.
However the core game structure is actually "Mass Effect" type narrative. The story is presented, you have options to select which route to take with that story.
It's not exactly 1 on 1 with Mass Effect Narrative but we shouldn't focus on that. This game gives you certain options towards the direction of the storyline.
Here's my problems with the game though. Games like these in my honest opinion frustrate me through the decision making process. ME PERSONALLY, have so much weights across variable options in conversations that I personally get frustrated when I'm limited to certain options of this game.
Which doesn't make this game negative by all means, just in my view I have different takes or directions that I want to take.
Games like this provide the options however only so much to provide only so much storyline.
Another thing is the story takes place where you just about to graduate high school and go on to college. With this you talk to Emily along the way, a long holded friend, a lost companion that is with you along your life of a journey.
This game/story is not very long by the way.
I cannot get into the characters of the story, it's just so many variables that I wish I can implement in the game. Such as after the selection of the choice of reply, typing out my own response, etc.
What I do want to take is, even though I tried to bash on the my negative point of view in this game. I sincerely recommend it.
This game actually brings some sort of "feel" back to us whether we care or not it brings some sort of familiarity with life in general of what we go through in a daily basis.
I personally cannot replay the game because of the inputs that I want to put in the game. To me even though I have different choices to choose from in the game I still find the game somewhat linear. Games like this are hard to develop due to so many different variations/elements that could or would happen in game. Pretty much I'm comparing this game to a an actually real life perspective.
All in all. I recommend this game. It's free. Glad I didn't pay for it. Brings that feel of familiary. In the end though, frustrated.

Идеи игрового мира S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Тень Чернобыля базируются на повести братьев Стругацких «Пикник на обочине», снятого по её мотивам фильма режиссёра Андрея Тарковского «Сталкер», а также на реальной зоне отчуждения Чернобыльской АЭС[8]. Разработчики рассматривали идею создания игры на основе зоны отчуждения ещё задолго до начала разработки S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Однако мысль о создании продукта, основанного на смешении «Пикника на обочине», сталкерства и зоны отчуждения возникла накануне второго официального анонса игры в марте 2002 года.
Изначально концепция данного проекта, имевшего тогда рабочее название «Oblivion Lost», никак не относилась к Чернобылю. Как подтверждают сами разработчики, его сюжет был схож с сюжетом фильма «Звёздные врата». Действие игры должно было происходить в будущем — во время галактических империй, с тысячами населённых планет и разумных рас. По сюжету, путешествие между планетами осуществляется с помощью порталов — недавнего научного открытия. Игрок и его группа являются частью авангарда и играют роль первопроходцев — первыми встречаются с новыми, неизвестными до этого и, возможно, представляющими опасность, мирами. В игре должны были присутствовать постройки ацтеков. Данная идея успела перейти на стадию разработки — сотрудники компании создали играбельный билд «первой» Oblivion Lost.
Однако концепция игры, схожая со «Звёздными вратами», показалась разработчикам вторичной. В рамках создания такой игры требовалась проработка множества виртуальных миров, что небольшой фирме было не по силам. Команда поняла, что создание «ультрареалистичного» игрового мира будет для неё более подходящей задачей, нежели создание фантастического. Кроме того, разработчики хотели найти уникальную для игровой индустрии идею, чтобы встать в один ряд с лучшими разработчиками уже после своего первого большого проекта, и понимали, что их текущая идея, повторяющая уже созданные вещи, таким требованиям не соответствует. 29 марта 2002 года они съездили на экскурсию в зону отчуждения. Это явилось последним шагом к решению о полной замене концепции: она стала напрямую относиться к Чернобыльской АЭС и местности вокруг неё.

The game's pacing is excellent, as it is essentially little more then strings of setpieces, allowing the developers the freedom to carefully craft enemy placement and spawns. I am only choosing the thumbs down option, because i wouldn't recommend the game in its current 'early access' form.  And what i say below is solely based of that understanding that it IS an early access, and that hopefully the glaring problems get fixed.
Main problem:
The Game is pvp based, full time.  Which is fine, I've played such games before and im use to being killed, use to being taunted by immature 15 year olds out for a laugh and such.  BUT, what this game has in it currently that makes the PVP in it both stupid in one aspect, and annoying/frustrating for any first-time players, is partly the Character Creation's fault.
You can make yourself a 3ft tall, skinny as a tree, black skinned character.
What does this do?
Well it seems the damage model, and determining if you get 'hit' or not, is based off your characters unique shape.  There does not appear to be any 'standard' hit-box as it were for avatars.  This means that the best way to make a PVP based character, is to make the smallest, thinnest character you can make.  As anyone with a 'normal' sized character, has to look 'down' the entire time they are trying to defend themselves as well as struggle to hit a 'thing as a rod' shape.  Yet the person running around as the pygmy, has no problem at all hitting the more 'normal' sized character.
As for the skin-tone?  Same as with the size. It offers people an advantage.  That of being nearly impossible to see at dusk/night.  As most of the land is covered in grass, or some type of woodland, those 3-foot tall pygmy's that also have the darkest skin-tone available, are essentially invisible to sight in a game with 'natural' light.  While people with more 'standard' skin-tones (white, tan, brown) stand out like ghosts even at night.
Again, giving all the advantages to the 3-ft tall pygmy's.
If the people working on developing this game wish to keep the same character creation options in it, that they currently do, then they need to ensure that if a player sets their character up to be the lowest possible height, then a 'attack' by anyone at what would be a 'normal' player height, should still hit the player who's made their character 3-ft tall.  Give all avatars, no-mater their shape, the same 'hit-box' as it were.
As for the skin-tone issue. That one i'll not really touch, as it'll just invite the internet version of the 'race-baiters' and the like,  The only thing i can think of is to have players spawn with more clothing than a 'small-clothes' around their waist.. that is colored something other than black (like red or white?) that if removed results in some sort of damage resist penalty unless its replaced by some other clothing thing.
Minor Issue:
A more minor issue i found with the game (again, in its early access state) is the lack of any real 'food' resource near the starting area (generally the beach).  You can find plenty of resources that are needed for crafting, and the crafting itself is rather easy to figure out.  Even gathering water is automatic without having to first craft water-skins.  But food?.. That is rather scarce.   The Map Designers may want to look into 'slightly' overpopulating the spawn-in locations with more berry bushes than they currently do.. or even make a few more chickens show up than what have been.
Asside from thsoe two issues, the game:
Looked GREAT
Ran Well
Was quick to learn the basics
Needs a 'slight' tweak to the crafting interface (mainly making it easier to find specific things)
Could use a bit more Flax.... Flaux?... Flux?... the one resource that seems to be required for all crafting.
Once the PVP/Combat/Hit-detection stuff is changed/fixed.. the Game looks to be a great open-world pvp Sandbox.

Do not let my play time fool you, I've spent an ungoldy amount of time playing this digital heroin before it hit steam. Which if you can already tell, usually is a trademark of a good game.
Factorio is a game about automation, a subject very few if any games tend to build their core theme around. The general idea is you start out on a hostile planet with nothing but a few iron plates in your pockets, and from that you create a sprawling megafactory belching pollution into the atmosphere like it's the industrial revolution. This factory produces everything from small gear wheels to monstrous death tanks and beyond. This fuel for megalomania is achieved by creating machines to do the crafting and hard working for you; miners to do your digging, inserters to do your lifting, conveyors to do your moving, smetlers to do your smelting and assemblers to do your crafting. All the while enraging the natives.
The replay-ability, at least for me comes from the process of streamlining your factory. The first time you play, your base will most likely be a total spaghetti mess with conveyors overlapping conveyors overlapping everything else in a glorious logistical disaster. But as you play new files you'll gradually make the process more efficent and more clean which then snowballs into expansion, in short, this game is perfect if you love hoarding resources as efficently and cost effectivley as possible.
For an early access title, it's one of the most amazingly well done games I've had the pleasure of playing for a long time and is well worth the money, though a word of warning; If you have a life or upcoming deadlines, don't buy this game because it'll suck the play time right out of you.

In terms of creativity this is a very successful sequel and a loving continuation of the Just Cause series. This game is totally gorgeous, fun and loaded with cool content. It’s just such a shame though, that there are some serious problems with the performance. The outstanding quality of the design work, makes it shocking, that it could have been released in such a poorly optimised state. As so much love and consideration seem to have gone into making it something special. However, it appears to be yet another example, of the economic side of things pushing the release date forward. Resulting in an incredible game with mediocre performance at best. The pricing and distribution of the DLC content also represents some shady business practises. Although again, from a design stand-point, this additional content is fantastic stuff.
Following some tweaks which included making some changes in Windows 10. I managed to get it running, just well enough, to be able to enjoy myself. However I am still experiencing crashes, stuttering and poor framerate. I’m running it on a GTX 980, an AMD FX 8350 and 8 Gigs of RAM. Apparently it’s the RAM that’s the main problem, as there is a warning every time I start up the game, stating that my system memory is low. Typically however, my 8 Gigs of system RAM, is totally fine for gaming in 2016. Especially since I spent over 700 Euro to get a GTX 980 with 4 Gigs of VRAM.
Basically, Just Cause 3 runs like♥♥♥♥♥♥and you’ll need a powerful rig to get it running even moderately well. I have read online that if you have 16 Gigs or more of system RAM, it helps a lot but that is not normal. I get how people are angry about the performance problems but this game still deserves a lot of praise.  I’m going to recommend it because it is an example of how amazing videogames can be in 2016. Even though, the corporate money making side of the industry, seem to be determined to ruin things with short term thinking. If you have a decent PC, you can probably still get it running well enough to appreciate how incredible it is.
Edit: I got some feedback in the comments and it seems like some people might also get 'okay' performance, on low to medium end PC'S, with low settings. This seems to be a bit random though, so maybe you should do some research before you buy.

Now I have played a ton of Demon's Souls, Dark Souls and on top of that a couple of the old King's Fields games. I've owned the first two on consoles and figured I would just buy DS2 for the PC even though I've played it for console. I do love From Software but this game to me is more of a step down than a step up.
Each game had it's flaws which is fine since every game can not be perfect to everyone but this one seemed to just upset me. I will just list some Pro's and Con's in my view while explaining why and keep in mind this is just my opinion. Some are self explanatory though so I will just leave them as is. Now I will only post some of the Pro's and Con's I have with this game but these are pretty much some of the aspects I Like/Dislike about it.

1. Dual wielding is more Viable
Due to the power stance or just dual wielding regardless it seems more smooth and fluent than the older titles.

2. Hub for merchants
I did not mind going through areas to get to a certain merchant in DS1 or in Demon's Souls for the few that were not in the nexus but this just made it more convienent.
3. More castings along with a more variety of Hex spells
4. More Bosses along with resulting in more unique items
5. Bonfire Ascetics
While NG + in the previous titles were great for acquiring new items or something you may have missed, being able to do it before then was great. Now I still go for NG + after doing everything but I do like to try to get everything in one go when and if possible.

1. Always go right
Now between the pc and console version I have done everything but half the bosses just made me shake my head. Go fight Old Dragonslayer, The Pursuer, Dragonrider for an example. You can just circle right around them the whole time and kill them without worry.
2. Enemy respawn limit
Sure you could use a bonfire ascetic to make the enemies come back and harder but I preferred it much more to as long as you were able to use a bonfire they would just keep spawning endlessly.
3. Area Design
While some of the areas were great I still miss areas like Tower of Latria and Anor Londo.
4. Too easy
Yeah I played hours upon hours of the previous two so even though I knew how the controls worked and had an advantage etc only had problems with a couple of enemy types which I adapted to quickly.
Go back and reading number 1 of the Cons goes with this as well but I expected more. Demons Souls I died here and there while Dark Souls I died quite a bit more. Out of the hours I had on console and the 90 some I have on here I just did not find much of the game challenging unfortunately.
5. Ambushes
No seriously where did the ambushes go. There were some here and there but that is what killed me most the time in Demons Souls or DS. I think they could have added more but this is not really as important as my other opinions though.
Example like once you find out a guy laying on the ground gets up and jumps at you it just turns out to be common sense to poke at guys laying on the ground just incase so those do not get you anymore either.
Anyway while these are just my opinions and I have had over a few hundred hours logged into each Demon's Souls and DS I just feel it's not as good as the previous ones. Sure I may only have a couple hundred hours on this game all together but I feel I have played it enough to throw it out there.
I still will play it every so and so but just hope if they make another game of the series (Not counting Bloodborne) they will look back at the other two and come up with something a bit more different than this title. I do recommend new players to play the other two though and if they want to pick this one up that is fine but I am going to have to write this off as the other two were great in my book but this one was the bad egg even though still enjoyable just not the same.

+Lots of awesome alternate skins for every God!
+Lots of customization: avatars, God skins, emotes, loading frames, announcer packs, etc.
+New updates/patches very often.
+New gods released often.
+SMITE has an up-and-coming E-sports scene.
+Developers listen to community feedback on forums, (mostly Reddit.)
+At the time of this review there is 6 different gamemodes. Conquest, Clash, Siege, Match of the Day, Joust, and Assault. Also included are 3 ranked modes. Ranked Joust, Ranked Conquest, and Ranked Duel.
Cons:
-Lots of pay walls to get certain skins; ie: having to spend money on a "chest" with 50 items in it, when you only want 2 of the items.
-Some server issues crop up here and there. Nothing too serious.
-Toxic players. What online game doesn't have those, though?
-Only really balanced around one gamemode, Conquest. Though, every mode is balanced well.
Overall, the pros outway the cons by a ton. I highly recommend this game.

Welcome back to Planet Mobius / earth - no one even knows at this point - where Sonic is called for an emergency attack on a nearby city. The path towards the city has turned into a desert and debris is everywhere. When Sonic shows up to the city Eggman is back at it again, taking over the world and such, Sonic makes some witty comments, Eggman makes a less witty comeback and then, out of the blue, a new foe appears. This new foe goes by the name “Infinite” (do not steal) and is seemingly invincible. Along with him are foes of Sonic’s past and together they beat him senselessly, to the point of incapacitating Sonic. He is presumed dead and through the coming months Eggman builds his empire over the defenseless people of Mobius / Earth. A resistance, compiled of Sonic’s friends, is formed to retaliate against the control Eggman has gained over the world. Turns out, there’s a new recruit coming soon and that recruit is... You. Meanwhile an unsuspecting Tails is about to meet his doom to the hands of Eggman’s minions. Suddenly, an interdimensional wormhole comes out of seemingly nowhere and who else would come out of this wormhole, but Classic Sonic! He saves Tail’s life and they travel together in order to rendezvous with the resistance and end this endless battle.
All things considered, the premise is really good. This is what a good plot in Sonic should be: blunt, while also making sure it’s not being too serious. I do believe that there’s more potential to this story than what it currently is, but it’s good nonetheless.
Infinite is given backstory in the Shadow Episode and is genuinely interesting. Classic Sonic is in this game, but no one cares, so moving on.
People like to refer to this game as “Sonic Generations 2”, but I’d say it’s more along the lines of Sonic Colours 2 mixed with a few Generations aspects. Rings are still your life force and there are three characters - and therefore three playstyles - Modern Sonic (The one who “dies”), Avatar (The one you create) and Classic Sonic (The one nobody asked for).
Modern Sonic is fast paced action, goal is to get to the end of the stage as fast as possible. He has a boost, a stomp and a homing attack. Modern’s boost has always been the simplest mechanic he has had, never actually needing to use brain cells in order to use it. This game is no exception and even steers Modern for you in certain sections. I am not a fan of this mechanic, I like the fact one may go fast, but the game just comes out too easy as a result. The game does prompt you to stop your momentum for quick platforming with mechanics such as the stomp. Using this in mid air allows Modern to stop all momentum which makes it useful for platforming in 2D sections. The homing attack makes Modern even simpler to play. This ability homes in on enemies if you jump in their general direction. I may sound like I’m complaining, but I’m honestly fine with this gameplay style.
Avatar stages are very much like Modern’s stages; fast paced, 3D level design, etc. You can design the avatar - as it is an avatar - as you so desire. You can choose from seven different species: Dog, Wolf, Cat, Bear, Rabbit, Bird and a Hedgehog! Each of these have their own perks. Difference gameplay-wise being that there is no boost and every homing attack feels as slow as riding shopping cart in a mall. Homing attacks utilise a wire hook, with which you can swing from certain floating sphere thingys. Most of this is automated however, which is really disappointing as it could’ve opened some potential for really great level design. Think that’s the only difference? Think again Buddy! You have the most broken and overpowered weapons known to hedgehog. Introducing wispons! You get a choice of: Burst, Drill, Hover, Cube, Lightning and Void. Burst is a flamethrower allowing you to mow down enemies like that time you used deodorant as a makeshift flamethrower; Drill is a… drill and gives you a burst of speed thrusting you forward like there’s no such thing as hit detection; Hover is essentially a shotgun blast and pushes enemies into each other; Cube is a massive hammer that destroys enemies and turns them into coins (Yes, coins); Lightning is a lightning whip that thrusts you forward as you destroy everything in front of you; Void is a gun which shoots literal black holes around three times the size of your avatar. This literally works as a black hole, SEGA has gone mad with power send help. Each of these Wispons have abilities that will skip entire sections of levels all working in the same fashion: gain height or gain speed. The avatar is honestly the greatest part about this game. The levels are well made, the mechanics are solid and it brings something new to Sonic without it seeming too drastic of a game changer.
Now time to talk about the literal worst thing that happened to Sonic Generations as well as this game: Classic Sonic. You liked Sonic Mania? Me too, let’s put a speed cap on it and break literally all momentum when jumping. Classic Sonic is as basic as it gets; 2D platforming, your run-of-the-mill spin dash and the all new drop dash. There really isn’t much to say about this one honestly. He’s the boring character, his gameplay has degraded from Generations and he’s just shoved into the plot because Sonic Mania came out three months ago.
(DLC)
Episode Shadow takes place a month before Eggman’s attack. It consists of three short missions containing backstory for Infinite as well as Shadow’s appearance in the main storyline. Think of this as a free side distraction from the main game that doesn’t bring anything new. This does, however, allow you to play as Shadow in Modern Sonic stages which is pretty neat.
- Avatar brings new and interesting ideas for future games
- Soundtrack is memorable and something unexpected from a Sonic game
- Modern Sonic has improved mechanics since his last appearance
- Story is interesting at some major points in the story
- Classic Sonic is at his worst due to the Hedgehog Engine 2.0
- Level design is short and sometimes uninspired
- Game feels like it’s on autopilot for half of the entire game
All in all, Sonic Forces really isn’t a great game, nor is it a bad game. This game
had three level designers and really suffers as a result of it. Some of the most fun I’ve had in this game is breaking it trying to get the fastest times possible. This game isn’t bad, it’s just disappointing in some aspects. 6/10.

And of course, just when you think you've got a handle on checking d.o.b, gender, home country, work visas, etc, etc, you have to start cross checking more documents.
One particular mechanic that I'm thrilled by is how the timeline is handled. You can jump back to any previous day and branch a new story-line to see different consequences instead of having to start all over again. I don't know how many times you can do this, but even just once is nice, as opposed to starting back from day 1 to see how different day 29 could have been.
I hope to see more from this developer in the future.

In conclusion, there are hit or miss new additions, but still a solid game overall. Rome 1 is still my favorite, followed by Medieval 2, but this game is worthy of the franchise.

Androids. I just loved them. there was definitely something ironic and sarcastic in the way they'd be polite, try to help, "worry" that you may get hurt, etc, but actually just attempting to do Alien's job for him.
What i didn't like was the ending. now, I don't know if there will be a sequel, or whatever, but it certainly felt like i've played this game for nothing in the end. I know, all opinios are subjective and all, but couldn't help feeling this way. Like, the damned Alien just had to be there on the other ship no matter what. Too predictable and unnecessary to the point you throw your hands in the air and yell WHYYYYYYY? But my opinion is my opinion.
Next. Alien. Glued to Ripley like a nasty piece of bubblegum that gets stuck on your shoes if you step in it accidentally. Who cares about these other random people on Sevastopol? Ripley surely tastes better.
People enemies. Seriously. Even the Alien himself didn't spot me in the far far far corner of the coridor, but these normal ordinary people with a guns miraculously noticed me everywhere, probably heard me fart behind the screen and shot my... nether region. Besides, is that even that necessary? Yeah, there are mobs, but c'mon. That can't be the entire crew on the station (a few sobbing randoms don't count).
I'm not asking for an easy game to go through and be comepletely and totally guided by the hand. No. What i mean is Alien, androids and human foes - it gets repetitive and boring, which, I believe, was a pity because Alien sure deserves more than that. I think it would aid to the suspense if Alien did not pop up so often and didn't remaine glued to Ripley for the entire game, but rather, kept on reminding of his presence, and showed up when you'd least expect him. More puzzles would help too. And it wouldn't be so annoying to hide and crouch all the time when you could've at least had some time to explore around the station. I found that in many cases, I had to run through the area and skip so many places simply because i'd get Alien giving me a warm hug, had i dared to go anywhere. Therefore, this was scary at the start, plain eyerolling later on.
Verdict. 7.5/10

Borderlands 2 Review
What is Borderlands 2
Borderlands 2 is a FPS (First Person Shooter) that takes place on an alien planet called Pandora. Pandora is a ruthless unforgiving world consisting of bandits, rivaling companies fighting over a resource called eredium, mutants, and alien wildlife that’s only seeks to kill you and your friends. Though not all is death and pain on Pandora.
In borderlands 2 there a great deal of features and unique skills you can utilize to change your style of gameplay and experience throughout the game.
Pros
When playing borderland there are six characters the player can chose to experience the game from. Each character has three skill trees with 11 different skills each tree, making for 33 individual skills to choose from. Depending on what tree you chose your style of gameplay varies from each character.
For ex. The Psycho is a melee based character whose special ability relies on heavy close combat with the enemies. And in contrast to Zero an assassin who uses long ranged weapons to deal damage from afar.
Some of the Psycho’s skill trees, Bloodlust and hell born have similar gameplays. Bloodlust allows for buffs on enemy kills while hell born relies on a chance to catch on fire to gain damage boosts, the ability to heal from catching aflame, and a unique ability that lets the psycho to breathe fire.
Zero’s two trees, sniping and bloodshed have completely different stiles of gameplay where one relies on ranged weapons while the other tree provides boosts to melee stealth ability.
Story and quests
The main story starts off with the player chosen character navigating through a glacier with a small robot. The glacier is used as a prologue or an introduction area to allow the player to learn the controls and prepare them for the main game. It offers small side quests and lets the player go at their own pace. In the prologue following the main quest is difficult without doing side quest to level up the character.
One of the first side quest you obtain is to clean a grave yard of alien monsters called bullymong. In this quest the player is rewarded with cash and experience. Experience levels the character up making them stronger so that they can complete the main story quests.
Another side quest at the beginning is to obtain bullymong fur by meleeing the alien brutes to death. After the fur is collected you receive an option, you can give the fur to your trusty robot companion or sir hammerlock the one who give you the quest in the first place. Depending on who you chose out of hammerlock or your robot you can receive either a new sniper or a new shotgun.
Graphics and gameplay
Borderlands 2’s graphics are different in their own creative way from other games.
The game looks like it was taken right out of a comic book. It has the features and 3d look of an FPS but its developers chose not to make the graphics look realistic. Instead they aimed to replicate the look of something animated on purpose.
Each individual weapons along with their abilities, ammo's, stats and look are randomly generated. This also applies to the gear that can be found through the game as well.
All Pandorian monsters have their own individual abilities making each encounter challenging and interesting.
Pandora is an open world where you can chose your path, vehicles are available to hasten your travel over your journey between quests.
Con
Rarely Minor bugs occur when venturing into the wasteland. Usually these don’t change or affect gameplay. These unusual occurrences often happen in multiplayer and can provide a laugh when playing with friends.
For instance in one case when playing online during a cut scene a characters head made an abnormal 180 degrees turn for 5 seconds until snapping back into place in an instant.
Conclusion
This concludes my borderlands 2 review. As displayed above the pros outweigh the cons for this game. Personally its one of my all-time favorite 4 player online FPS’s to play with friends.
Single player alone for the story and comedy is worth buying this game. You’ll be laughing nonstop with your friends while shooting down your foes in the face. I hope this review will help you decide (or not) to buy this game.

Very fun game so far.   The taxation concept is implemented in a nice way that makes it easier on rp(taxation is automatic) little explanation required).  Hopefully they continue to add more things to enjoy while they polish other things off.
Character customization is pretty good so far,  you can make your character look goofy or similar to that of a cartoon character or you can try to even things out for a normal image.  I also respect the Banner customization,  although it could use more sigils to pick from.
It feels good to choose a sigil and give it a color,  then shoose a color of the backround etc.
It is great to place your "crest" in-game and have your banner displayed on it as well as letting visitors know whose land they tread upon.  Whether you refer to your guild as a House,  Clan,  Order,  Cult,  etc.,  or some other such thing,  it can be personal,  or you can join another player by swearing fealty to theirs and adopt their banner by doing so.
Once again this indirectly helps rp for those who wish to rp family members or property to create a more sustainable community/gaming experience.
If you play on a server with ppl who do not suffer from a lack of vision,  you might be able to forge alliances and establish neighor and guest rights while political intrigue developes itself.
Like in most of these types of games,  there is lag at times,  there are cheaters/exploiters abroad,  dealing with servers hosted by strangers usually sucks because it's a hit and miss trying to find responsible hosts that don't exploit(or allow thier friends to exploit).
That being said this game still presents much potential for capitolizing on certain concepts and implementing them in a logical manner.
It took me a while to upgrade my fist castle attempt,  while testing out the various craftable technology(forge,  windmill.  torture devices,  execution devices,  cages,  weapons,  armor,  hanging objects,  wall objects,  ground things,  small banners,  Large banners!,  doors,  windows,  etc.),  They have plenty of weapons but could use color dyes or more armor sets to help with faction-ing.

The graphics aren't the best in the world but the game is fun.  The physics could use some work but I didn't care much.
I would hide in my castle and look out the the ocean during the thunderstorm environment,  the sound effects of the storm,  and intensity of the rain during these parts seemed realistic enough and caused my anxiety to grow and become overwhelmingly apparent.
In closing I would like to say that this game is fun so far and best played with friends or on servers with like-minded people.  I recommend this game for the progressive implementaion of it's concepts and the potential to supply one with actual gaming(fun).  If they manage to add enough more things to it and fix the bugs it could turn out really good.

Let's face facts, Techland, as a developer, sucks.  Badly.  Their track record is one of bugs, glitches, poor writing, and general failure.  Needless to say when I saw the developement for CoJ Gunslinger I was skeptical as ♥♥♥♥, hell we all were.  But trust me when I say that this game is astonishingly good, especially coming from Techland.  It is, at it's heart, a combo based western twitch shooter, basically the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ child of Bulletstorm and GUN (RIP GUN we miss you).  The game's pacing is excellent, as it is essentially little more then strings of setpieces, allowing the developers the freedom to carefully craft enemy placement and spawns.  The game is short (roughly 6 hours for one playthrough) but vastly entertaining, with (what is quite literally) one of the best uses of Unreliable Narrator I've ever seen in contemporary games.  Everything feels polished and fun, with additional Arcade and Dueling modes to round out the replayable story.  This is easily going to eat up 20 hours or more of my time, and it definitely seems like one of those games I'll be dusting off years from now just to hear Silas snarl his way through the story one more time.

This game is an enigma for me. Russian 'end of the world' stories all seem to revolve around 'bombs drop, we all die... yet we don't all die. Mutants attack, weird anomolys pop up... we have to survive in this nightmare.' Now in this game it's not the end of the world, only the area around Chernobyl.
The game is rife with interesting options for ways to kill people. There are some systems in the game that don't really effect gameplay as much as you'd expect (factions for instance... you can pretty much fight whomever you want/can kill... instead of spending weeks farming faction lol). Stealth is by far better rewarded than in most games, but you can still take the 'RAMBO MUTHA F*(&&*%*&%ERS!' approach, but be prepared to get lit up if you are outgunned. The mutants are pretty interested and surprising, and the anomolies can really make the landscape alive... in more ways than one.
There is some minor RPG elements with the way gear works, but honestly once you get the hang of it you can pretty much get your hero up to insane levels of power and plow through targets with little effort, just have to spend time getting the right rocks... so to speak.
Graphically the game is a bit dated, but the gameplay holds up. If you want a nice open world feel for a nightmare... by all means get this game. If you get stuck (Learning curve can be a bit rough) look up one of the hundreds of guides out there to give you a hand.

Transistor, a cyberpunk themed action RPG made by Supergiant Games is set in a futuristic city called “Cloudbank”. You take the role of “Red”, a young women who gains control of an extraordinary weapon. After a mysterious group nearly kills you, you start your journey, slowly puzzling the story.
The art style, music, and narration create a gorgeous, astonishing and captivating place you want to be part of. Beautifully drawn and rich locations where every step is a pleasure to the eyes, the amazing music by Darren Korb, the fantastic voice acting by Logan Cunningham and the memorable, intriguing characters which grow to your heart are not the only aspects that the game has to offer. The combat is remarkably fun and fresh. While you only have one weapon, there are dozens of "functions" which you collect on your journey through Cloudbank. Those functions act as perks which can be  combined with each other and/or used either aggressively or passively matching your playstyle.
All  in all Transistor is a masterpiece and is probably my favourite indie game. Not only I recommend on buying the game but the gorgeous soundtrack it offers which is absolutely worth it.

The world, although pretty cool with its programming theme, isn't as vibrant as I hoped it would be. The character backstories you unlock through fighting aren't really all that interesting either, although the main story is still fairly solid.
The ending is good but also rather abrupt. I had hoped for a bit more to it, but it was done well and really I'm only complaining about anything at all because I'd previously played Bastion.

Alright, this review is going to be a long one but I'm telling you this now, I completed the story and these are all my opinions. Also, I'll add a new bulletpoint to this everytime I think of a new topic or I remember a topic I forgot to mention. But I won't change what I already wrote. Finally, SPOILER ALERT!
Pros:
-The music is amazing, obviously. Yes, there is no Crush 40, but "Fist Bump" and "Light of Hope" are two GREAT songs regardless. The piano is truely heart warming. Just listen to both of these songs. The Classic Sonic music has a bit of issues in my point of view, but it's okay. Again, the piano is amazing in the instrumental verison of "Light of Hope." I'm a little biased by it cause I play piano, but moving on.
-Your avatar tries to make you feel like a kid again fighting along side Sonic and his friends and honestly, it worked for me. The last cutscene where Sonic says "You and I aren't so different. See ya later, buddy." and gives you a fist bump honestly touched me. Having a custom avatar was a great idea by SEGA.
-Graphics and frame rate are top tier. Nothing else needs to be said.
-The overall idea of Eggman taking over 99.99% of the world and you, Sonic, and his friends having to fight back in an all out war-themed game is so different than previous Sonic games. It's not happy-go-lucky nobody gets hurt or dies. I think SEGA finally realized that most of its fanbase is much older and needs a different themed game and they did a good job.
-Cutscenes are great and they have great voice acting.
-Avatar customization has a bunch of options for you to choose from so go nuts creating your own character.
Cons:
-The character movingment is choppy and Sonic's double jump is practically nothing like Sonic Colors or Generations. Classic Sonic's jump feels like the gravity increased. The Avatar is the only one that has good movement.
-The level design in Modern Sonic 3-D sections is practically automatic. All you do is hold the boost button and BOOM, you win. I like that there is more 3-D now, but it does most of the work for you
-Classic Sonic in this game is kinda cool but we already had plenty of 2-D Sonic in Sonic Mania. I know that Sonic Mania and Sonic Forces are connected with Classic Sonic traveling between dimmensions with the help of the Chaos Emeralds and Phantom Ruby but I don't get that nostalgia feeling and honestly, I don't want to with this game. Sonic Mania took care of that.
-Speaking of nostalgia, the inclusion of Green Hill and Chemical Plant is redundant. We already had Sonic Generations and Mania including both of these stages so enough is enough. I'd like some new stages please and maybe some diffferent classic stages.
-The radio conversations between characters before a stage is great and all but it's too much. And during the stage the conversations take keep interupting the gameplay. They are annoying most of the time and I think they could be condensed into a few extra cutscenes.
-There is no reward for collecting all the Red Rings, Green Numbered Rings, and Silver Moon Rings. I didn't get all of them but when I heard that there is no reward for getting them all, I lost interest.
-There is no Super Sonic in this game to my knowledge. Again, I thought getting all the Red Rings would unlock him but no. There are rumors going around about DLC but I don't know all the details.
-Also, the amount of air you get underwater as Classic Sonic seems A LOT shorter than Sonic Generations ans Sonic Mania.
Mixed Topics:
-The Red Rings are practically handed to you. I played though each stage and I got all of them in one run in 10 out of the 30 stages. This can go either way depending on if you want them to be challenging or easy to collect.
-Game length is short where you can complete it in about 3 hours. However, there are a bunch of extra stages plus Episode Shadow so they try to rope you into playing those.
-Daily missions are a thing and I'm kinda split on this one.
Again, these are my opinions and I'll be adding to this whenever I think of a new topic. But in short, if someone were to ask me "Should I get Sonic Forces?" I'd say "It's a good game so yes, but wait until it goes on sale for $20. Get Sonic Mania first since it ties into Sonic Forces and it's better. Plus Sonic Mania is already $20." Final Score: 7.0/10

A smooth and polished game, a bit short but generally very enjoyable.
Modern Sonic:
Basically the same gameplay as what it was in Generations.
Avatar:
Similar to Modern Sonic, with slightly more platforming and slightly less speed, and has a few weapons and wisp abilities to choose from. A familiar but yet refreshing experience.
Classic Sonic:
Fun to play, but can't really compare to Mania (which you could expect).
Length:
30 main stages (bosses included), 9 extra stages and 3 DLC stages, making up a total of 42. Each has a length of about 2 minutes if you go smoothly without dying. I would say slightly shorter than Colours (which had 45 stages).
Story and story-telling:
The main story is not very complicated. I would say the script and the (English) acting is much better than in Colours, Generations and Lost World. Good rhythm and tension. Has some plot holes but nevermind. Appreciate the handling of the title screen, world map and ending in creating the story atmosphere.
Stage design:
Stages blend well into the story. Not as diversed as recent games. Some stages are really good, a few feel like replicates of old stages.
Difficulty:
"Hard mode" is about the same difficulty as in Colours.
Music:
Awesome like always.
Re-playability:
I would go back for the red rings, try out different wispons and speed-running some of the stages. May sometimes return for the music and the boss fights.
Others:

If this is your first Sonic game,
do not be turned off by what the "in" crowd calls bad controls/physics. Sonic simply does not follow the standard formula when it comes to jumping and in air control. Learn to think of the jump button as an analog stick and use the differring jump heights as your control and not try to maneuver with the stick so much. Learn that he is a speed character so you will have to jump ahead of normal platformers as his very real momentum will take you over an edge. Accept that and we're good, if you fight it then you will give into the dark side of Sonic hate.
While I still think Generations is the better game, I really enjoyed this one, especially that the story itself asks you to replay areas as S.O.S. missions because once you play a stage a few times you will inevitably get a better feel for it and possibly even get into flow. I also liked that they got rid of lives in that you just start from the checkpoint as many times as it takes (and I died a lot)
The main downside is that the game is pretty short. I never ever achieved the completion time of any game on HowLongToBeat and I didnt here either but I still finished it including multiple S.O.S. missions and the unlocked special stages (but not Shadow episodes yet) in half the time it took me to finish Generations and Lost World.
Also, just my opinion, but I liked the story.

So, Borderlands 2; a friend of mine who also has it gifted it to me and I was excited, I heard a lot of great things about this game and thought it looked cool to try out thanks to my friend.
What do I think about it? It's a good game, but in my opinion it is a bit overrated in some respects, and is given a little too much credit in places it probably should not recieve such credit. First off what I liked about the game. The gameplay of the game is fairly solid and balanced, you won't find yourself in an area of the game that a level 6 player should not be in, the tutorial and how to play section of the game is straight forward and simple; duck, take cover, fire and kill anyone trying to kill you. This is doubled by the setting of the game with a psuedo-space western style sci-fi storyline where you are basically thrown in the wastelands of what space considers the Wild-Wild West. The guns are amazing and neatly designed gameplay wise and aesthetic wise, the dialogue and characters are for what it is worth; hilarious and fun.
With that said though; as much as I enjoyed it, I do have a few qualms with this game that I feel I need to address in detail, most notably the story. I am honestly not that big a fan of it; all the characters while fun and enjoyable, I can honestly say they don't really do much to make themselves memorable or iconic. All of the characters' personalities kind of run together all the same to be honest with me being incapable of being able to tell them apart from their personality traits alone. Not that there aren't any that are memorable, but the ones that do stick out don't appear or are showed off as often due to the whims of the story; everyone kind of is a wisecracking, crazy murderous freedom fighter that basically are after one goal. There is some level of backstory and lore to create a method within the madness of this story, but I honestly forget what it was because it kind of takes a backseat to it all in the end, at least from a details perspective.
I also am not a fan of the AI in this game. I mean, the core mechanics of the game is to be a sort of tactical shooter with RPG elements with level up systems, statistic calculations with different weapons and equipment, but the enemies kind of play the game like it is not such, they seem to be able to take more bullets and damage from the players weapons than you can take from them it seems like no matter how much higher your gears' stats are, how does a Level 6 enemy survive a Level 29 Assault Rifle more than one round? I'll never know how. Another problem with this games AI is that the game relies on simply pounding you with enemies and surrounding you with them and overrunning you by shear numbers rather than actually being more tactile than you. I know the in-universe explenation is because the majority of the enemies in the game aren't very bright, but that doesn't excuse the rest of them that play this way and the way that they can basically overcome the Tactical Shooter Base of the game, again, judging by how the player plays, that is the idea; but the enemies don't follow that which I find not really game breaking, just weird and a bit frustrating at times.
Overall; I do think it is a game that is worth a look for anyone interested in a semi-open world First Person RPG shooter.

First semi-serious review here;
In all this game is worth the £15 asking price.
There are problems with hackers, yes. However this is an issue mostly solved by joining whitelisted or passworded servers. Although having said that there are many whitelisted and passworded servers that are completely rife with admin abuse such as;
****    Vikings 24/7     ***** (Dont join if you value your time)
The game is fun, really fun actually. Running around gathering resources and building bases is really good and the developers have really got it right in that regard - base building is a time consuming but entirely fun and rewarding experience. The problem with building a base is that you may find yourself close to breaking point when you log on and find your base (which took you hours to build and perfect) is destroyed by hackers or server admins (like what happened to me on Vikings 24/7 server). It would be entirely unfair to blame the devs for the latter problem but it seems the former issue will be solved sometime in the near future.
However the Devs have explained that they are focusing on installing more stringent anti-hacking software to combat the hacking, that is, in truth, rife. I have no reason to disbelieve them as they
like fair and hard working individuals that care deeply about their game and won't just take your money and run (a la "The Stomping Lands"). This is reinforced by regular communication to the community and updates most weekends. So good job on that devs.
The combat system is fun some of the time but most of the time it isn't. It's not wholly trash but is in a serious need of a tune up. Buggy, laggy and in the worst of cases - a nightmare.  To compare it to chivalry is sort of misleading and does RoK no justice.
Yes it has the same type of attacks (overhead, thrust and swing) but the blocks are not the same and it has
of the fluidity and complexity that chivalry brings to the table.  However i think the developers may have shot themselves in the foot by referencing Chivalry when it comes to combat because Chivalry in many eyes is the pinnacle of medieval combat (despite all the drag-hards) and it focuses purely on that combat. Where as i see Reign of Kings in a different light - its bigger than Chivalry in respect to the game's scope and concepts. Is it completely fair to draw a comparison? No. Reign of Kings is as much about building bases, guilds and gathering resources as it is about combat and while the combat lags behind in development its other facets are being improved. It sadly doesn't solve the problem of fps drops, phantom reach, lag and hack and slash attitude to the combat system - where it seems that 90% of people just run around slashing as much as they can in hope for a kill.
Ideally, being a huge Chivalry fan i would love to see the same fluidity, variation and complexity in combat in RoK as resides in Chivalry but its a tall order - perhaps even an unjust one.
TL;DR
+GG
+Fun with friends
+Good Devs (so far)
+Base building is great fun
-FPS drops
-Clunky combat system
-Hackers
Worth £15? In my opinion - yes. Its always more fun with people though.

I've got an MSI Ghost GS60 gaming laptop. My specs are the stock ones if you want to look it up.
This is easily one of the most polished and well put together early access titles I've ever played. This is easily one of my favorite games in my library. I initially saw the game on their website and a friend and I decided to purchase it for a fun romp through torture/kidnapville. It turns out that I did very little torturing and kidnapping upon actually playing the game.
There is no terrain deformation or "terraforming" in this game and it does not intend on being implemented at all. At first, this may seem like a negative point, but the fact that the terrain is static affords for a much more strategic implementation of your building without the concern of people digging in or under your base. Building is fairly simple once you understand the mechanics, and if you've played Starforge, the block placement scheme is identical.
Environments are beautifully rendered and harvestable resources look natural while still being easy to identify. The lighting effects are second to none, and they way that the light sort of hazily bends around physical objects, (even if they are player made) is astounding for a title in it's alpha stages.
Weapons and armor are well balanced, but the combat system could use more depth. For instance, you currently do the same amount of damage regardless of using a stab, slice, or overhead attack. This will be easy to eventually fix, and I'm sure that they have plans to do so in the future. Siege weaponry falls into three categories; trebuchets, (which you have to counterweight and load) balistas, and bombs. As I am writing this review, bombs have been disabled due to the devastation that they can cause with an hours worth of grinding. I am not sure if they will be added in at a later date or rebalanced. All other siege engines work well within the game's resource curve and require more skill to use.
The only complaints that I have entail a more stable resource cost for certain blocks, and the actual public servers hosted by Code}{atch having serious issues. Obviously, greater anti-cheat measure need to be implemented as well, but in alpha stages, I don't expect that to be on the top of the to-do list.
Playing on a public server, (my first and only experience was with NA South B2) you will experience lag spikes almost every time a new player joins, and the servers will very frequently de-sync. The de-sync can be fixed by simply logging out and back in, but anything that you did during that period of de-sync is effectively null and void, as the game will place you back at the most recently synced instance. This can be quite annoying, especially because it tends to occur about once an hour (give or take). If you read any of the other reviews, you'll see that there is also a very large hacker population in the game. I use the term "hacker" lightly, because they're really just running a trainer in the background, so script kiddy would be a more accurate description.
Playing on a private server, I have experienced exactly zero of the afore mentioned issues. We have a small group of individuals on an RP instance and we all work to create rules and a running story for our kingdom. It's similar to a public server without the griefing. If someone takes the throne on our server, it's because they gathered men and laid siege to the castle and it's just awesome. The server never de-syncs and we have an extremely strict anti-hacker/anti-exploit admin who is not timid with the ban hammer.
I would never play this game on anything but a good private server. The difference is night and day, and there are tons of private servers that are hosting all of the time with different designations (i.e. combat, building, RP, etc.) Otherwise, the base game is great fun and one of the best games I've played in 2015 thus far.

I know that when some people hear "Call of Juarez" their minds jump strait to the monster of a game that "The Cartel" was, probably the game that ruined the series, however Gunslinger does a complete 180.
Gameplay: The gunfighting in this game may seem generic at best, a closer look shows that it is a very well fleshed out system. You score XP for each kill in a "Bulletstorm" style system rewarding you for more unusual kills and combo chains. You then use those point to buy skills that improve your preformance with weapons and even extend your combos.
Visuals: Visually "Gunslinger" has a very impressive artstyle that draws heavily from games like "Borderlands". Set peices are vibrant with colors that bring the game to life. I've forgotten how good a game looks when you get away from the grey's and browns of most of the games that have recently come out.
Story: Without getting into the Spoiler territory, Gunslinger's story is a classic Old West tale of "The Dish Best Served Cold". You play as a bounty hunter named Silas Greaves who is on the tail of the one person who can quench his thirst for revenge. The entire game is brilliantly covered by some grade A voice. Whenever a character adds or removes something from the story it will physically change change the level you are playing right before your eyes. When one of the Starry eyed kids listening to my story recalled one of my exploits from a dime novle that had me duleing Wesley Hardin, Silas jumped in and corrected him on what really happend. I went from dueling one guy to being in a shoot out with half a dozen. Its a very welcome and enjoyable twist to storytelling and this game nails it.
Even if the gunplay is somewhat generic the stunning visuals and the amazing story make this game a breath of fresh air in the stale cloud that makes up todays shooters. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who likes an amazing if somewhat short story.
9.1/10

Call of Juarez: Gunslinger... good, bad or ugly?
First, forget everything that CoJ: The Cartel brought you in the CoJ franchise. That previous CoJ was pitiful and a very bad game (still, will buy it once it get utterly cheap one day though) and I'm glad Techland decide to get back into the Wild West with Gunslinger. The game seems to follow a few tidbits of backstory from CoJ: Bound in Blood, as the McCall brothers, aka the protagonists of BiB are mentionned a few times in Gunslinger. Aside from that, if you never played any CoJ, it doesn't matter as in my opinion, this Gunslinger is surely the best CoJ game there is.
PROS:
+Fun gunplay.
+Great voice acting and soundtrack.
+Decent graphics for a budget title (Chrome Engine 5, same as Dead Island).
+Furious pacing, no filler and all killing spree!
+The narrative approach is quite interesting.
CONS:
-Sound-clipping issues at release but were fixed lately from a patch.
-Main campaign is short and very linear (expected for a budget title).
-Frustrating damage indicator.
-Duel mode can be tedious to master.
-Predictable ending.
OVERALL:
For  a Call of Juarez game, I've enjoyed Gunslinger pretty much and I'd even say it is slightly better than Bound in Blood (which that one is a very good CoJ game!).
I recommend Gunslinger especially for a budget title, you can't go wrong with it. For a cheap game, you should give it a chance! Better yet, if you love Wild West games, you'll like Gunslinger pretty much! It is reassuring that Techland is heading in the right direction with Gunslinger and I do hope some continuation follows later on!
RATING:
8.0 / 10

I just played and completed this for the first time and despite it being almost a decade old, it was one of the best shooters I've played in a long time.
The game truly makes you feel alone in the Zone; you'll learn a lot as you play, almost every encounter is incredibly dangerous, and you'll be scavenging for ammo at every opportunity.
I'd recommend playing on 'Master' difficulty, as the enemies are bullet sponges on lower difficulties and 'Master' doesn't really become ridiculously difficult until the end of the game. Most importantly, apply the fix shown at the link below to cure mouse input lag and other anomalies otherwise present in the Steam version:

Honestly, I understand not everyone may like it, its dated and at times clunky or cheesey, confusing even and sometimes frustrating, but if youre able to overlook the simple flaws it has, beneath is an incredible gem of a game.
Its based (very loosely) on the Russian novel "Roadside Picnic" by Arkady and Boris Strugatsky.
(Which is a fantastic novel Id also recommend)
I have yet to play the sequels but Ive heard this is the best of the games. There is also a movie titled "stalker" that once again loosely shares a similar plot to the games and novel.
The atmosphere and chills the game produces is fantastic.
It actually scared me senseless at sometimes and the enemies you fight are unique and interesting, even if you may tire of killing them over and over as there isnt too much variety, but the game remains fresh by supplying you with new weapons, locations, items, artifacts, armour and other loot that keeps you sastified throughout your playthrough.
The look of the Zone and the areas around it are incredible. You feel a sense of dread and fascination as you walk into open areas filled with destroyed facilities, communications stations, army bases, abandoned towns and villages, Stalker camps and strongeholds, safe zones and pieces of land scorched by anomalies that will turn you into paste or burn you alive.
Very fun exploration too as the Zone just looks great. Collecting artifacts and making profit feels rewarding and the battles are nerve gripping at times. Play with headphones at night for best experience (seriously though)
There are basic survival needs as well, the character must eat periodically, bandages are used to stop bleeding, medkits heal greater wounds and later on radiation, infections, burns etc. Some enviromental suits protect against these things too. Different ammo types for practically every type of weapon..
I could go on and on, but you really should just try it for yourself!
Definitely worth it!
It usually goes on sale quite often too, so grab it during one and youll save a bunch!

People seem mixed about Sonic Forces. I guess it's time for a review then.
Pros.
► Clean graphics and overall effects.
► Musics and soundtracks are great. Since it's a Sonic game, we couldn't except less.
► Overall story. I said overall, it has flaws but I think it's still a decent way to put almost anyone important to the Sonic universe in the same storyline.
► Custom character. Wipsons, clothes and gameplay feel complete and pretty polished. Even if I am not a huge fan of the "Trot foward for 3 second to high speed run" which feels random. This was a pretty nice bet Sega won. Time to show the world your edgy and cheesy boi.
► Overall gameplay. I've also said overall. It's indeen feel fast and like the previous modern Sonic games. However there are some letdown that need to be pointed out. QTE are new addition which feels nice on the first try since it's super easy but gets old up to a certain playtime
► Infinite. Even Shadow looks less dark and edgy next to him, but the introduction of the Jackal race in the Sonic universe was nicely executed and he really feels like the real Neutral Evil boi we needed for Sonic Forces.
► Characters that appears in the game always have a decent role like mah boi Silver. HOWEVEEEERRR some got tricked and only earn a poor cameo or even no apparence at all.
► DLCs policy. Free and feels like a real addition to the game and not like a hole in a unfinished game unlike other comapnies' DLC policies.
► Replayability. Some people will argue with this but that's okay. I love to do again times to times my favorite levels.
► PC port. I AM TALKING ABOUT THE PORT ITSELF NOT THE OPTIMISATION. We finally have a proper options menu and settings unlike previous titles that used that silly settings window, that was translated by a silly dude, before starting the game
Neutrals.
► No Infinite introduction. Even the Shadow Episode doesn't provide a proper introduction to Infinite. Which means we have to read the comic or the wikia to understand it.
► Gameplay issues and randomness is of course a problem due to the weird jump system in the 3 phases system (Classic Sonic, Modern Sonic and Costum Character). Unfortunately I got used to it, but at the beginning of the game of course it didn't feel right.
► 30 FPS lock on cutscene. Well, when the game came out, on day one, if you didn't lauched the game in Big Picture, the cutscene and QTE would go nuts at like 15 FPS with awful audio bugs no matter which set up you got. Now it has been patched like yesterday and it feels of course better. Still, it's 30 FPS.
Cons.
► PC port optimisation is mostly trash. I didn't expect any issues but a lot of people are experiencing crashes at some points of the game. Meaning they can't go any further in the storyline. So watch out.
► Classic Sonic. Yes I said earlier his gameplay was okay. But nexto to Generations his gameplay is not okay at all. Frustrating, long blind jump, autoscrolling on Iron Fortress (worst level), bad jump and annoying dash sum up prety much what Classic Sonic has to offer.
► Storyline holes are somewhat a problem too. Who is Infinite? What is the Jackal Squad? Where does the Phantom Ruby come from? Phantom Ruby prototypes? What this the fate of Dr.Eggman and Infinite? Does friendship can really destroy a unlimited energy power that can create illusion to kill people and dominate the entire world? So many questions unsolved.
► Durability. I can play it over and over again. But if you pick it to finish it once for the story and never play it again, Sonic Forces will be hell of out expensive. The story takes like 3-4 hours. So you better pick this game on sales.
TL;DR.
Sonic Forces is really a good game for my side. It has a long moment since we got a decent modern Sonic game on PC. I've had a great experience. Great ideas, some of them perfectly executed, the others failed. Regarding what you want to do with this game (play it over and over again, or do it once), it can be lacking of durability.
