This game checks off every mediocre mark it possibly could and because of that it's honestly one of the worst Sonic games I've played in a good long time.
Everything about this game feels dull, bland and uninspired. There's so many moments that almost shine through. Moments where I crack a smile. Moments I almost get to enjoy a design aspect before it's taken away. Moments where I almost have fun. Sadly none of these last anywhere near as long as they could.
The gameplay is middling. I didn't exactly hate any of it, but it all felt like it blurred together in the 3 hours it took to beat this game. There's only two stages in the entire game that I remember and one of them had a stage gimmick that only got interesting just before the level ended. I get that most stages are 2 minutes for the sake of padding out the number of total stages the game has, but none of them get a chance to grow and develop as an interesting idea because of it. Every stage is void of character, depth, or any worthwhile design.
The character creator seems very lazy for how much focus it has on the game. No height/weight options, no RGB slider for color, no mixing and matching of tails, ears, hair, or anything else of that nature. Every character you can design ends up being a hollow shell of a design, only slightly brought to life by unlockable clothing items. There just isn't enough there to do anything worthwhile.
The custom character itself is actually enjoyable to play. The variety of weapons you can get are interesting enough to use and the grappling hook is a nice alternative to Modern Sonic's homing attack. Stages where your avatar teams up with Modern Sonic are even better. It's actually amazing how well the two playstyles blend together. You never need to worry about which character is currently "leading". Instead you press whatever feels natural and the game does the rest for you. Need to boost? Press the boost button and Sonic takes the lead. Want to use a Wispon? Tap that trigger and your avatar jumps to the front. It's honestly a huge shame the entire game wasn't this.
Which brings me to the third character, Classic Sonic. I can't for the life of me understand why he's here. The classic physics are still fairly wonky, he feels completely out of place in every stage, and he's basically entirely useless to the plot. There were actually moments playing this game that I forgot Classic Sonic was a part of it. He feels forced in for the sake of catering to the classic fan club, and they're much better off replaying Sonic Mania.
The graphics aren't terrible, but the UI feels a bit intrusive to the screen. The custom characters all look dead and empty. The environments have some detail, but feel lacking compared to the scenery in Generations, Unleashed and even Colors. The lack of enemy variety leads to some boring fights, boss battles are uninteresting at best and re-used from other fights or games at worst.
The plot is abysmal. Most of the game's story seems to be conveyed through talking heads, making any impactful moments or feelings of an actual war going on feel like nothing is happening at all. At one point early on the game even has the nerve to explain a key plot element via a text dump. Not even a single still image to go along with it. Characters are introduced just to leave a few minutes later or have no other role in the game. Cutscenes that feel like they could go somewhere interesting end abruptly or just never end up doing anything.
Overall, the game feels bland and rushed. There's tiny glimmers of hope that poke out just to be put away minutes later. Nothing about the game is outright terrible, but I can't say I can recommend any aspect of it either. Classic fans have the much greater Sonic Mania to play. Modern fans will have more fun replaying Generations/Unleashed/Colors. Even people who want to play this to get that "bad Sonic game" laugh out of the way will get more enjoyment playing Sonic '06, Shadow the Hedgehog, or another poorly viewed Sonic game. There's just nothing here.

I can see where this game works as well as doesn't work for others, although for me it was a fun enough game to play.
The custom avatar is mostly one of the highlights of the game in comparison to several issues, the mass amount of gear to gain is huge and with them being associated with the missions (complete stage with S, use a certain attack in this stage etc) is really fun. The time missions being a challenge but adds more to your game time.
In terms of stages and gameplay, it gets a little iffy. The Avatar stages are some of the best with the many different wispons routes you can take depending on what you have equipped, but you must be careful since some stages are not build for certain wispons, mostly the drill which have lead me to my doom multiple times. The Classic Sonic stages are fun as well, it’s as much as you expect from classic sonic.
But then there's Modern Sonic.
Depending on the stage you will other have a good time, with some QTEs here and there but he has some almost major issues with his controls. Firstly, there are times where some of his attacks and turns are automatic, this can lead up to some huge mistakes and commonly a "try again". Examples being one of the Mystic jungle stages, if you quick step during a turn that you have slight control over, you will find yourself being fling off the edge and to a "Try Again".
Also note the Zavok boss also has an auto jump when he attacks and gives you a chance to homing attack him, if you jump yourself when he attacks it will most likely cancel the homing attack making you go through that boss fight even longer.
Another issue with Sonic is his ability to platform, this is highlighted in an extra stage with pods, the platforms are so high up and far apart that you must make sure you have the highest jump or you will die and Sonic can easily change what you think is the highest jump you can go to a short one leading to your death. That stage is just annoying to begin with and if I remember correctly all you get in completing it is a wispon. There are also issues that Sonic would speed up too quickly during your jumps with would mess up, same in reverse where he is much too slow for the jump and doesn't make it.
Overall, I found it to be a fun game, if you can get by these control issues with Modern then you might find yourself having some fun times. Try it out, if you think it's not worth the current price (40 US - 60 AUD) then keep it in mind when a sale comes up and get it for cheaper.

I absolutely adore this game.
I love strategy games, but often the "best" strategies are artificially hemmed into a game. In Total War games units get a moral hit when being flanked. This isn't a real emergent behavior of the simulation, it's a product of pushing what ought to be the best strategy onto the player.
Factorio is beautiful because there aren't any right or wrong ways to play the game. It simply provides you with pieces and lets the player figure out what to do with them. Every strategy will arise completely organically from the emergent behavior of the game.
People who like math and engineering should all love this game. People who don't like figuring things out for themselves might not like this game, but it's not like you have to be a genius to play Factorio. You build your factory. It's only as complicated as you make it.

This game is about the journey of Amanda Ripley, daughter of Ellen Ripley. It begins fiftenn years after the first alien movie (1979), Amanda is after the flight recorder of the Nostromo to discover what happened to her mother. The story is amazing,  it can last up to 17 hours and it feels like you're inside an alien movie all the time. It is intense, addicting and terrifying.
The game is played in first person. You can craft itens to survive such as noise devices to distract humans, you have a gun in this game and despite being useless against the alien it can be useful against other enemies. There's a suvival mode to see how long you can survive in a map with the alien. You can use vent ducts to move around but beware the monster also uses them, when the time comes and he is on your tail you can hide in lockers, really small lockers, under beds, under the floor and lots of other places which are not completely safe, so expect your heart to pump out of your chest when the beast is starring at your hiding place.
The alien's A.I. is almost as terrifying as he is, it'll make you frustrated. The alien will respond to noises from shots to footsteps, so be careful and only use loud gadgets when there's no other choice.
It is afraid of fire, so molotovs and the flametrower can be useful. It can also be distracted with flares, so be careful when you use them in the dark.
It is incredible how they manage to make all the assets so similar to the ones in the movie, the spaceship design, the door mechanism, the clothes, the toys, for the alien movie lovers like me this was amazing. The performance is great, it works perfectly with no stutter or any immersion breaking problem at the highest settings, my pc specs are below.
Processor: Core I7 2600k
RAM: 16GB
Motherboard: Asus Maximus IV
Graphics Card: GTX 970
Not only the visuals, but the audio is also loyal to the movies. The alien's footsteps approaching, the voice acting, the eletronic devices, the door opening sounds, the amazing orchestra that scares you more than the alien, all this coming together to deliver one of the best horror games you have ever played.

Someone bought me this during the steam sale. I gave it an honest try, but I've got to say... It's not really that fun. At first there was a serious "Boarding USG Ishimura" vibe, but then it turns into a brutally punishing stealth game.
I mean, I get that the alien is invulnerable, even if I disagree with that, but the humans and robots are not... But there's not enough ammo and gadgets to fight them, not even if you're very clever, and there's no Metal Gear-style way to assassinate them if you sneak up into melee range undetected. You'll resort to making hit-and-run melee strikes on the robot's backs, hitting them twice quickly with a giant hammer that feels like lovetapping them with a nerf sword, then running to hide in a vent for four minutes to make them go back to their derping-around post, only to do it again, and again, and again. NOT fun, NOT entertaining. I found myself looking for cheats to give myself ammo and gadget-making stuff so I could just have a FAIR FIGHT, and then said "why am I bothering? I don't even like this franchise."
And of course, the moment ANY enemy sees you, all of their mates know exactly where you are: justified for the robots (radio,) but not for humans.
In short: It could have been a fun action-horror game with one BIG BAD that you always had to run/hide from, but instead it's just not fun, because every enemy is basically overpowering and there's no stealth takedowns, it is not. Go play Metal Gear Solid V if you want tactical stealth action, go play Dead Space 2 if you want action horror on a giant eff-off space station.
[edit]Post-Completion addendum.
I don't know why I did this to myself. I really do not.
Anyway, with enough modding, Alien Isolation becomes playable; primarily this entails allowing firearms to damage the Xenomorph (Mr. Happy as I had taken to calling him,) which drives him off, greatly increasing the amount of all finished goods and ammunition you can carry, modifying the flamethrower so it eats fuel half as fast, and modifying the item construction recipes so that they also give you some ammo when used.
And after enough modding, the game became... Playable. With a satisfactory quantity of firearms and firearm accessories (bullets,) fighting against hostile humans and androids became fun, but Mr. Happy became more... Well, chasing him off wasn't hard, but he was always present, necessitating frequent hide-tanning, and any one screw-up on my part led to instant death. As it should be, I guess, if that's how you like your games.
Anyway, I suffered through the whole slog to the end, to find out that they... Basically copied the ending of the first Dead Space. SPOILERS BELOW THIS POINT: YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!
Basically? Everybody dies. EVERYBODY dies. Ripley gets captured by an alien at one point, in a thoroughly BS encounter (seriously, who in god's name puts a GIANT AIR DUCT in an AIRLOCK,) leaving it an open question whether or not she got implanted while she was unconscious. Meanwhile, the station went to hell, and you escape on the ship you got in on, only for a xenomorph to have somehow boarded it. You would have thought that an alium wouldn't have been able to board a ship in space without causing a huge noticeable hull breach, but no. Ripley survives by blowing herself out an airlock yet again, leaving her floating in space alone, and then a flash  oflight and sci-fi woo-woo sound implies that someone showed up as she was losing consciousness. Credits roll.
Expect Alien Isolation 2 to take place aboard an improbably huge mining vessel with a psych ward in which Amanda is trapped, as everything is going to hell in a handbasket.

I have mixed feelings about this game.
On the one hand, we have the technical aspects, which are positive:
- the game is very (I mean VERY) well optimized, runs butter smooth in ultra on my 4 year rig (i5-2320, GTX 750, 8GB RAM etc.)
- the design is very nice, a clear continuation of the original Alien movie (everything looks like designed in the 80s)
Gameplay-wise, there are some strong points too:
- atmosphere is top notch, the space station is scary enough without feeling cheap
- the crafting system and the tools are a nice touch
- the sounds are good, everything creaks, beeps, things go bump in the night etc.
- I was scared sh|tless playing hide and seek with the alien (for a while that is)
But then there were some aspects of the game which totally broke immersion for me, and were annoying as hell.
- People having no problem "accidentally" running into you in a very large hall, no matter what; yet not noticing you when you literally are an arms length away. This is no joke: in Mission 3 I was crouching in the corner just beside the door and a guy entering the same door walked by me twice like a blind bat.
- The Alien wandering "accidentally" always in your vicinity in the missions you have to evade it. It has the whole hospital floor for itself, yet you always have to hide in lockers and hold your breath. It's like the alien can't see you, can't hear you, can't smell you from a distance, yet is drawn to you somehow. This made the hide and seek a trial and error for me, and poof, the suspence and terror was gone after a while.
I had the feeling that a lot of encounters were scripted to a point where the question was not "How can I solve this?" but "How do the developers want me to solve this?".
I gave the game thumbs down, but that doesn't necessarily mean that this is a bad game. If you're not bothered by the negative aspects I mentioned, then you should definitely try it. Especially while on sale (that's how I got it anyway).

Large sections of the game are designed well, the visuals, the sounds, and the characters are all very well done. But its the alien that actually breaks gameplay. Instant-fail stealth mechanics vs an alien that you can't hurt, and have scarce resources to even distract, is just not fun. Maybe its good survivial horror, but its clearly not for me.
Finally an Alien game done right!  Perfect mix between suspense, stealth, and action.  Just watch out for those hallways, they are OP! :D

Supergiant Games have done it again.  Transistor follows in the footsteps of Bastion with its beautifully painted backgrounds, excellent voice acting, and fun gameplay.  The story is very well done, revealing only what's absolutely necessary and leaving the rest up to the imagination of the player.  Darren Korb has grown musically since Bastion and it shows (or should I say sounds?) in the superb soundtrack (my favorite track is Signals).  You should absolutely buy this game.
Art nouveau cyber punk - nuff said :)

This is a short game, much shorter than Bastion.  (Finished in 10h, a casual play through could probably be 8.) It is absolutely worth every penny, but be ready to be left with this powerful, empty feeling when you're done.  I understand that they were probably aiming for ending the game while you still wanted more instead of dragging out an ending, but the gameplay is so engaging that they could've doubled the number of encounters and still had replayability left over for days.
Storywise... ouch. They somehow learned ways to improve on the Bastion experience. At times the monologue is a little overwrought, and you're left with a ton of unanswered questions (I'm reminded of what watching LOST was like, sadly in a bad way) by the end.  I'm hoping to get more out of their New Game+ option. We'll see.
Totally solid title, though, would seriously recommend that anyone who enjoyed Bastion or loves really good story pick this up.

Rome 2 - Emperor Edition..
Short Intro:
Well unfortunately for me I'm giving this title, a negative review with some positive points.
Like other Rome Total War loyal addicted fans (I did play 80+hours, finished 5 full campaigns including Rome twice, and played all the DLC's of the first game) I was very excited to get my hands on this game.
I waited 2 months to pick this game on a 75% sale (Obviously or else I don't think this game worth the price)  but finally after installing .. I came across a different gameplay than I expected.
1) Let's begin with the DLC's cuz I see they are a big part of some negative reviews that I've seen.
(-) They are overpriced? Yes
(-) They could easily be in the game without buying them? Yes
(-) The main problem with the DLC's that some of them are overpriced and some of them don't even need to be included as a DLC.
(+) The only positive side that I can find is that mainly the campaign packs are worthy to buy, mabye on a discount.
2) Graphics:
(+) Graphic wise the game is beautiful as it is and very well optimized, I'm not expecting anything particular from a RTS game.
3) What broke me and made me feel.. Disappointment and confused is the campaign itself, a factor that I don't see in many negative ( or positive ) reviews.
The Campaign :
(+) They added so many new stuff in the campaign and expanded the older things.
(+) Diplomacy - I enjoyed it because it's more organized with more options and more spacious.
(+) Factions - Added more factions which is great !! More enemies? I love it.
(+) Military - New units, better looking units , different type of fighting and defending stances to control your army and use it the best you can.
(+) Map - Obviously the map is bigger which it should be, more provinces etc very nice.
(+) Naval Army - You actually fight with the fleets? Laying siege through the sea? Hell yeah.
(+) Battles - Don't have so much to say as I quitted the game before playing many battles but from what I've seen it shouldn't worry anybody. (P.S the ambush battles are perfect)
Now as you walk towards the hill, you suddenly take a huge fall..
(-) Overall stats and layout - I feel like they invested so much into the game, adding or editing stuff that I had no idea what to do with all that information. I literally found myself spending a hour or two just trying to understand the gameplay of the campaign.
(-) Technology Trees - I like this idea, it should've been in the first game but again it's just too much for me to handle.. I didn't know which tree should I pick and what are the consequences of the choices that I will do with those trees.
(-) Faction Layout - What The Hell. What happend to the family tree? How do I know which family members are mine and which are my ally's ? I like the records subject
(-) Unit Stats - I prefer the first game unit stats, which gave us simply the AT. and Def. points, and their skills.
(-) General and Agent Stats - Cunning, Authority and Zeal - Bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. It's complicated personally I don't find it attractive and it just makes me "think more" rather than "enjoy the game and play fluently".
(-) Settlement Stats - Also a big difference between this and the older settlement info page in Rome1.
I had good time understanding and reading the info of the settlements in Rome1 (public order,wealth,trade etc)
Now what they did is add new stats and traits to the buildings, so it all got mixed and for me it's pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to read and again try to understand, what the hell am I doing.
Short Summary -
I was one of the people who fell down trying to play this game. It gave me a headache. Trying to read all the new stuff, and understand it and even if I do, I'm not sure what I do or how I do.
It was too much for me, mabye it is.. Mabye it's just me.. Mabye I got used to the first game..
I did play only 4 hours but I wanted to quit because I felt I can't continue to play this game and even if I did.. I just couldn't find all the fun the first game gave me.
Do I recommend this game? Sure if you're a classic RTS fan especially Rome Total War's fan. But don't get your hopes so high.
Do I think you will enjoy it? Depends. I guess it will be up to you.
Is it better than the first game? Personally I don't think it is, in terms of enjoyment.
That's why, I think it's best to pick this game in a big sale (75% discount or more ) I bought it for 15 bucks.
Do not buy any DLC before trying the main game first.
Will I play it again in the future? Perhaps, mabye with a more open-minded head. Mabye when I get more free time to spend on this game, and also start with Short Campaign Mod (which should've been in the game in the first place).
Again I write this review on my point of view.
Thanks for reading my review it was really important for me to write it.

Having invested 117 hours according to Steam, Dark Souls 2 is, to be sincerely honest, one of the most precious, rare gem I have ever played since I started entering the gaming scene of the '90s SNES era (5 or six years old)! Character customization is deep, allowing a full physical customization to those who are into it. Take it at face value--Dark Souls 2 is amazingly hard to master. Literally any enemy you encounter is a viable threat as each hit sustained can withdraw a decent to horrendous amount of HP, and trust me that I say your character, whatever the chosen class, will need to increase HP as progress is made. Not only that, but factor in other important attributes like Endurance, Adaptability, Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith, and a lot more you will need to manage your Souls well.
Laid-back answer: each monster you successfully slay grants you the monster's souls; you spend them leveling up your attributes and/or buying, enchanting, and repairing weapons/armor. Merchants sell items  which you buy with souls. When you die, you lose all your souls. Fortunately you can run back to the spot you died and retrieve them. Unfortunately if you die a second time before collecting your dropped souls, they are gone forever... dun, Dun, DUN! Basically, view souls as currency and in this type of game it is the true design of risk and reward.

In addition to carefully managing souls, I cannot stress how important stamina plays a gigantic role. To simply put it, each swing of a sword, club, spear, staff, and shield blocks getting pounded and dodging reduces stamina. Less stamina equates to less actions, but this also applies for your opponent as well. You will not know how much stamina an enemy has, only its HP is displayed, but you will know by the actions performed; monster swings in a 180 degree arc three times means its stamina is completely depleted, and now is your perfect opening to unleash hell. Monster takes a swing or two means it still has stamina so be cautious. Light or strong animation, observe the differences and approach appropiately. The action is nothing like God of War or Devil May Cry!
The gear loadout is pretty brilliant. Each armor/weapon has its own stats and you can strengthen them with many diverse enchantments.
Exploration is like a grade school field trip. Different routes can be traveled and you are not limited to a set destination. Having trouble with a particular area or boss? Work on another map and come back. Even some bosses can be optional by traveling a different path. Check every inch of the environment! There are a plethora of hidden secrets, rooms, and treasure. You will know by reading the messages placed by other helpful, or troll, players.
Bosses can always be dueled by co-op with other players. A total of three, including you, can co-op bosses or even just the trash monsters. Want offline mode? NPCs can be summoned. Even you can be summoned to aid if you engrave your re-useable summoning sign called the Soapstone.
Not for casuals, but if you are one I guarantee you will want to punch pregnant puppy over and over in sync with how many times you die. Do not give up! Persevere!

After playing Sonic Forces for over 160+ hours, I think it's time I write a review.
The story is very plain, weak, and overall boring. 80% Of the games dialogue is through dialogue boxes, which gets irritating after a while. It was perfect for the levels but seriously the WORLD MAP? all that dialogue put into the world map would've been better for cutscenes. In the first couple of cutscenes it's been shown that Tails has gone insane, but what we've seen Tails is perfectly fine. Sonic is apparently killed during the fight but instead of the player finding that out on their own, the games dialogue box states Sonic is alive. Of course Sonic would be alive but why reveal it so early? Sonic, who was tortured by Eggman seems to be perfectly fine and cocky like always, Six months of torture would've done at least SOME damage to Sonic.
Where did that perfect jump from Generations go? Sonic, Classic Sonic, and your Custom Hero all feel sluggish when it comes to running and jumping. Playing as the Custom Hero you can be slowly walking/jogging to going at an alarming speed rate *Space Port does this a lot*  All the characters feel heavier but the one who was effected the most was Classic Sonic. In some areas of Chemical Plant Zone you can be going at a nice fast rate and then roll into a ball, to then get instantly flung down into the ground wondering what the hell just happened.
From so many reviews and fans, we can all agree the levels in this game are pretty short, although what do you expect from the boost. Unleashed, Colors, and Generations all had pretty short levels. But that doesn't compare to the design, Sonic Forces has some of the WEAKEST level designs in Sonic history, even though I should cut them some slack for being 3 newbie's.
A lot of this game is automatic, you can just put the controller down and go get a drink or use the bathroom or something like that, about 7-12 levels in this game are over automatic, which isn't good for someone who actually wants to control the character.
Ah yes, we really wanted Green Hill, Chemical Plant, and Death Egg back, we've already had stages from Sonic 1,2, and 3&K return in Sonic Mania. Wasn't that enough? Nope, let's just keep going with reused stages and ignore original stages like Casino Forest!
or Metropolis!
Why only bring Shadow back as a playable character? He's basically the same as Sonic, why not Knuckles, Silver, Tails, even f*cking Vector.
Now that I'm done with the Negatives, it's time to go onto the Positives
The world has been taken over by Dr. Eggman and Sonic is trying to take it back with Classic, Rookie *OC* and the rest of his friends, along the way they keep getting stopped by past villains such as Zavok, Shadow *kinda* Chaos *also kinda* Metal Sonic, and a new villain known as Infinite who is more powerful and faster than Sonic. Unlike the past Sonic titles this one was the most darkest. This game makes you take Dr. Eggman more seriously and makes you think what the hell did Eggman unleash.

The music is a step up from any other Sonic title, all the music is original even for the reused stages which is honestly surprising. Classic Sonic has the Genesis style soundfont but fails it horribly but still pretty catchy, Modern Sonic has the.. Well you know the regular Modern Sonic music we've been hearing since Unleashed nothing new to it, and finally the Custom Hero has the Adventure style music with lyrics, but also takes some style from 2016/17 and mixes the whole song up, very very catchy.
Your own oc in a Sonic game, make em' ugly, make em' pretty, it's your choice they'll show up in the dialogue boxes, cutscenes, etc. It's one of the best parts in the game in my opinion.
After Unleashed there were no Sonic games that kept credit to their respective character. But Forces stepped up and did it, Sonic feels like Sonic, Tails feels like Tails, Knuckles feels like Knuckles, it's honestly great to not see them as the idiots they were in the short lived Boom spinoffs.
We may not be able to play as Silver, Vector, Espio, Omega, Rouge, etc. But it is good to see them since we've only seen them in Generations and that was it, feels refreshing to not just see Knuckles, Amy, or Tails again.

This game is about the journey of Amanda Ripley, daughter of Ellen Ripley. It begins fiftenn years after the first alien movie (1979), Amanda is after the flight recorder of the Nostromo to discover what happened to her mother. The story is amazing,  it can last up to 17 hours and it feels like you're inside an alien movie all the time. It is intense, addicting and terrifying.
The game is played in first person. You can craft itens to survive such as noise devices to distract humans, you have a gun in this game and despite being useless against the alien it can be useful against other enemies. There's a suvival mode to see how long you can survive in a map with the alien. You can use vent ducts to move around but beware the monster also uses them, when the time comes and he is on your tail you can hide in lockers, really small lockers, under beds, under the floor and lots of other places which are not completely safe, so expect your heart to pump out of your chest when the beast is starring at your hiding place.
The alien's A.I. is almost as terrifying as he is, it'll make you frustrated. The alien will respond to noises from shots to footsteps, so be careful and only use loud gadgets when there's no other choice.
It is afraid of fire, so molotovs and the flametrower can be useful. It can also be distracted with flares, so be careful when you use them in the dark.
It is incredible how they manage to make all the assets so similar to the ones in the movie, the spaceship design, the door mechanism, the clothes, the toys, for the alien movie lovers like me this was amazing. The performance is great, it works perfectly with no stutter or any immersion breaking problem at the highest settings, my pc specs are below.
Processor: Core I7 2600k
RAM: 16GB
Motherboard: Asus Maximus IV
Graphics Card: GTX 970
Not only the visuals, but the audio is also loyal to the movies. The alien's footsteps approaching, the voice acting, the eletronic devices, the door opening sounds, the amazing orchestra that scares you more than the alien, all this coming together to deliver one of the best horror games you have ever played.

Someone bought me this during the steam sale. I gave it an honest try, but I've got to say... It's not really that fun. At first there was a serious "Boarding USG Ishimura" vibe, but then it turns into a brutally punishing stealth game.
I mean, I get that the alien is invulnerable, even if I disagree with that, but the humans and robots are not... But there's not enough ammo and gadgets to fight them, not even if you're very clever, and there's no Metal Gear-style way to assassinate them if you sneak up into melee range undetected. You'll resort to making hit-and-run melee strikes on the robot's backs, hitting them twice quickly with a giant hammer that feels like lovetapping them with a nerf sword, then running to hide in a vent for four minutes to make them go back to their derping-around post, only to do it again, and again, and again. NOT fun, NOT entertaining. I found myself looking for cheats to give myself ammo and gadget-making stuff so I could just have a FAIR FIGHT, and then said "why am I bothering? I don't even like this franchise."
And of course, the moment ANY enemy sees you, all of their mates know exactly where you are: justified for the robots (radio,) but not for humans.
In short: It could have been a fun action-horror game with one BIG BAD that you always had to run/hide from, but instead it's just not fun, because every enemy is basically overpowering and there's no stealth takedowns, it is not. Go play Metal Gear Solid V if you want tactical stealth action, go play Dead Space 2 if you want action horror on a giant eff-off space station.
[edit]Post-Completion addendum.
I don't know why I did this to myself. I really do not.
Anyway, with enough modding, Alien Isolation becomes playable; primarily this entails allowing firearms to damage the Xenomorph (Mr. Happy as I had taken to calling him,) which drives him off, greatly increasing the amount of all finished goods and ammunition you can carry, modifying the flamethrower so it eats fuel half as fast, and modifying the item construction recipes so that they also give you some ammo when used.
And after enough modding, the game became... Playable. With a satisfactory quantity of firearms and firearm accessories (bullets,) fighting against hostile humans and androids became fun, but Mr. Happy became more... Well, chasing him off wasn't hard, but he was always present, necessitating frequent hide-tanning, and any one screw-up on my part led to instant death. As it should be, I guess, if that's how you like your games.
Anyway, I suffered through the whole slog to the end, to find out that they... Basically copied the ending of the first Dead Space. SPOILERS BELOW THIS POINT: YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!
Basically? Everybody dies. EVERYBODY dies. Ripley gets captured by an alien at one point, in a thoroughly BS encounter (seriously, who in god's name puts a GIANT AIR DUCT in an AIRLOCK,) leaving it an open question whether or not she got implanted while she was unconscious. Meanwhile, the station went to hell, and you escape on the ship you got in on, only for a xenomorph to have somehow boarded it. You would have thought that an alium wouldn't have been able to board a ship in space without causing a huge noticeable hull breach, but no. Ripley survives by blowing herself out an airlock yet again, leaving her floating in space alone, and then a flash  oflight and sci-fi woo-woo sound implies that someone showed up as she was losing consciousness. Credits roll.
Expect Alien Isolation 2 to take place aboard an improbably huge mining vessel with a psych ward in which Amanda is trapped, as everything is going to hell in a handbasket.

I have mixed feelings about this game.
On the one hand, we have the technical aspects, which are positive:
- the game is very (I mean VERY) well optimized, runs butter smooth in ultra on my 4 year rig (i5-2320, GTX 750, 8GB RAM etc.)
- the design is very nice, a clear continuation of the original Alien movie (everything looks like designed in the 80s)
Gameplay-wise, there are some strong points too:
- atmosphere is top notch, the space station is scary enough without feeling cheap
- the crafting system and the tools are a nice touch
- the sounds are good, everything creaks, beeps, things go bump in the night etc.
- I was scared sh|tless playing hide and seek with the alien (for a while that is)
But then there were some aspects of the game which totally broke immersion for me, and were annoying as hell.
- People having no problem "accidentally" running into you in a very large hall, no matter what; yet not noticing you when you literally are an arms length away. This is no joke: in Mission 3 I was crouching in the corner just beside the door and a guy entering the same door walked by me twice like a blind bat.
- The Alien wandering "accidentally" always in your vicinity in the missions you have to evade it. It has the whole hospital floor for itself, yet you always have to hide in lockers and hold your breath. It's like the alien can't see you, can't hear you, can't smell you from a distance, yet is drawn to you somehow. This made the hide and seek a trial and error for me, and poof, the suspence and terror was gone after a while.
I had the feeling that a lot of encounters were scripted to a point where the question was not "How can I solve this?" but "How do the developers want me to solve this?".
I gave the game thumbs down, but that doesn't necessarily mean that this is a bad game. If you're not bothered by the negative aspects I mentioned, then you should definitely try it. Especially while on sale (that's how I got it anyway).

Large sections of the game are designed well, the visuals, the sounds, and the characters are all very well done. But its the alien that actually breaks gameplay. Instant-fail stealth mechanics vs an alien that you can't hurt, and have scarce resources to even distract, is just not fun. Maybe its good survivial horror, but its clearly not for me.
Finally an Alien game done right!  Perfect mix between suspense, stealth, and action.  Just watch out for those hallways, they are OP! :D

I really enjoyed playing Factorio, and will most likely continue to play it for some time. In general, sandbox games and other types that require you to be really creative haven’t been the most fun for me, including even Minecraft, but I seem to really enjoy the more complex and challenging types. Infinifactory is another one that I enjoyed a lot, and even though it was more a puzzle game than sandbox, it still involved creating well optimized factories and conveyor belts.
While the game is very fun and can easily last me hundreds of hours, it just feels like there’s untapped potential. This is mainly because there are no goals, except to just constantly refine how you create a factory. It even feels like an RTS at times, since there are enemies and you can make a variety of military items, but combat isn’t complex at all. While the base game wouldn’t really work, it would be nice to see a modified game mode where multiple players/AI build a base/factory more focused on combat stuff, and it plays out like an RTS would normally.

S.T.A.L.K.E.R - Fantastically broken.
IF YOU ONLY LIKE LINEAR/COHERENT GAMES IGNORE THIS REVIEW
S.T.A.L.K.E.R Shadow of Chernobyl is an openworld FPS-RPG very loosely based off the book Roadside Picnic by Boris and Arkady Strugatsky (good book). It tells the story of a stalker with amnesia dubbed the Nameless One on a quest to find a man known as Strelok.
I first played S.T.A.L.K.E.R in 2010. I was at a tip shop, saw a copy for 1 dollar and bought it.
I'm sad to say that I COMPLETELY missed the point of the game and hated it. I found it sluggish, bland, weird and too hard. A few years later I saw it on sale here and thought why the hell not, I'll give it a spin for five bucks, and absolutely adored it. This game still looks really good for 2007, definately better that -ugh- Fallout 3 due to its high-res textures and impressive draw distance.
THE GOOD
The randomness of the world is something praised and criticised simultaneously, but I tend to see it as a part of the appeal of this game as it lets you feel like your engagement, achievement and path are forged by you. There is a path to an objective but the path is filled with other interaction, not just Fallout 4-style fetchquests and pop-pop gun battles, though those are sadly common in sidequests. The NPCs interact with each other in interesting ways such as playing guitar at campfires, banter and passing vodka back and forth, and some of my fondest moments in S.T.A.L.K.E.R have been spent cowering around a campfire in the pitch-black night listening to mutants howl and distant gunfire from bandits. It's fantastic when stuff like this happens, and because of its random nature these times feel priceless.
THE BAD
Hoo boy, the bad. You might be surprised to hear this after my bloated paragraph of praise but holy sh!t is this game lackluster. The radiation of Chernobyl seems to have completely altered time and space in the exclusion zone because enemies while living or dead will fly into space or sink through the floor. At one point a soldier fell through the ground while alive and as I tried to see where he had gone he shot out, catapulting me into the sky, where I promptly fell to my death. Due to sh!t like this and the crushing higher difficulties S.T.A.L.K.E.R's most important key is F5. A good example of this is when you have to cross under the broken bridge to get to Garbage, and a crowd of soldiers are in your way. This section literally requires you to quicksave after every kill, as do most fights throughout the game. The more difficult mutants like
hand your♥♥♥♥♥to you on a silver platter early on, and bandits can turn shotguns into Dragunovs for no clear reason.
TL;DR
This game is REALLY GOOD, but is plagued with issues that bring down what could be an almost perfect horror/action FPS-RPG. If you can stand some issues at the beginning and like challenging games by all means buy it, but if those issues sound unbearable to you give it a miss.

Supergiant Games have done it again.  Transistor follows in the footsteps of Bastion with its beautifully painted backgrounds, excellent voice acting, and fun gameplay.  The story is very well done, revealing only what's absolutely necessary and leaving the rest up to the imagination of the player.  Darren Korb has grown musically since Bastion and it shows (or should I say sounds?) in the superb soundtrack (my favorite track is Signals).  You should absolutely buy this game.

This is a short game, much shorter than Bastion.  (Finished in 10h, a casual play through could probably be 8.) It is absolutely worth every penny, but be ready to be left with this powerful, empty feeling when you're done.  I understand that they were probably aiming for ending the game while you still wanted more instead of dragging out an ending, but the gameplay is so engaging that they could've doubled the number of encounters and still had replayability left over for days.
Storywise... ouch. They somehow learned ways to improve on the Bastion experience. At times the monologue is a little overwrought, and you're left with a ton of unanswered questions (I'm reminded of what watching LOST was like, sadly in a bad way) by the end.  I'm hoping to get more out of their New Game+ option. We'll see.
Totally solid title, though, would seriously recommend that anyone who enjoyed Bastion or loves really good story pick this up.

Being a bit of a wild west enthusiast, I've had my eye on this game for some time.  The thought of playing in one of my favorite settings, and interacting with some of the west's most polarizing figures, was to tempting to pass up.  And this game doesn't disappoint.  The gunplay is obviously a lot of fun, but the ultimate question was, how will the story hold up?
The story is absolutly amazing, you play the fictitious bounty hunter Silas Greeves, impressively, the game does a manificent job of weaving Silas's story into true events, effictively blending the facts with the myths and legends of the wests most amazing stories and gun fights.  Your story begins in Abileen, Kansas when an aged Silas enters a saloon much to the amazement of the patrons.  He's immediately beset by requests for stories on his journies throughout the west.  He starts from the beggining, when he rode with Billy the kid.  I don't want to give any spoilers on Silas's story, but you'll be impressed with all the facts contained in these stories.  You'll hear plenty of referenes to the famed Lincoln county war,  you'll bear witness to kid's capture by none other than controversial lawman Pat Garrett himself, and you'll witness the kid's legendary jail break in which he guns down James Bell and Robert Ollinger, both represented in the game.  It even references Ollingers well known 10 guage, double barrel shotgun, widely feared by many.  You'll learn a lot about the history of these figures, through the story, and collectible secrets that unlock facts about events and characters throughout the story that are known to be true.
You'll encounter so many of the wests most amazing gunfighters and stories, if your a wild west enthusiast, this is a no brainer, buy this game.  If your curious about the west and want to experience it through an action packed game, while learning about some of the hard individuals that lived through this era, buy this game.  If you enjoy a solid FPS with a great story, buy this game.  I can't say enough about how great this game is, I've yet to beat it, but for 15 dollars this game is a steal, and if you pre-ordered and received Bound in blood, it's just an amazing deal.  So what are you waiting for?  You can thank me later.

Very simple. Repetitive, but that's part of the intended experience. This game has a lot of social commentary interwoven in with it. You play as a border crossing checkpoint officer. As the game progresses you struggle to make ends meet and support your family and you get caught up in the politics of the nations and soon you find yourself questioning your own loyalty.  Simple but well done.

One poor immigration officer's decisions can make all the difference in the world. This game divides one's loyalties and moral convictions through heart-pounding decisions, all while putting on pressure to not dally too long. The humor and inventiveness in "Papers, Please" makes it a classic thriller in decision-based games.
Don't be fooled! This isn't any ordinary retro-style game!  Honestly, even the music and sound-effects are impressive. It is original, well-executed, and will leave an impression on you. You will not regret trying it.

Challenging, yet rewarding gameplay.  DO NOT expect this game to hold your hand.  You will learn by dying... a lot.  And when you finally don't die you will jump around your living room, fist pumping the air in excitement.  Do not buy this game if you are the type to throw your controller across the room in frustration, because it will happen frequently.
You will quickly discover that the strength of all weapons is pretty balanced.  Almost every weapon in the game can be used end game, you just have to optimize your stats for the weapon you want, learn its move-set, and play to its strengths.  The "stronger" weapons are the ones with the simpler movesets that don't have much of a learning curve and a more even speed to strength ratio.
Graphically, the textures on this game are beautiful.  At high resolution the environmental and character details are astounding, but they still look a little flat since most of the detail comes from surface maps.  Expect PS3 level graphics, albeit at a higher resolution.
PVP is fun with experience, but frustrating as you're learning the game.  Players can invade you anywhere, at any time, and can ruin your day if they catch you while you're already struggling with the PVE content.  Play offline if you don't want to get ganked.  Join a covenant with an arena early to get some practice in to even the playing field.
If you like this game, I highly suggest the DLCs, as they are some of the best content in the game.

Nothing here that made RO great. A poor "reinvention" and an even poorer gaming experience.
1) No Cards. There's 0 reason to revisit low level mobs.
2) No WoE. Perhaps this will be installed later though.
3) No trading, Chatrooms, or Vend. (Ergo. Little reason to socialize with anyone ever)
4) No open world. Extremely linear.
5) Poor stat Incentives. Most people pick up STR or INT.
This game offers nothing that other MMOs offer despite being spritish. It runs off of RO nostalgia and the gameplay isn't that fun. I tried my best to enjoy this game but when you have lag on top of the already lackluster gameplay it's more of a chore than fun. I have no reason to grind out mobs. I don't have goals like I did in RO.
RO you wanted to grind mobs to get a 20% damage to water, monster card. Took that card and put it on top of a size % card and then you grinded out thara frogs so you can get that card to sell.... etc etc. Virtually every mob was useful to grind or map was fun to revisit. The Grind was heavier... but along the way you could socialize with people.
In TOS, you literally level and dump. I have like 7 people in my friends list who I never see again because we also level at different times. We have no reason to talk. There is no real open world, no true exploration, and the magic that was RO is gone. You don't have fun choices. RO you could run full INT sniper and be completely viable with some nutty build you invented. Stack some weird cards, have 30 different equips, etc. In TOS, you can't do that,  you have more choices but at the same time... you have less options. There are some skills that are straight up useless.
Is it horrible? No. It's somewhat fun at times and you are motivated to level. But besides that... It's missing out on EVERYTHING else. Crafting, market, trade, and partying is utter garbage. They implemented a "local" party system. But most times you don't have any real reason to party with people besides grinding up. In the days of old RO you partied up to take down MvP bosses, do WoE, or some other fun stuff. You talked about♥♥♥♥♥♥while waiting for MVPs, made chat rooms etc.
All that being said... Is it RO and should it be judged by that measure? No... Its it's own game and has it's own merits. But let's be honest. MOST of us are here because it's related to RO. And if you're here for that reason, turn back and wait for them to fix everything before trying it out. I have 65 hours on this game and have been EAGERLY waiting years for this. Very dissapointed. But... Hope for the future...
Hope my friends... Hope.

Cheers and good luck.
***Just After Early Release***
I keep seeing people say, "Because it's early access... blah blah blah... give it a chance"
It is not early access, it is Exclusive access! meaning that the game is supposed to be completed, this isn't considered a beta nor should it.
Now that that is out of the way, I do recommend this game. Now that may seem♥♥♥♥♥backwards however the game ITSELF is good. IMC is definitely not handling themselves in a professional manor though and thus it's very much disrespecting the players who have been/are supporting them.
I do have high hope for this game, it was very nice to finally get into a game where it felt that I was customizing my character to the way I wanted to. [stats, specs, etc excluding cosmetic]
I am reminded of ragnarok which many people have come here because of that classic. However I also am a vet maplestory player [vanilla I'd like to say] and I find it also brings many aspects in which I look for in a game.
They are limiting the game in many ways, with trading, overpriced monthly premiums, market holds [holding your money for 48 hours after you sell an item on top of if you're a free player they take 30% of it on top! of the fee for putting the item up].
For right now, I do recommend it. I do hope they actually listen to the community, we are the ones who will be supporting IMC.
My personal request is, be transparent!!!! Don't let a known game breaking bug go for over 24 hours before posting about it. If you're working on it, then take the consideration to allow us to know that that is just what you are doing.
It would ease the mood of the players who are left in the dark with the frustrations of what would seem a lacking or caring company.
TL:DR - The game is great, overall the game itself is amazing and holds true to many aspects people come to play it. However IMC feels like a brand new company in my eyes. Not showing transparency and allowing things to blow way out of proportions.
Will come back to review in a couple weeks after IMC attempts more. As of right now, they are screwing over all players.

Excellent game and really the ONLY quality hunting simulator out there on the net.
Don't let other reviewers fool you, it IS free to play, at least to get your appetite whetted. You can hunt Mule Deer and Rabbits originally, though you only start with a gun permitted for rabbits. But for $9.99 every 3 months to unlock every species, and the fact that usually you only need one type of rifle to hunt just about everything (one of the three Anschutz rifles) the game is a great way to get some hunting "experience" when you either can't get out there, or don't want to go through the hassle.
There are plenty of bugs and other glitches in the game, though far less than anticipated. Animal AI has improved drastically as of late, and you really have to think like a hunter to take down those trophy bucks. They react strongly to scent, and many have great eyesight. This in turn means you have to capitalize on nearby cover, and make sure you are reading the wind properly. Misuse of both cover and wind means never getting that buck or other trophy within range to take them out.
The community for the game are VERY helpful, most veteran hunters (myself included) are more than willing to take newbies out for hunts and show them what to do to get consistant results. The game itself is cheap to get into, unless you WANT to spend the money on all the weapons and gadgets, no more than $50 will get you set up for pretty much anything, and the $10 every three months will keep your membership active which means you won't have to be spending for liscences every 7 to 30 days.

Transistor is short, beautiful and coupled with an AMAZING soundtrack.
The game to end, without finishing every little detail, is about 5 hours long.
Gameplay is really dynamic and fun; every ability you unlock can instead be used as an upgrade for other abilities or as a passive buff to the protagonist.

Transistor is depressing. One of its central themes is hopelessness. The world is dying, and there's nothing you can do to stop it. Your best friend and the love of your life is dead, his soul trapped in a giant futuristic greatsword, and there's nothing you can do to save him. You can try to talk to the outside world, to survivors, through terminals scattered throughout the city, but no one reads your messages or listens to what you have to say. You can vote on what you want the sky to look like, what you want the weather to be, but your vote is only one amongst thousands.
Despite this air of soul-crushing hopelessness, or indeed perhaps because of it, Transistor turns into a very touching and heartwarming story about perseverence and determination. You play as Red, a body without a voice, and you wield the Transistor, a voice without a body. Your job is to save the city, rescue your lover, and defeat the evil organization responsible for all this.
Or at least that's how it all starts out. The story evolves very naturally into something far greater. It's given to you in very small pieces and it can be incredibly intimidating. Where Bastion's story was very simple (Fantasy World -> War -> Calamity -> You), Transistor's is a ridiculously layered cyberpunk adventure. Luckily though, the pieces are very easy and intuitive to piece together, unlike say Hard Reset or EYE: Divine Cybermancy levels of lunacy. Transistor's story is also much more personal and emotional than Bastion's, though unlike in Bastion, there was no point in Transistor's story that filled me with impotent rage or choked me up and brought me to tears. Transistor is so much more subtle than that.
The combat is interesting. Red can routinely switch between traditional isometric diablo-style ARPG combat, or activate a turn-based mode in which she wails maddingly on the targets of your choice and then cannot re-enter combat until her turn bar has replenished. A wide variety of skills are presented, but there are only four active slots for them. On top of this, the Teleport skill is the only one that can be used while your Turn Meter is recharging, so one of your choices will always be delegated to it, and another slot will always be given to one of the two quick-recharging autoattack-style skills, so the actual ability customization is further limited.
The upgrade and passive system however suffers from not being limited enough. In my biggest criticism of the game, the upgrade system for skills is FAR too complicated. Between juggling passive slots, memory, and using active skills as passive skills to boost other active skills unless you convert them into hard passives and AAAAAARGH!!! This is all needlessly complicated for a game in which you either click on things until they die or pause the game and click on things until they die. I would have much more preferred Bastion's simplistic upgrade system to this, though to be fair it does add for much more deepened combat than Bastion (although that isn't saying too much).
The other main criticism is that the game is rather short. It does pace itself very well, and it does have a NG+ mode, but it doesn't really foster too much replayability unless you're obsessed with 'chieves or like running through low-level monsters as an unstoppable killing machine (and who doesn't amirite?). There is a challenge mode, but I gave up on it rather early. Unlike the story, I found it to be poorly paced and was constantly thrown into scenarios specifically designed to suck as much fun from combat as possible.
Despite these points, Transistor is a very good game with a very good story and a very good soundtrack that is definitely worth a recommendation. Normally for a game this short I'd advise you to wait for the price to drop a bit (20 bucks does feel an ounce steep for this), but considering Supergiant consists of only twelve people and they actually self-published this time, I'm all for supporting the artists as much possible. I highly recommend Transistor.

Sonic Forces is a game that had potential, but the developers chose not to use that potential. While the graphics are the best for a Sonic game, the blocky art style (similar to Lost World and Runners) does bring it down a little bit. Gameplay is, not the best. A lot of portions in the levels are pretty linear, however multiple paths do appear in several places. Classic Sonic was just jammed in just for banking off nostalgia, he has no plot relevance and controls terribly in very terrible level design. Sonic and Avatar are the better portions of the game, and can sometimes be a blast to play through. The QTEs that the game offers via Double Boost and actual QTEs are not really necessary, as they only require one button press every time. The bosses are pretty mediocre (spoilers!): Infinite and Metal Sonic are pretty much the same bosses except for when the avatar goes against Infinite. Death Egg Robot, phase one is just Egg Dragoon. Phase two is pretty much the Zavok boss fight, and phase three is just taken straight from Nega Wisp from Colors. Overall, I would say that the game is meh overall. Decent at best, but bad at worst.

Modern Sonic

Custom Character

Classic Sonic

Tag team?

Story

Stages

Music

Graphics

To start, this game isn't bad, I'd call it mediocre to good. It was overhyped and didn't live up to most peoples expectations. The story was also a huge disapointment. In the trailers and such, they make the story look so much better than it actually is, but I will hand them it for going after a darker tone. But Infinite as a villain was a let down, especially when you know his origin after playing Episode Shadow. The gameplay is great, but some of the physics, especially Classic Sonic's, are downright awful. Or sliding down the water slides can screw you over pretty bad sometimes too, or using boost in certain places. Otherwise the game is enjoyable when it isn't suffering from bad physics or it playing itself. The stage design isn't too great, it isn't bad for first time stage designers but when compared to Generations and such, it's pretty awful. It works, but it's just boring a good 70% of the time and pretty straightforward. If they brought back the stage designer from Generations this game would have been 100x better. But as every Sonic game has a great OST, this game does as well. I wouldn't pay the full $40 because the game is severely short but if you can get it for maybe $20 or under, go for it, quick one sitting blast of fun (sometimes). The custom character idea is good, but Sega made a mistake by giving people a literal OC creator. But the run down is:
Pros:
30 Stages
Avatar gameplay is really fun
Awesome OST
Darker story than most Sonic games
Cons:
Short as hell
The game plays itself sometimes
Underwhelming story, only element, is again, the dark tone
Boring stage design
Physics that screw you over sometimes
I'd give this game a 6/10. Generations was much better, go play that if you haven't and don't bother with this game unless you can get it under $20.

I completed this game on the Switch before buying it on the PC.  So that's $80 on one game, which tells you that either I'm not good with money, the game's pretty darn good, or both.
But here's the sad thing: Sonic Forces is a really good game ... on the Switch.  It runs beautifully, the controls are tight, and there weren't any glitches.  On the PC, however?  Lot's of slowdown and stuttering.  The controls are weirdly floaty and sensitive.  And I had to restart the game at one point because Knuckles wouldn't stop telling Sonic how glad he was to see him.  And the level-select UI takes up half the screen.  Really, the only thing the PC version has over the Switch are the trading cards.
The game itself is good.  The levels are beautiful, the gameplay is intense and speedy (as it should be in Sonic), the soundtrack is perfect, the voice acting is good (bonus points to Liam O'Brien and Mike Pollock, amazing jobs as always), Infinite is an awesome villain, the online bits are integrated well into the gameplay, the customization is fun, and the avatar character gets a nice character arc.  My only gripes are that the story assumes you're either read the comics or played Episode Shadow first and plays out accordingly, with some things never explained or expounded on in the main game itself; and that the game ends so soon that it left me begging for more.  There's gotta be some story updates on the way, dammit!
So in the end, I really wish there was a "neutral" option.  Because I love Sonic Forces, I just don't love the PC version.  8/10 for the game in general, 5/10 for the PC port.  Do with that what you will.  Consider this thumbs-up a "neutral" vote.

The hook of Borderlands 2, the very reason that I found myself thinking about it when I worked or tried to fall asleep, is the loot. Guns, ammo, character skins, grenade mods, class mods -- there’s always something just a bit better, something you so desperately didn’t even know you needed until you found it in Borderlands 2. Just like Diablo or a number of other action RPGs, the hunt for loot becomes intoxicating because of the tiny rush you get each time a rare colored item spills out of a chest or is dropped by a recently slain enemy. Every firefight and intense boss battle becomes all the more rewarding, because, though you might die a few times and want to crush something near you in real life, it suddenly feels like everything is going to be OK when you’re blasting away enemies with a newly looted gun.
Guns really do make up the bulk of the loot, and that’s great because you’re going to spend most of your time in Borderlands 2 staring down a gun sight. No matter the quest, at some point something or someone is getting pounded with lead. Thankfully, snappy shooting and lots of environmental hazards combine with each class’s unique ability to turn every skirmish into a playground. You simply have to decide the best -- or most entertaining -- way to kill everyone.

I absolutely adore this game.
I love strategy games, but often the "best" strategies are artificially hemmed into a game. In Total War games units get a moral hit when being flanked. This isn't a real emergent behavior of the simulation, it's a product of pushing what ought to be the best strategy onto the player.
Factorio is beautiful because there aren't any right or wrong ways to play the game. It simply provides you with pieces and lets the player figure out what to do with them. Every strategy will arise completely organically from the emergent behavior of the game.
People who like math and engineering should all love this game. People who don't like figuring things out for themselves might not like this game, but it's not like you have to be a genius to play Factorio. You build your factory. It's only as complicated as you make it.

Alien Isolation is the most suspenseful game I have ever played. A big part of why it was so suspenseful was the amazing sound design. Hearing the alien’s footsteps and shrieks with surround sound headphones while the brilliant dynamic soundtrack was playing was an experience like no other. Another reason why the suspense is masterfully done is the genius save system where you have to manually save at save stations. There are moments where you have played for more than 15 minutes without saving. This created a sense of urgency and massive tension because if you died you would have to replay those 15 minutes which nobody wants to do. I never cared more about staying alive than I did in this game. I started putting myself in ripleys situation like it was real life and was thinking what my next would move would be. There were times where I didn’t want to move at all from a hiding spot because going back out there was a big risk and a small bad move and it’s all over. The ai is so unpredictable which is amazing I never knew what it was going to do next. It’s also one of the most immersive games I have ever played. The atmosphere and environment was beautiful and I felt like I was in the original movie, it stays so true to its license. The graphics are stunning, the atmospheric effects as well as the lighting is artistic and the attention to detail in the environments is outstanding. Gripping story with great voice acting. One of the best stealth games I have played, the list continues. I never felt so hopeless Iike I did in this game which just encourages you to stay hidden from everything and the stealth mechanics are just so well done. A big complaint I hear about the game is the pacing but I never had that problem, I thought it was paced amazingly. Never did it feel slow or boring, there was never a dull moment in this long game. I loved it from start to finish. I seriously can’t think of anything that the game did wrong, all complaints I hear about the game I either didn’t experience them or I just disagree with like the backtracking and cheap deaths by the alien. The backtracking made sense and it was welcome, it never felt out of place or boring to go through. Every single death that I experienced was either bad luck or my fault, never cheap. In my opinion this game is a must play on hard, I don’t think I would have liked the game as much if I lowered the difficulty. The game wasn’t very difficult on hard I was never frustrated, I was very careful and planned all my next moves ahead of time and I got through the game fine but then you have the IGN reviewer screaming in his video not to play on hard or other reviews saying they had to lower the difficulty because it was way too frustrating and unfair... these people are spoiled by modern games. IGN’s review of this game is criminal and by far the worst review I have ever seen by the way. This is the best game released in 2014 and my favourite survival horror game of all time. This is a masterpiece in every sense of the word.

Ahh, a new MMO, and it looks like something between Diablo 3, Torchlight 2, and Final Fantasy Tactics...and I had such high hopes.  I'm going to try to be fair, I really am, but bad things are just what they are, so here we go!
-=The PROS!=-
1. Phenominal Soundtrack!  ( On Youtube:
)
Words cannot fully describe the win involved in the soundtrack for this game, and if I could buy just that, I totally would.
2. Beautiful Art Design!
The environments and lighting are awesome in this game, even on a low-end graphics card (Radeon 7850, 1gb DDR5).
3. Fun spell effects and animations!
The earthquake spell for wizards is amazingly fun.  As a caster you feel powerful indeed (while your spells aren't on cooldown, anyway).  The swordsman's skills are deadly as heck.  The cleric's healing doubles as land mines, and it rather satisfying to lead enemies over.  The archer?  Looks deadly, never played it.
4. Funny enemy design!
You've not had a complete life until you've used the earthquake spell to mince an entire garden in veggie genocide as a response to a charging mob of angry onions!
5. Teleport to Return Quest-Giver for FREE!
Yep, you get all the Newt♥♥♥♥♥♥Linings you were sent to gather, and you just press BACKSPACE to teleport back to the questgiver!  How cool is that?
6. Interesting Classes!
There are only Four Classes, but like the only for in ESO, you can do a lot with these...and each one can become like eight subclasses.  The wizard, for example, can become a Pyromancer (Fire Mage), a Cryomancer (Ice Mage), or a more powerful Wizard of the Second Circle at the first Class Rank Up.  I had some confusion about what is available when, and what people ingame are saying is different from what is listed online in helpful tools (
), but the upshot is that there is a lot to work with here, and some of the classes are hilarious or very interesting.  For example, there is a cleric class that carves totem poles that allow you to do things from teleport from a teleporation point (that the totem becomes), to run around a totem three times and be invincible from playing Ring Around the Rosie.  Another example is the Linker class, which allows a mage to share stats with other people, and looks like it could be insanely powerful in the right hands.
-=The CONS=-
1. Incomplete/Poor Quality Control.
This game was released over a year ago in Korea (you know, the REAL one in the south with less angry Bowl Cut Jr. as dictator and more Gangnam Style).  Why is there lag?  Why are there so many bugs?  Why won't the NPC talk to me instead of just turning to face me and stare deeply into my character's eyes?  Sometimes quests hang, and the teleports even carry over to the wrong character in the return-to-quest teleporting thing, making it iffy at times.  It feels like a BETA release.
2. Pay to Trade
I'm all for free games, but for the love of all that's fun, don't do crap like this as a game developer!  You have to be part of the premium (subscription) crowd both to trade an item to someone or to have an item traded to you AND you only get a certain number of trades a month with that setup!  This works out to something like fifty cents per trade for both parties involved.  What's worse, every time an item changes hands, it loses 'Potential', which lowers the item's value, and if an item changes hands enough, it becomes worthless.  You think you can join this 'free' game with your friends and share gear?  You think you can give your buddy that sword you just picked up since you'll never use it, and it is a clear upgrade for him?  Think again...  But, hey, you think, maybe you can just shared-bank it to an alt, right?  Well...
3. No Shared Bank Space for Non-Premium Players
That's right!  Unless you pay the sub fee, you don't get access to this feature, which makes picking up gear you can't really use on the character you're on quite infuriating!
4. Auctions Don't Solve These Things!
While you CAN sell things at auction, the AH takes a cut, and the items still lose Potential in the changing of hands.
5. Dumb Enemies
Mowing down droves of enemies is great and all, but at least early on, the difficulty in this game comes down to being handed a mallet and a bottle of booze and told to amuse yourself out there with the baby seals.  Enemies that can actually attack worth a damn seldom hit you, and it takes like a dozen or more enemies to become any sort of threat, which can be solved by one or two well-placed spells.  I'm sure it gets harder later, but up to level 20, nothing is a thing you can't casually step over on your drunken rampage through the woods to grandma's house.
6. What's a Megaphone?!
Like Maple Story, to talk in zone chat, you need a megaphone.  It's an item that lets you talk in zone chat.  No, you aren't told you need this when you start the game, you just have to figure that out.  No, people aren't ignoring you; they can't see what you're saying unless you are right next to them.  Any help a noob would get in zone chat from the community in most MMOs is denied you here because you have to go buy megaphones first...with their shop currency...and that currency, while given to you at a very slow rate, maxes out low, and can only otherwise be obtained through real money transactions.  This punishes noobs, and that makes me sad. :(
7. Holy GoldSpammers, Batman!
On DAY ONE of the pre-release of this game, the gold spammers were already at it, and they can fill up your entire chat box with their spam.  It is up to you to block them, and what's worse, the game has a scrolling marquee that mirrors chat, so if you get gold-spammed, their website is rolling across the top of your screen for three minutes.
Conclusion: It's fun to play when it works, but there are things that the devs have done that, while Korean players might put up with them, Americans simply won't in any kind of large numbers.  Unless they change this BS, we're going to find other games to play, and this free game will become a free ghost town.  A pretty world with no players isn't a game worth playing in terms of MMO, and that's where things will go if they don't give up the obvious cash-grab policies.  Instead of denying players features that are basic and expected (such as the ability to trade) and forcing players to hand over their credit card info for those features, the devs might consider doing something like making ingame vanity stuff in quantity that people actually want, like ArenaNet does with Guild Wars 2 (which is also free, and you can trade in it!).  Their cash-grabbing feature-levering is going to blow up in their face if this continues.

If you are looking for a free to play hunting title i have to start this review with some bad news: this game is not free to play by most interpretations of the term "Free to play". As a limited member you can do the following:
Unlike other free to play games you cannot feasibly unlock new content by playing the game a lot or by being good at it. You are stuck with what you have and that is it – and it’s admittedly not too much.
So, you made it past the initial post explaining the game is not free to play and might be considering picking the game up? In that case, let us talk about the games pricing model and what it entails. The games pricing model is twofold: there are both subscriptions and items purchases.
:  Subscription starts at 9.99 for a 3 month period which is arguably quite good compared to most MMO's. In exchange for your subscription you will receive unlimited ammunition for all the weapons you own, and a license to hunt all species of animals in the game. It is also possible to buy ammunition and animal hunting licenses as separate items though the monetary exchange rate for this is fairly bad in comparison. (But perhaps worthwhile if you are a very casual player)
: Buyable items cover a broad range of possibilities. There is weapons, scopes, clothing, deployables (Hunting towers), utilities (Animal callers, storage increasing backpack) and temporally power-ups (Wind indicators, facial paint et cetera).
Except for the power-ups all items are permanent once bought, with the caveat being that you will need an animal license and ammunition to hunt specific animals. There is an additional caveat as well: Each weapon can only be used on a subset of the animals in the game - you cannot use a pistol on a bear or a rifle on a pheasant for example. If you want to hunt all animals you will need to buy multiple weapons. The utilities sold are somewhat more optional though a huge convenience: callers enable you to coax animals them out of hiding or locate them, while specific clothing will provide superior camouflage thus fewer running animals as you try to sneak upon them.
Bottom line? Expect to buy a membership and - depending on playing preference - one or more weapons, scopes and clothing if you wish to fully enjoy everything the game has to offer. The cheapest variety would be buying the wayfarer pack for about 15 Euro's; this includes 3 months of membership, a shotgun, a pistol with scope and some consumables. The shotgun itself is - with different ammo types - able to take down every type of animal in the game.
Alternative you can do some research and find yourself a relatively cheap combination of items that allows you to hunt virtually everything the way you want it. Still, don't be surprised if you end up forking 20-30 bucks over initially if you chose this route (that figure includes a 3 month membership).
Despite the games price model arguably being steep I personally find myself enjoying the game quite a bit, so for me it is well worth the triple-a equivalent price I spend on it so far. Considering my current time invested, the subscription fee and my lack of a need to buy new items the game will be cheaper than a regular subscription MMO if I keep playing it another month or two, while spending a similar amount of time on it.
That said: I can only advice the game to people who – like me – enjoy hunting simulations quite a bit. If you plan on picking up the game you should be able to live with the thought of having to possibly do a relatively sizable investment initially, followed by a fairly mild recurrent billing scheme. It is not a good pickup for people looking exclusively for a free to play title due to the rather sharp limitations and the inability to unlock content by playing a lot or being good. Still, the game itself is a lot of fun if you like hunting sims. If you can stomach the need for payment and don't mind doing some research into the items you want i can hearthily recomment it.
