1st person, open world, apocalyptic action shooter with RPG, fiction and horror elements. It's the 2nd game in timeline, following soon after the events of S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky. This is the original S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and first game in the series, about zone that surrounds 30km around destroyed nuclear power plant. Aftermath of tragedy at Chernobyl power plant (Ukraine USSR) that took place in 1986, when one of nuclear reactors in Chernobyl nuclear power plant exploded, releasing big quantities of radiation and contaminating large area around the plant and nearby town of Pripyat. Developers took this true and gruesome story, added fiction and horror elements from the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. books, to make a unique and atmospheric 1st person action shooter experience.
Story takes place long after the events of 1986, now it's 2012 and zone around Chernobyl is nothing like it was before. In year 2006, there was 2nd reactor explosion (fiction) that expanded the zone and sent waves of energy and radiation outwards, killing every living being in the area. Only military personal and scientists were allowed to enter the zone. Even though military closed all the entrances and fenced down 30km area around the power plant, despite the dangers people started to venture inside the zone, exploring unknown areas, discovering new anomalies, artifacts and creatures within. Later those brave yet outlaw individuals were called Stalkers.
Though your story in beginning of the game is unclear, because you are suffering from some sort of amnesia, you must uncover the events that took place before you awoke on Sidorovich's table, with strange tattoo on your arm and single objective in your "Personal digital assistant" (PDA), to kill someone called Strelok.
Game has open word imitation with many large, open yet fenced areas to explore, as well as indoor and underground levels. All areas have checkpoints between them, and going through one will load the next area connected to it. You can easily check map, objectives, statistics about yourself and much more in your PDA. Many areas in game are radioactive and hazardous, some filled with anomalies that are dangerous and hard to notice, so make sure you always listen to your "beeping" Detector (no puns intended) to quickly leave the dangerous area.
As well as invisible hazards there are plenty of dangers that you can see, one of those are mutants (creatures, animals, people that were exposed to large amounts of radiation, and through many generations mutated more and more), some previously were wild animals or livestock, others are heavily mutated humanoids. All of them are very resistant to radiation and many in game hazards, which explains how they survived the 2nd reactor explosion in 2006.
One of many ways to protect yourself from hazards is wearing suits made by Stalkers, they range from simple clothing with simple weather protection; one piece body suits with rebreathers to armor with chest kevlar plates and radiation reflective layers, to protect you from many types of harm. As well as gear, there are many medications that can save your life: few kinds of medikits, bandages, anti radiation drugs and injections. Some basic survival equipment includes: knife, binoculars, food (sausage, bread, canned food, energy drinks and vodka which is ideal to reduce radiation exposure).
Main source of income in game are artifacts. Usually found near anomalies and secret stashes where Stalkers and other people hide their valuables, around the world. There are many different kinds of artifacts, each with their own unique look, statistics and value. Most artifacts will give you useful "buffs" but also expose you with radiation, others absorb radiation or add positive effects, so mix and match to get the best symbiosis, or simply drink more vodka / anti radiation drugs if your radiation exposure is reaching high levels.
There are many kinds of weapons in game. Different kinds of pistols, sub machine guns, shotguns, assault rifles, machine guns, sniper rifles and grenades. As well as some futuristic weapons I wont mention to not spoil the game. You can put scopes, silencers, grenade launcher modifications on some weapons. There are few bullet types for each weapon, as well as many bullet calibers. You can't modify or repair armor and weapons like you can in S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky, so I would suggest to get mods for that if you really want to. Game has working ballistics system, so bullets fly in arc and will ricochet from surfaces.
Game has few factions and depending on your actions, you can be either hostile, neutral or friendly with them. Hostile reputation will not benefit you in any way, neutral will grant you the ability to speak and trade with them and friendly will open up some side missions, discounts and chance to join said faction. Best game for faction play is S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky. Just wanted to add, even though game has many difference types of NPC roles, there are no female nurses, cooks or any females whatsoever. Developers decided not to include those because of harsh world and nature of players, go figure.
To close it off will say that game is somewhat aged and may not look that appealing to many players. But what game lacks, it compensates with atmosphere, grim feel, gameplay and story. It has working day and night cycle, life simulation for NPC and decent AI. Game will not hold your hand, and is challenging on harder difficulties if you don't take cover behind something. Voice acting is a bit basic but only if you play with English language, it's just a bit weird with the accents. I experienced minor graphics glitches concerning lighting and shadows, as well as many xrCore.dll relates crashes without modifications, but maybe it's just on my end.
Other than that game is fun, with tension and scare moments once in a while. Try this out, and better yet get all 3 games and play them in this order: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky, S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl, S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat for the best story experience.
P.S. Don't forget your anti radiation sun cream, it's not often but occasionally you can see sun in between rain and thunderstorms.

As insanely addictive as it is fun, Factorio caught me completely by surprise.  I picked the game up after hearing from a bunch of friends that it was great and also due to the fact that it had a 99% overwhelmingly positive rating on Steam.  The videos and screenshots didn't have me entirely sold on it but I decided to give it a go and within an hour I was hooked on it.  So hooked, in fact, that it became the only game that I played for nearly a week.
The premise of Factorio is that your ship crashlanded on an alien planet that is rich in raw materials and packed full of hostile creatures.  At first you'll be harvesting resources by hand and trying to set up a small outpost but within a short period of time you'll have set up the basics of your ever-growing industrial assembly network that will process all kinds of resources and goods into increasingly more complex goods.  As your technology level rises the variety and potency of your production will continue to increase.
Gameplay clips and screenshots won't give you even a glimpse of the true game experience, which is unfortunate, and because of that I almost passed entirely on this great game.  If you're on the fence at all about it I highly recommend that you pick it up.  You won't be disappointed.  There are few games out there that can give you the feeling of accomplishment and satisfaction that Factorio does all while having a lot of fun putting it together.

There are many Eureka! moments in this game and they all feel great.  Theres just something really satisfying about staring at my screen trying to puzzle something out and wondering how I'm going to make things work and then having an idea pop in my head (which may or may not be correct) and trying it out.  When things do go as planned I feel like a genius and when they don't I feel like its very easy to understand why things weren't working the way I had hoped.  Because its easy to understand what you did wrong and learn from it, every time I restart my game I feel like my new factory is significantly better than the previous one.  They only real criticisms that I have is   I really like the art style as well.  Reminds me of watching my uncle play PC games when I was younger.  The only real criticisms that I have for the game is that it takes a long time to get a new factory up and running.  It can take awhile to get to a point where your factory can start automating red science (where I feel like the goes from being a grind to being more engaging) and that their is no planning mode initially (Like in Prison Architect).  You have to pre-plan so much when you start a new factory that it would have been nice if there was a way you could start marking down where you're going to put things while you're waiting for your resources to build up.  There's a blueprint mode that comes later as research, but I really wish it was something that you got initially.  Beyond those two complaints, however, I'm having an absolute blast playing it and could see it being something I stay with for a long time.

Boosting gameplay with Modern Sonic and Shadow, Traditional side-scrolling gameplay with Classic Sonic, General 2D+3D platforming gameplay with your own custom avatar character with a variety of wispon weapons.
I played this game on my gaming PC which has a gtx 1080 so I was able to play it at 4K unlocked FPS with all the settings maxed out so YMMV.
Like any Sonic game, need I say more?
About 40 levels if you count the boss fights and bonus DLC levels.
The level themes have had a decent amount of variety. You have your GreenHill clone, industrial level, space level, a bit of desert, casino, and water here and there, forest level, city level, and Eggman’s base level. But I wish the game could have included a fire and ice level.
For a Sonic game I thought the length was fine others who’ve never played a Sonic game may think otherwise but a platforming game can only be so long when you have a character that moves so fast, besides I’d rather take quality levels over a large quantity of bland levels. It took me 6-hours to complete the story but there’s plenty of post-game stuff to do such as collecting all the red-rings and getting all S-ranks, completing all the side missions, and collecting all the avatar gear. The main game is longer than Generations so that’s a step forward at-least. And may I just ask for all the people complaining that the game is too short, would you like Sonic Team to bring back the werehog? Honestly just think for a second. The reason why we got the werehog in Sonic Unleashed was because Sonic Team feared that the game would be criticized for being too short with the boost gameplay alone. So I just want to say, please be careful what you wish for, or in this case, please be careful what you complain about.
Most levels will probably average you 2-3 minutes on a good run. To some however this may seem short but people have to keep in mind that this is a Boost-Sonic game. Sonic moves so fast that the levels can only last for so long. Not to mention that being able to take multiple routes to get to the goal is a staple in the Sonic franchise which understandably cuts from the length of the levels. So whatever floats your boat. If you prefer long and linear levels then Forces will disappoint you, but if you prefer shorter levels with multiple routes then you’ll enjoy the levels Forces has to offer)
The major selling point of this game that is supposed to set it apart from previous Sonic games is the fact that instead of fighting against Eggman to protect the world, Eggman in this game has already won. He’s already taken over the planet, Sonic is captured, and Sonic friends are desperately trying to salvage the 99.9% of the world that they’ve lost. But the problem is that we don’t see Eggman conquer the world, we are just told that he did. After the cutscene when Sonic is defeated by Infinite, we are told through text that 6-months have passed and Eggman has taken over the planet and are later told through dialogue between Knuckles and Silver that Sonic was captured and taken prisoner by Eggman. This was a really disappointing transition for me, it's almost as if the animation team wasn’t given enough time to animate scenes of Eggman’s robots taking control of the planet, the rise of the Eggman empire, and the capture of Sonic which should have been the focus of the game story-wise.
However despite my complaints about the story, at the end of the day, Sonic Forces is a cartoony platformer game. A Story with animated cutscenes and voiced dialogue isn’t needed or expected, it’s really just icing on the cake and I respect Sonic Team for taking a risk and trying to have Sonic deal with a serious plot again, so I do not count story nitpicks as a real con against this game. If we can have games like Mario Odyssey with no plot at all get 10/10s then Sonic should be criticised for plot either.)

How they went from Sonic Generations to this, I have no idea. Below is simply my opinion, so your experience may vary:
What I liked:
- Great visuals; there are some very good-looking levels.
- Boost for Modern Sonic now has a 'hop', making smaller jumps easier and making movement more fluid. (though level design doesn't complement it)
- Getting rid of Generations Classic Sonic's "hold X to insta-spindash" for the Drop Dash was a welcome change.
- The story isn't terrible, but the writing could have used work.
- No more life system!
What I didn't like:
- Level design. Expect random enemies placed around and tons of homing attack chains. Automation is everywhere. Rings are very abundant in certain stages. Sometimes enough to where It ruins the aesthetic.
- Animations; specifically, Modern Sonic. Generations had a perfect set of animations for Sonic. However, the animations for Forces all the way to the Sonic's idle (the one in Lost World, may I add) doesn't hold a candle to the ones in Generations. Why not just reuse those? This may seem overly nitpicky, but it's something you have to look at all the time.
- Wisps; please, stop bringing them back. They were fine for Colors.
- 2D sections for Modern Sonic. You have Classic Sonic yet again. Keep those 2D sections to him.
- Speaking of Classic Sonic, he shouldn't have been in this game to begin with.
- Music. It is a huge step down compared to some of the previous games. I personally did not like any of it.
- Voice acting. (still) Yes, I'm going to be that guy. Certain voices just do not fit certain characters. **Mike Pollock's Eggman performance was very good as usual, however.
- Avatar stages; I dreaded playing through these. Having to go from Modern Sonic to one of the Avatar stages is very jarring. Both characters have similar gameplay, but completely different physics. I don't mind the Avatar idea, but it was poorly executed.
- Controls; this is something you would have to try for yourself as it's rather difficult to explain. Modern Sonic has limited air movement, and now also lacks the drift ability. Even the spline path automation fails to keep Sonic on path in some stages.
I could go on and on. 40 bucks is asking for a bit much for a game that takes less than 3 hours to finish. These games lately have also been lacking a certain "feeling" like no love was put into them. (IMO) You could feel that with Sonic Mania, but not with Forces.
One final note:
Sonic Team, you are only hurting yourselves by locking these games down. You already have the foundation, let the fans try making the content for a change. (like Mania) Look into Steam Workshop or something.

Disappointing. Painful. Uninspired. A worrying sign for the future of not only Sonic, but many games.
These are the terms and terminology I would consistently use to describe this title. I've always been a Sonic fan, and I still am. Which is why I have to finally put my foot down, because instead of just trying something different, they have damaged what has previously existed and done nothing special.
Let's start with the good. All the good.
- The Graphics. They're flashy. They're good. Expected.
- The boost itself. The effect has improved massively, a better streak that makes you feel as if Sonic is going hella fast (he is not, this game is slower than colors which makes it the slowest of the four boost gameplay games)
- The custom character. The choices are somewhat varied for the body, and there are large numbers of costume items to choose. Most of my fun was had goofing around with that and a buddy giving suggestions. From total anarchist fox to a schoolgirl outfit just cause.
-The cutscenes and acting are awful. Except for Sonic. Every scene with him is humorous and quippy. He's much like the Sonic Colors character, namely in that he spends most of his time pointing out how ridiculous other's motivations are.
-The music is good. Sometimes. Sometimes it's awful. It's a mixed bag.
That's all done. On with the bad.
-Everything else.
The reason this game is awful is entirely context. If you've never played a Sonic boost formula game, or a classic game in general, you may think this game is alright. If you like games that literally play themselves, you may like this game.
Some of us HATE a game inwhich the first level can literally be completed at top speed by holding forward, then holding only X, then jumping a total of three times. Those are all the inputs needed. That's it.
In comparison to the games that this title serves as a sequel to, it's a step backwards, a showcasing that Sega has no faith in their own Sonic Boost gameplay.
This title suffers from simpler animations, simplified movement (there is no longer a drift, the game plays itself far more often without ANY input necessary, QTEs are not failable (you can hit A at any time during them)), and extremely lenient scoring with no consequences for failure. No lives counting down, just a score that becomes lower, but ultimately the daily reward they effectively force on you means your score is meaningless: you will get an S.
Dying 5 times gets you an A.
All of that is side features. The core feature of the game is hollow. The levels are uninspired and simple, there is no real variation in your pathway that is meaningful, and much worse is classic sonic.
For anyone who actually understands why Sonic 4 was not well received, the physics of classic sonic in Forces are terrible. He slides a ton, he controls like trash, it's almost like they took the code from Generations and decided "nah, we're gonna keep Classic Sonic, but not the controls and physics everyone loved."
Worse off, there's no reason for him to be there story wise. Literally the bad guy is warping reality, so he just shows up. Once the bad guy is defeated, he leaves. Similarly he offers nothing but to run through some levels as "another Sonic."
The custom character COULD have used all those classic Sonic levels to flesh out their own capabilities and gameplay, but no. Sega only works in halfsteps. They don't trust the boost despite glowing reviews of Generations for its boost stages, as well as Unleashed.
A halfstep with a werehog,
a halfstep with 2d focus,
a halfstep with classic sonic,
and now even less due to both classic and the custom character.
It doesn't matter much that the game included them all, each portion of gameplay in this title is not good. It's passable at best. Failable with context.
Do yourself a favor and look up the stage "Rooftop Run" from Unleashed. Then look up any Sonic stage from Forces. None of them compare. This is why I will not recommend this game. It's simply a step backwards to be more inclusive and easy. And I do not agree with the final product and its myriad of issues.
I will continue trying to find something worthwhile in this game. I won't hold my breath.

I wanted this game to be good. After the success of Sonic Mania, I really wanted it to be good.
Now, it wasn't necessarily
, it just wasn't
. Mediocre at best, honestly.
I like to start with positives, and unfortunately for this game, that won't take long. In my opinion, the soundtrack is fantastic for the most part. The classic sonic music is a little spotty, but other than that I enjoyed it quite a bit. The voice actors did a fantastic job given the circumstances (i.e. crappy plot), and it was nice to see all of the voice actors we know and love in play. In terms of graphics, the game looks decent, definitely not the worst, but definitely not the best. The plot isn't super interesting, but I still felt that I wouldn't be satisfied if I didn't finish the game.
Now onto the negatives. Gameplay is
, and that's something you definitely don't want in a game about the so called "fastest thing alive." Classic Sonic feels clunky and the aerial momentum is all ♥♥♥♥ed up if you input a different direction than where you're going. Classic Sonic levels take a long time, especially
. Modern Sonic feels incredibly linear, and groups of enemies don't even feel like a threat in any capacity, in 2D and 3D sections. Half of the time I felt like I was just pressing the boost button and waiting for a section to be over. The avatar is a whole different beast, as it tries to combine aspects of the two Sonic's gameplay as well as incorporate new gameplay mechanics. Personally, I found avatar gameplay the most tolerable of the three. It didn't feel as linear as the others, as you can change your Wispon which, more often than not, allows you to access different paths in the level. The customization aspects of the game are fun yet ultimately useless, and don't benefit you in any way. The pair-up levels are an interesting concept, but all amount to you button mashing for 3 seconds and then just putting the controller down. Hard mode doesn't feel like a challenge in any capacity, and I couldn't even tell you what makes it hard mode. There are times when the game just drops frames which is forgivable in my opinion, but it's often at times that don't make sense for frame rate drops. The cutscenes don't always line up with what happens when you're looking at the map.

The difficulty is almost entirely due to world geometry not actual fight difficulty. I died from enemies a very small number of times, and died from being pushed off a small ledge or attacking off a cliff much more often. Player invasions are not optional unless you go "offline", these invasions are a constant annoyance and ruin any fun to be had in the pve enviroment. Going offline means no in game "messages" or blood puddles ( Messages are tips and clues players can leave behind in the game world for others to see, the blood can be examined to see how someone before you died in that location. ) The screen shots you see are not from the version of the game you will get upon purchase, they even admitted that the game had to be dulled down upon release because they just could not reproduce consistant frame rates with their engine. Some sections of the game look nice, but most look really dull and repedative. Eventually I became bored not knowing where to go next after having run into numerous dead ends and locked doors. On the plus side there are some cool enemy models in game, some very unique ones in fact, though nearly all of them engage in combat the same exact way and end up feeling like pallet swaps more than unique fights. You never really know what most of the stats on gear do, resistances are represented by low res icons that are unclear in their description. Pretty much just going with whatever seems to give the best overall numbers seemed to work. Being a caster is pathetic, EVERYONE plays a melee based setup. Dissapointing, very dissapointing. The first Dark Souls was no magical experience either, but at was slightly better than this labotomy of gaming.

Absolutely incredible Action RPG from Supergiant. This is their follow up to Bastion.
You adventure through the steampunk-esque city from a top-down perspective while the sword, Transistor, offers Red (you) dialogue throughout the game. Supergiant seems to be pushing this narrative style as a motif of theirs, and this time the character providing the dialogue is speaking directly to the protagonist, rather than speaking about them, as in Bastion.
Everything about this game is incredible. The customization is very in depth - there are plenty of playstyles available. The combat is real time with the addition of the Turn, which is very similar to the turn-based elements incorporated into certain games, most notably the recent Fallout games - you have a set amount of 'time' that can be used for movement or planning attacks/abilities.
If I can posit a criticism its that the game is a little short - I like something I can really sink my teeth into. Also, there are some puzzle-esque elements in the beginning that strangely do not make any appearances afterwards. This seems quite odd and somewhat of a missed opportunity.
Nevertheless, this is a must buy. Go buy it.

This is an interesting game with respect to the gameplay, which consists of FPS, free roam, and survival horror all packed into one. One thing that sets this game apart from other FPS games is the difficulty. Even at the lowest difficulty, a few bullets are enough to kill you and your health does not instantly regenerate like in some other games. This forces you to take a more tactical approach to dealing with large groups of enemies as opposed to running out in the open holding down the trigger. This, combined with the strict weight limit and the dense radiation in Pripyat and Chernobyl changes the game from a fast paced shoot em up to a slower paced game oriented around survival.
By far the highlight of this game is Lab X-18, which really brought out the survival horror aspect of the game, as it is a poorly lit lab packed with several invisible mutants, floating objects, and other terrifying elements.
The one thing I would change about this game is the ending. I feel like the game ended a bit too abruptly. The final cutscene was less than 30 seconds long, which took away from the overall sense of accomplishment. Apart from that, the game was great.

Do you like building a base, and defending it while collecting resources? Then get this game, because this is the best base building game there had been in a long while, if not ever!
It's called Factorio because it's based on the idea of building a factory, but like many RTS games, you have to obtain and manage resources - building one thing that leads to another, and then another, while defending yourself on an alien world.
But it's the way that you go about this that is so compelling about this game, and that's where the factory bit comes in. And basically you are building a factory, a factory where you have to intrically manage the distribution of every resource you collect, there is nothing abstract, you see it all, on conveyerbelts, in storage boxes, in your production machines, or in your personal storage. It is, therefore, a clear, closed logical system, which you have to manage, and where you can see and manipulate every single element.
This is the games strength. More than any other game I have played, it satisfies the itch to manage a logistical system, and make it as efficient and beautiful as you possibly can. Add to that the fact that you have to defend this againt hostile creatures, and integrate a system to do this into your base, and you have a very satisfying and addictive game.
The game includes:
* Tech tree - you have to make the resources for research
* Walls, turrets and gates

EDIT: I admit I didn't touch on the gameplay the first time I reviewed this because I was complaining about the story, so I added some of that here.
I wouldn’t call myself much of a Sonic fan, in fact this is my first Sonic game in 15 years.  I bought it because I’m a sucker for create your own character games.
While I did enjoy Sonic Forces at first, and I would almost recommend to anyone who likes Sonic games in general, I am having trouble recommending this to anyone who wants this game so they can be their own character in their own sonic story.  If you don’t want to share the spotlight with both Sonic and Sonic Classic, you’ll be disappointed that your character’s involvement is rather lackluster. Despite SEGA’s tag line “The fate of this world is in your hands” it really isn’t.  You’re better off writing fanfiction for yourself if you want to feel more empowered as a character than in this game.
The Gameplay itself was fun for a little while, but the clunky and slippery controls combined with stiff platforming and instant death pits really aggravated me to the point I would spend 30-45 minutes on a single stage because of cheap deaths.  I had to switch from my controller to the keyboard to play some of the classic Sonic stages and even then my character wouldn't jump and when he did, it was such a small jump.  I died so many times from this, I almost chucked my controller in rage, and I NEVER get that way with any game.  At least in Oath of Felghana, I died so many times because I screwed up, not because the game was unresponsive it sabatoged my gameplay.  Even my friend ragequit the game after experiencing the same problems I have so I know it's not me.  I don't know why people are saying this is easy.  I never had such a hard time beating a game as I did Sonic Forces, but I was determined to see the end.
I bought this game hoping to be immersed in the Sonic Universe as my own Sonic Avatar.  I enjoy games where I have my own character interacting with characters I know and love.  Games like Dragonquest IX, both the South Park RPGs, and Dragonball Xenoverse have your character as the hero to help the main characters save the world.  However unlike those games, Sonic Forces does NOT have you as the hero, but the sidekick.  I can’t tell you what a difference that makes.  Saving the world is NOT up to you, and you are assisting the Sonics, rather than being aided by them.  The whole game seems to talk down to you, like you’re just some glorified pest control and often the DECOY to allow the Sonics to do their thing.  You don’t even have a name.  You’re just some anonymous soldier that just does the dirty work for the main characters and most of them just sit around patting each other on the back,
About 66% of this game has you playing as Sonic or Sonic Classic, and that bothered me, because I wanted more Avatar gameplay, to the point I redid levels just to play as him more.  They do have SOS quests but sometimes you end up having to play as somebody else’s avatar.  Why would I care about somebody else’s character? I want to play as my own, that’s a big reason why I bought this game.  Their avatars aren’t even dressed anyway, just a bunch of bland nobodies, and if you die once, you lose the level automatically and all the effort you may have gotten from the level.  Also the SOS levels that require you to save the avatar means you have to comb over the stage very carefully other you lose even if you beat the stage.
The storyline itself seems to focus more on Classic Sonic being the hero, and the other characters make such a big deal about him and the other Sonic, you might as well be a fly on the wall.  Most of the cutscenes you’re not even in.  You barely interact with any of the villains directly.  Can you imagine in Dragonball Xenoverse if you played as Goku more than half the time and your character was just hanging around and showed up sometimes?  That’s not what I expect when I play a game with a custom avatar.  We, as the player, want to be drawn into the story, to feel like we matter and to leave an influence on all the other characters, heroes and villains alike.  Sonic just ends up holding your hand the whole time and he does all the work for you.  Why is your character even here?  The story about the avatar being the only survivor in the rebel attack, is just glanced over.  Even when your character has a moment to shine in some scenes, it fizzles out and doesn’t mean anything in the long run.  Sonic saves the world, you just helped a little.
At the end of the game everyone makes such a big deal about Classic Sonic’s contribution, they just glanced over your character, and nobody even bothered to congratulate you on your hard work, just “Okay guys, let’s clean up this mess and go home”  That ending is what motivated this review.  I slaved over this game from beginning to end, and the pay off was that everyone cheered for Sonic and Sonic Classic and my character got no thanks. Everyone walks away and the game is over.  After the credits you get a slight pat on the back by the other characters, and they don't really care that you decide to leave.  So Sonic Classic gets this giant farewell and your character gets the "You're leaving? Okay see ya."  This angered me on so many levels.  What was the point of having my own custom character if he just gets glanced over the whole story like some Sonic Fanfic character on DeviantArt?  If the custom avatar was taken out, the story wouldn’t change.  Except for a couple cutscenes, I never once felt it was MY story, but rather Sonic’s story that I just happened to be in for a little while.  At least in the NES title Hydlide you get a generic "Congratulations" which is more thanks than what I get in this game.
SEGA missed an opportunity with this game, and it’s not because of the crash bugs, or the sloppy controls, or the stiff platforming, or even the short length of the game, but I was disappointed by my lack of involvement as my own Sonic Character.  I wouldn’t have minded sharing the spotlight with Sonic, but his sidekick Tails had more involvement in the story than me.  I was hoping that this game would have had more of a focus on my character’s struggle for achievement and eventual gratification that I did something, like it is in other games with custom avatars.  I felt this disconnect that I wasn’t contributing much to the story at all and in the end, my character leaves and is forgotten.
I at least got some enjoyment out of this game, and the costumes are very fun to play around with, but I was really hoping my character would have had a bigger role in this game.  I do hope that if SEGA makes another custom Avatar game, they’d do something more with it.  For example, maybe Sonic is out of the picture completely and our character is the last hope in saving him and the world, with this constant struggle to even be half the hero that he is, ending with a final realization that our character made a difference.  That would have been a lot more satisfying.  I can’t deny that Sonic is an iconic character, much like Goku, or Link, or Megaman, but in custom avatar games, they should give you, the player, a chance to be a hero and not be just another sidekick.  That's how I feel these games should be made, as a love letter to the fans, and not an obligation.  Afterall I want to feel like I’m "Batman", not his "butler"

Papers, Please is a triumph of game design. Pulled inexorably into a world of grey morality and suffering - and all with C64 style graphics - you are taken deep into the bleak existence of a soviet-era border guard. With a strong central premise and intelligent, minimalist scripting, it's more compelling and unsettling than most AAA titles out there. If you've 'enjoyed' soviet-era literature or film, if you fancy some cerebral/philosophical exercise, or just want to remind yourself what games can achieve when they are made outside the 'annual clone' publisher cycle, buy this game.

I had no idea what I was getting into with this game. From what I'd heard you just sit at a border checkpoint and decide if people are allowed to enter the country or not. And that's exactly what I got, but Papers, Please is so much more than that. It's not just a job simulation, it's a story of moral choices and corrupt government. It's not just about a border guard, it's about a man who struggles to provide for his family, who must work for the smallest of wages to make some of the toughest choices. You sit in your little checkpoint booth. A man comes up and hands you his passport. You skim over the information and stamp a big green "APPROVED" for him. He thanks you and starts to walk away, but before he does he says, "my wife is right behind me, please be nice to her." Sure enough, up steps a nice young woman. There's her passport. You look down and see an expiration date of last month. "This document is expired" you say. She stares at you, eyes wide and pleading: "Please, if I go back to my country they will kill me. Please let me in." What do you do? Do you risk losing your paycheck and therefore leave yourself unable to buy medicine for your sick son? Or do you abandon all morality and turn the woman away?
Papers, Please is not an easy game, nor is it free of consequences. Not only does it become insanely difficult to reivew piles of papers and make sure every little details is accrate and correct, but every choice you make determines who you are and the path you take. Will you work tirelessly for the glory of Arstotzka, or will you join the Order and be a part of the uprising against the tyrannical, corrupt government?

This game is amazing, for some reason I don't quite know yet. You just start playing and suddenly you realise you've been stamping passports for three hours. Highly immersive and a unique style. It feels like you somehow play God in a world in which you are but a pawn of a totalitarian regime. One of the weirdest experiences of 2013 as far as gaming is concerned.

So, to start, I have just finished Sabred of Infinity for the first time, so if you want to know what its like to play through it 5 times, ill have to get back to you (because i do plan mulitple playthroughs)
I hardly ever write reviews for games on steam. For the most part, i think someone should be able to judge how they are going to feel about a game based on the general description of the game and its overall reception. Most people, i think (including myself), even if they look at reviews, go into the reviews with a certain disposition towards the game one way or another and tend to discount the reviews that dont already side with their own pre-formed opinions.
This game is uniquly special though.
As there are not a lot of good, modern text based games these days, at least that i know of, i feel the need to review Sabres of Infinity.
This might be one of the best games i have ever played.
If Sabres of Infinity was 19.99, i would tell every one of my friends to buy it.
There are plenty of books that cost 10-20 dollars, and this is essentially an amazing book that you get to be a part of.
The writing is amazing, and while i usually hate games that force me to play as a specific person (i love to create my own original character) this game makes you truely feel the pressures of the role you must undertake, and it makes you enjoy it.
Its quite a respectable length, especially for its price, and they choices you make all feel like they have weight and influence over the course of your story. I have only finished one playthrough, so im not 100% how much can change, but it seems like there are a lot of different options, and i have already seen several choices that i made that i know caused certain decisions later down the line to either succeed or fail.
If you are someone who has played games like Baulders Gate, Dragon Age, Mass Effect, Kotor 1-2 (#Bioware Fanboy) and the best part of those games was the story, dialogue, and decision making, you WILL enjoy this game. Its not quite the same as any of those, because obviously there is no "Combat" or controlling your character on a screen, but the decisions are just as real.
It is a deeply immersive and well described and drawn out world, with characters that feel real, where every choice you make feels like the most important choice of the game. For the quality of content you get, compared to the price of the game, they are basically giving this out for free, because i would pay a hell of a lot more for this game than they're asking. 10/10, Im off to buy Guns of Infinity

Absolutely incredible Action RPG from Supergiant. This is their follow up to Bastion.
You adventure through the steampunk-esque city from a top-down perspective while the sword, Transistor, offers Red (you) dialogue throughout the game. Supergiant seems to be pushing this narrative style as a motif of theirs, and this time the character providing the dialogue is speaking directly to the protagonist, rather than speaking about them, as in Bastion.
Everything about this game is incredible. The customization is very in depth - there are plenty of playstyles available. The combat is real time with the addition of the Turn, which is very similar to the turn-based elements incorporated into certain games, most notably the recent Fallout games - you have a set amount of 'time' that can be used for movement or planning attacks/abilities.
If I can posit a criticism its that the game is a little short - I like something I can really sink my teeth into. Also, there are some puzzle-esque elements in the beginning that strangely do not make any appearances afterwards. This seems quite odd and somewhat of a missed opportunity.
Nevertheless, this is a must buy. Go buy it.

Definitely what you'd expect from Supergiant. This game is a lovely little vaunt through their most recent aesthetic. You can expect much of what you got from Bastion, and if you've never played Bastion (how dare you), that simply means that you're getting your money's worth.
The artistic sides of the game are, much like Bastion, its strongest points. The game is absolutely gorgeous, the voice acting is fantastic, and the music is beautiful as well. The gameplay itself could do with a bit of polish, but the combat and customization  systems themselves are innovative, enjoyable and deep.  Encounters will challenge and press you to synergize abilities, and the turn-based strategy elements that have been added to a Diablo-esque combat system give it a tactical depth that it wouldn't have otherwise, turning the game from frantic hack-and-slash to tactical nightmare in the blink of an eye.
All in all, very well done, Supergiant! 9/10, with only one point deducted for a slight lack of polish on the gameplay front, as well as the fact that the game is a bit on the short side.
Absolutley beautiful game with mechanics to match! The story is compelling and keeps you on your toes.

As if their first title, Bastion, wasn't an amazing hit, the fine folks at Supergiant Games found a way to take their shining gem and go a step further. The game carries all the signature qualities that made Bastion a stellar title: gorgeously hand-drawn art, stellar soundtrack, intriguing storytelling, and intuitive gameplay. They took the fluid combat system of Bastion and brought it to the next level by introducing a more strategic take on the combat system and added immense depth to the weapon and ability system. If you loves Bastion, get this game. Even if you haven't, you owe it to yourself to try this.

This is for a pure vanilla run of the game. I can't speak to modded experiences. I intentionally chose vanilla cause I saw my buddy playing this game back when it came out and I myself really wanted to play it as well.
Finally played it and well... It's a very overrated game. It has a lot of great ideas nothing works well, and some of them work against each other.
The game is an open world FPS and works hard to give an open world RPG feel where item management and food management and running quests (you're supposed to use quests to get the good items) help you get the edge on your enemies. Really very excited in concept. The problem is the shooting is bad (even on master difficulty) and the story line is completely uninspiring and full of cliches. The art direction is initially exciting but that falls flat because its more or less all the same. The game becomes a chore. The terrible shooting and strict item management makes the first few hour and a half or so, when your guns are legit bad, punishing. A few hours afterwards you start to feel rewarded, but then the missions become longer fetch quests with more shooting and the facade drops. Your guns aren't bad-- the shooting is bad. The item management punishes and never rewards, and the story is the barest excuse for a long fetch quest.
Which is sad because the game has promise. It isn't enough of an RPG to compete with Fallout 3 and New Vegas. And it isn't anywhere near enough FPS to compete with Metro 2033 and Last Light. There really isn't any reason to play this game vanilla.

If you want a game that is just fun and doesn't take itself too seriously as far as story, then I definitely recommend this game. The gameplay is a lot of fun, provided you have a good imagination, and the story is simple and fun but nothing to write home about. The driving mechanics leave a lot to be desired, however. Some cars feel very wonky and unresponsive at times, but aside from a couple story missions, optional side quests, and the (fun/frustrating) driving challenges, there aren't any reasons to actually drive. Every other aspect of gameplay is fun, the music is fantastic and fits the setting, and you are free to progress through much of the map at will. Unlocking the gear modifications can be a little tedious (depending on the mod you are after) but ultimately very rewarding.
Pros: action, freedom, environmental destruction, gear mods, scenery, EXPLOSIONS!
Cons: Relatively easy, short story, performance (for some), weapon variety.

Playing this game myself.  I can enjoy it, but I can't deny their are flaws to it.
-The story: It's meh, but I"m not sure what to expect at this point.  Sonic Team needs ot decide what they  what do with their cast of characters, cause they felt next to useless to me in this game.  I actually don't mind the other charactes if I can play as them or they show up in game in some way.  Als why put Chaos in there if you're not even gonna use him as a boss?
-Avatar Creator.  This is Sonic Team paying some attention to a big part of the fanbase.  I can't speak for every Sonic fan, but no doubt a vast majority of them have made their own OCs, and this is the first step in tapping deep into that market.  Whether you geneually want a self insert, putting you own OC in, or just gonna meme it up,  GO FOR IT!  That isn't to say it cant be improved upon.  Would prefer a variety of body types, and not locking certain hair styles to certain genders or species.
-Gameplay and Controls:  I won't lie,  This could have been better, but it wasn't bad enough to deter me.  Are the levels short?  A bit yes, but I personally felt it help compliment the theme of speed Sonic is known for.  While I will admit, I wouldn't mind them being about a minute or two longer.  I've heard most complants come from how automated it felt, but which I can sort of agree with, but it doesn't bother me as much.  2D sections aren't as bad for me at least as I  just implimented directional pad controls for them, and analog for 3D sections.  (Not sure everyone has that luxury though.)
-Graphics and design:  Looks pretty, but it the level and enemies can mesh up a bit to annoy the eyes a bit.  I do admit the enemy designs in this one were a bit unispired, and they needed much more variety to them in the future.   What urks me about some levels is not the existence of automations like dash pats and such, but how it just feels so unatural in universe.
Ideas to improve upon.
-Get rid of boost pads and replace with spin dash..  Can't say it will work for sure for Modern Sonic, but Classic had his own unlimited method of getting a kickstart to his speed.  I say merge the spin dash with the boost system.  Also bring back tricks as a way to charge the meter.  From there, it will should be easier to develop more natural level designs.
-No more Classic Sonic:  In 3D Sonic games anyway.  Just keep him 2D  (Both graphically and level based.)  It was good for one game, and that's it.
-Make avatar creator standard.  They don't even need to be in the story.  Just make it so you can play as them in any level, or make levels exclusively for them.
-Impliment the side characters as partners like the avatar was in this game.  Make more branching levels with paths that can be accessed with certain characters and their ablilites.  This can apply to custom characters as well.
Overall, if you like the feel of speed and can distract yourself with a character creator for hours on end,  I would reccommend it., but if you don't like basic controls or expect levels to last more than 3- 5 minutes, then I can't really reccommend it.

This is for a pure vanilla run of the game. I can't speak to modded experiences. I intentionally chose vanilla cause I saw my buddy playing this game back when it came out and I myself really wanted to play it as well.
Finally played it and well... It's a very overrated game. It has a lot of great ideas nothing works well, and some of them work against each other.
The game is an open world FPS and works hard to give an open world RPG feel where item management and food management and running quests (you're supposed to use quests to get the good items) help you get the edge on your enemies. Really very excited in concept. The problem is the shooting is bad (even on master difficulty) and the story line is completely uninspiring and full of cliches. The art direction is initially exciting but that falls flat because its more or less all the same. The game becomes a chore. The terrible shooting and strict item management makes the first few hour and a half or so, when your guns are legit bad, punishing. A few hours afterwards you start to feel rewarded, but then the missions become longer fetch quests with more shooting and the facade drops. Your guns aren't bad-- the shooting is bad. The item management punishes and never rewards, and the story is the barest excuse for a long fetch quest.
Which is sad because the game has promise. It isn't enough of an RPG to compete with Fallout 3 and New Vegas. And it isn't anywhere near enough FPS to compete with Metro 2033 and Last Light. There really isn't any reason to play this game vanilla.

The game that is not a game.
Many games in the Clicker genre are basically just idle mathematics programs which you get to interact with now and again when you are in the mood.  Most of these Clicker games have some objective (to beat monsters or such) and you get to implement decisions on how to spend points to maximize your output so that you can beat increasingly more difficult levels until you decide to reset your game for some added benefit and start all over again with an increased rate of gain.  This game follows suit except for one difference . . . they forgot the GAME part.
Oh you gain money, and can spend money to gain more money at a higher rate, but that is all.  You click on the screen if you want to and you gain money per click based on whatever your current mathematical equation is per click.  And you also gain money at a defined rate based on whatever current mathematical equation you have set up for that.  Then you just wait until you have gained more money and then you pick which mathematical equation to up so that you gain more money at an increased rate.  There are no levels, no objectives other then to have your computer compute, and you sit back and wait or click on the screen to aid your computer in it's computation.  When you have gotten tired of that you can reset your map to start your computer's computations all over with a bonus to how fast it can compute.
There is a map to look at, and in the very begining you can add a few extra graphics to it (you don't get to decide where, they just appear where they are supposed to) and at one point you make the decision to make the map one color or another until you reset your game and can make the choice again.  But pretty soon there is nothing more to add to the map and you have to do all your waiting looking at the same screen.
Now the title is Realm Grinder, but grinding is the act of doing a repetitive task until you can accomplish something.  This isn't a grinder; you aren't working towards anything.  You aren't even working at all.  If you don't want to click, you don't have to, and if you do, so what?  The computer momentarily adjusts its computations to your clicks and that's it.
I know the Clicker genre is not known for it's indepth or immersive storylines, but to forgo any means of an objective at all sure makes the whole process completely pointless.  I know my computer can compute, I hardly need to sit around and watch it do so.

Do you like building a base, and defending it while collecting resources? Then get this game, because this is the best base building game there had been in a long while, if not ever!
It's called Factorio because it's based on the idea of building a factory, but like many RTS games, you have to obtain and manage resources - building one thing that leads to another, and then another, while defending yourself on an alien world.
But it's the way that you go about this that is so compelling about this game, and that's where the factory bit comes in. And basically you are building a factory, a factory where you have to intrically manage the distribution of every resource you collect, there is nothing abstract, you see it all, on conveyerbelts, in storage boxes, in your production machines, or in your personal storage. It is, therefore, a clear, closed logical system, which you have to manage, and where you can see and manipulate every single element.
This is the games strength. More than any other game I have played, it satisfies the itch to manage a logistical system, and make it as efficient and beautiful as you possibly can. Add to that the fact that you have to defend this againt hostile creatures, and integrate a system to do this into your base, and you have a very satisfying and addictive game.
The game includes:
* Tech tree - you have to make the resources for research
* Walls, turrets and gates
* A railroad system for getting resources from outposts, including signals and schedules! You can get in the trains!!
* Total control over the layout of a massive system of conveyorbelts
* Automated systems of stock control and resource distribution
* Direct fuel, electricity, and solar power
* Combat, featuring self-powered armour and portable shield and lasers
* There's even a logic circuit system in the game that you can use to do pretty much anything
* So much more it would take pages to describe
There is no better game for designing a system of bases to manage resources and achieve goals while integrating a defense system, not that I know of anyway, and I have played most of them. If you like RTS or resource management games at all, this one is a no brainer. It's got the highest ever Steam rating for a reason - it's that good!
Oh and the fact that it's in Alpha is a red herring, there is more to enjoy here than most completed games (absolutely no exaggeration), and I have never had a crash or seen a bug once.
Buy it!

Before buying Dark Souls 2 on the 2014 holiday sale I had been very very skeptical of the third entry in the souls franchise for a number of reasons.  People were saying that the bosses were too easy, the game was unfair, and that it just wasn't as well designed as Dark souls 1.  Being a huge fan of the souls series, this got me worried.  Well I feel that after 20 hours of the game I can say with confidence that this game is still just as awesome as its predecesor.  While the games level design doesn't seem as solid as it was in DS1 it is still excelent and the enemy design actually seems a bit better.  The bosses are infact pretty easy (I've yet to die to a single boss more than once if at all) which is disapointing to say the least but that is more than made up for by the games multiplayer aspects.  The main draw for me so far in DS2 is the PvP and Co-Op.  The PvP is extremely solid and much less buggy than the PvP in DS1, there is a very active community, and the huge variety of weapons keeps it interesting.
Now there are some down sides.  No game is perfect and DS2 proves that gloriously with it's forst few hours of gameplay.  Coming from DS1 I was infuriated by the updated controlls, new rolling, and steeper learning curve.  While the steep learning curve is to be expected and I did eventually get used to the new movement system, there has been an issue that has been bugging me.  They still haven't fixed the damn lock-on mechanics so that they don't get you killed 7/10 times, this has been a persistant issue in all souls games that I was really hoping to see a loution for.  On to the multiplayer, all I can say is HaCkErS.  Some people go through the game without ever seeing a single hacker, for others it completely ruins the game.  Just know that some people hack the game to have infinite Health, Stamina, Poise, and Damage.  If you encounter someone like this just know that not everyone is like that and you can report them.  From what I've heard the developers, FromSoftware are cracking down on hackers and issuing bans on accounts that have been proven hacking.
Finally It would be nice if I addressed the fact that this game is HARD!  It's harder than DS1 in most places and that is great! But if that scares you enough to not get the game then just remember that the game is only as hard as you make it.  If you choose to make a really weird, useless build then its going to be tough as nails.  But focus on one archetype for your character (like a Paladin, cleric, theif, etc.) and all of a sudden the game will become much easier.
In conclusion I'd say that this game is absolutely worth every penny of its price tag, its a great game and a worthy sequal to the original Dark Souls.  I give it a 9/10
EDIT-- I forgot to mention the "Scholar of the first sin" edition which is set to be released in April.  It's unfortunate that the whole playerbase is going to be split between the two releases so I'd say if you're going to buy it but you've missed any sales then wait till april and buy the new version.  It sucks that people who just bought the game are getting screwed over but if you can get it on sale just remember that we are getting a patch that has everything from the nw version minus some updated graphics and the ability to have 6 people in one world.  New score would have to be 8/10

This game is a rollerocaster...
Some people have played this and come away seething with anger at how bad they feel it is, I don't get that but I can understand why they don't like this game. I'll try to break down my thoughts into categories because oh boy this is gonna be longer than the game itself is.
AVATAR CREATION
There's quite a few options and while the customisation options for clothing and accessories is limited at the start you very quickly amass many options. I personally quite enjoyed it but it isn't for everyone. You will get out of it what put in, in a manner of speaking if you take it seriously (well as much as you can) then it's quite good and I find it add to the experience well (when your character is around) Or if you just want to make "abomination the dear god why" then you can do that as well for a good laugh untill you have to keep seeing those nightmare eyes. One issue I do have with it is that your character never speaks and it's really jarring.
THE STORY
This game has a larger focus on story than previous sonic titles I have played and I actually do enjoy this but the actual story itself leaves a lot to be desired even for a sonic game. I get that it needs to be kid friendly becasue kids make up a fair portion of the fanbase but I'm certain even a child will find the story... just bad. I won't go into the details to avoid spoiling it but the Infinite, the main villain has a really stupid and unexplained origin even though the whole point of the episode shadow DLC is basically to explain the origin of infinite, but it doesn't even manage that well.
Another glaring issue is that other than Infinite there is never any threat, tension or feeling of danger at all. For example near the end of the game Sonic and your player character get sucked into a portal made by the phantom ruby to a place called null space. Then 5 seconds later you have escaped and sonic shrugs it off like nothing happened, he even makes a joke that litterally nothing happened (get it null space - nothing)... yeah it's about that funny in game as well. This isn't an isolated incident either. It happens all throughtout the story.
Another issue I have witht he story is how utterly useless tails is. All he does is put out his ipad not have anything usefull to add to the situations he is in and constantly whine and mope about needing sonic. Eggman shows up, he needs sonic, chaos shows up, he needs sonic, he forgets his password for his ipad, he needs sonic, he forgets how to eat food, he needs sonic. It's actually insulting how much of wet blanket he is when back in the day he was just as competent as any other character but now he wets himself at the first sign of any kind of danger.
THE GAMEPLAY
I'll break this down futher to explain in better detail where this goes wrong but let me tell you right now none of this is that good.
CLASSIC SONIC
First of all, Classic Sonic is the worst part of this game. In Generations classic sonic felt good, play comfortably and his levels felt fun to play through. In Forces classic sonic feels "off" I can;t describe it but it's not smooth or comfortable it's just clunky and he drops like he is made of lead. Also for some inexplicable reason to spin "attack" as it now called for no bloody reason) you have to be stood stock still and hold down and press jump no more holding X like in generations. Why have fun flowing movement to make playing a game fun lets just make it clunky and unintuitive. His levels are poorly designed also. You have parts where you have what look to be bottomless pits but are actually where you need to go and times when the same is actually a bottomless pit. It's infuriating and onthe level casino forest I spent ages fighting the stupid level gimick and the wonky physics just trying to escape a load of bumpers layed out in what was basically a trap endlessly bouncing sonic around until the physics would finally allow him to land on the correct side of a bumper to progress... 3 or 4 times in a row. It took over 20 seconds, which doesn't sound that long but the longest level in this entire game is less than 3 minutes long.
MODERN SONIC
Moden Sonics levels are very linear in "3D" sections, are very automated and you spend most of the time just watching the game play itself. Then you get to 2D sections and you have to fight the strange acceleration/momentum, awkward jumping mechanics that worked better in Colours and it just a bad time. You just spend most of your time holding X and very rarely you press A a few times.
AVATAR LEVELS
These are actually some of the best levels, they are similar to the modernsonic levels but you have the advantage of having different wisp powers to your advantage. Depending on which wisp you equip on your character you can have different powers available to you which open up different ways to navigate parts of levels. The homing attack on the Players OC is slower that sonics, much slower which must have been to incentivice the player to use the wispon to defeat enemies. The wispon is by far the best way to defeat enemies but some are just useless in combat. The end boss took 3x as long as it should have done because I basically had the wrong weapon equiped and it actually couldn't even hurt him leaving me to rely on the useless and boring "wire attack" (homing attack).
THE LEVELS
Most levels can be completed in between 1 minute and 3 minutes. It's kind of baffling how short the levels are. Also most levels either have an over abundance of automation so you actually play very little of them or they rely too much on the awful 2d platforming and are unreasonably frustrating because the platforming is really really really really bad. Again it's baffling because in Generation (FROM OVER 5 YEARS AGO) platforming was prett great, but here it's BAD. It's scary how badly this game has regressed from past titles. Basically Generations did it's level way better and longer than this games' levels and I don't understand. Did they playtest this game solely on kids with ADHD who also have a hard time grasping any kind of motor control other than holding X or letting it go to occasionally press A? I don't want to be offensive with that question but I do gueninely need to know because it is such a regression in terms of level design and gameplay.
THE GRAPHICS
This game has quite nice graphics for the most part. The UI is actually really nice, when you aren't rushing though a level it can look quite nice... but dear god the actual levels, when you are playing them, visually are a mess. There are times when you are holding X to boost and there is so much clutter and visual noise you can't see the level, you can't see where you are going it's just a mess and you hope that it just automates the next bit so you don't die to a hazard you can't see... and that's what happens nearly every time.
THE SOUNTRACK
Nornally Sonic games have great sountracks but this one is pretty bad. The main couple of themes are pretty great, fistbump and infinites themes are pretty good but the actual levels they're pretty bad. They are either bland and boring or in the case of classic sonic and the avatar they are just plain awful. The avatar has obnoxious vocal songs that you can't make out properly but they are not nice to listen to. Classic Sonic.. I don't even know, they tried to make them sound retro but it just feels hollow and soulless. Luckily the levels are so short you won't listen to any song for very long. I miss the old days where you would be humming the song from a level you enjoyed for days afterwards and it just wouldn't get out of your head but you didn't because it was actually good...
FINAL THOUGHTS
Ok, I know I just spent all that time complaining about everything but for the most part I actually enjoying most of this game. It's not that great, if you want a good modern sonic game get Generations, it's just better, in everyway. I'd go on but I've run out of space.. I give this game a 6/10.

Highly recommend for fans of mythology, this has one of the most comprehensive and still somewhat accurate representations of pantheons in a mainstream game. Plenty of interesting god lore and character archetypes to relate to. One of the cool things is that after thousands of years of human history, many of the mythological figures can still be relateable to a modern person.
- Do you want to be a primordial fatherly rock god, shaking the ground, shielding your subjects, pushing away the unworthy and bringing foes to their knees? For feminists, there is now a female mother god version as well.
- An arrogant god of music with a rockstar attitude, looking down on your fans below, sniping both foes and maidens' hearts with beams of light from your fingers?
- A sweet, sensitive, sort of shy girl who used to lock herself in her cave because the world was too much to bear. Friends cheered her up with a party, and now she's the sun goddess leading the charge, smiting foes with divine light.
- A spiteful ex-wife, simply searching for her husband. Who coincidentally is also now a zombie terrorizing the land of the living? Oh and she can turn invisible...
- Star-crossed lovers. Him, the legendary hero of mankind who shot down the evil suns. Her, an unwilling immortal stuck on the moon, patiently waiting for his return. Literally a world apart, unable to reunite because of a cruel twist of fate. Also now strangely fighting each other in a brutal deathmatch for the fate of the world.
On top of all of that, SMITE is pretty unique, being one of the first MOBAS with a 3rd person view. It brings together the builds and strategic team play of LoL/Dota with the a much more immersive camera view and aim-dependent mechanics similar to PVP action MMORPGs.

Edit: Valve, you really need to fix this review submission system. I can only submit short reviews right now and need to edit to get them longer.
Contrary to the game's description, this is not really a survival game. Sure, the goal is not to die, but that is true of a very large number of games. What this game actually is is a highly scripted stealth action fps horror game which often plays like a groundhog day nightmare (die a horrible death, but learn where enemies are so you can hopefully get a little farther before dying again).
With that out of the way, I want to say that I wanted to like this game. Being able to explore a space station is a lot of fun, and the metroidvania item progression to unlock new parts of the station had a lot of potential. Unfortunately, this game does have some major issues that ultimately shifted my perception away from fun to annoyance by the time I was done with the game.
First off, the good points. The atmosphere is perfect for an Aliens game, and the (somewhat) freeform Metroidvania exploration was a nice touch where getting new items would unlock new areas to explore. You have guns, but are heavily incentivized to use stealth due to the severely limited ammo and not wanting to attract attention.
Now (unfortunately) to the bad points. Note that I was playing on Novice in hopes of minimizing these so take into account that they will be exacerbated on higher difficulties.
The checkpoint saving system is a PITA. When there are many things that can very quickly kill you, and the heavy stealth focus making for often slow progress, it can easily be 15-20 minutes between checkpoints (even taking into account backtracking to find one). Deaths mean a significant time loss and significantly contributed to my annoyance. The amount of time you stand starting blankly at the save points watching the lights is also completely unnecessary.
Guns are in desperate need of a rebalance. The first gun you get (the revolver) is so pathetically weak (even on novice) and takes so long to reload as to be essentially useless. Either it needed to be significantly more powerful or should have been replaced with a semi-auto pistol with larger clips and faster reloads. The flamethrower goes through fuel too quickly (unless you think a quick half-second burst should use a full liter of fuel) but at least ammo is relatively plentiful in spite of that annoyance. The shotgun has way too loose of a spead (this unfortunately is a sin propogated by far too many shooters) and the bolt gun has too large of a reticle so it's only useful at shotgun ranges anyways. Pipe bombs aren't considered weapons by the weapon scanners (there's a mission where you have to leave your guns behind) but are by far the most powerful means of killing things in the game. Plus, the materials to build them are much more common than ammo.
The battery eating flashlight trope seriously needs to die. Even in the relatively power hungry flashlights of years past they lasted significantly longer than they do in this (and far to many other) games. Flashlight use is discouraged enough as is with the extra attention it draws. At least there's only a handful of places in the game that are actually dark enough to need the flashlight.
Quicktime events and minigames add nothing to games like this and only serve to add another layer of annoyance, forcing you to master a pesky little timed button pushing game that adds no real content. A lot of AAA games from this era did this unfortunately, hopefully they got enough negative feedback to convince the devs not to include it so much in future titles. The computer terminals and rewires don't pause the game and lock you in while using them with no quick way out, so it's very easy to die even if you hear an enemy coming up behind you. When you do abort, you completely log out so it takes a significant amount of time to get back in if you managed to survive being interrupted.
The AI can be very inconsistent. Sometimes they're completely oblivious to your presence, other times they see you from what seems like a mile away. All the enemies exhibit this behavior. The alien has the ability to teleport to your location and randomly appear out of nowhere, killing you so often that it ceases to be scary and simply becomes aggravating.
The scripted events are also quite annoying. There are quite a few scripted events that drag you out of control (or simply are abused to provide a cheap jump scare that you'll be numb to by the end) and put you on a sometimes lengthy detour that doesn't really add anything. The entire ending sequence (between extending the maintence platform and releasing the clamps is a prime example of this, and felt entirely unnecessary.
Normally I applaud a game for having lots of content provided I'm having fun, but this game overall felt like it had overstayed its welcome by the end and did not need to be as long as it was. The Metroidvania elements were ultimately wasted by the end since there wasn't really an indication of when it would be a good time to go back and visit the rooms I couldn't get into before, and now that I've been annoyed I'm not about to go back and replay to go find everything.
Overall, not a bad game per se, but definitely needed another rebalance and editing pass. It's a decent stealth horror game so pick it up on sale if you like those types of games or are an Aliens fan, otherwise stay away. Not really worth the full asking price IMHO.

Awesome game and so far an unreached experience.
You get solid shooter mechanics mixed up with some RPG elements (inventory system/attributes/effects like radiation or bleeding/"Magical" boni of the artifacts) set in alternative reality after the chernobyl accident.
Some people may argue that the graphics are too brown-in-brown, even for the scenario, but for the time you need to play through the game, you won't be bothered by this (as compared to a MMO/MP-FPS or something else you invest more time in). After all, it supports the scenario and mood of a nuclear shi*hole in which everybody wants either eat you, or steal your gear and artifacts.
Encounters with other stalkers/bandits/soldiers/etc. are challenging and the open areas give you plenty of opportunities to approach situations. Mutants and anomalies are interesting and need their own tactics to approach and sometimes gear (e.g. Armor against the mutants claws or a radiation suit for preventing your brain cells to cook while walking through an anomaly). You often encounter them in dark areas, often underground, which delivers a classy "horror-jumpscare"-atmosphere and makes listening to steps and the use of a flashlight relevant.
The time I played it on steam (33+ hours) was 1 play-through (not the first, I bought the boxed version earlier), but you need to be the same  hoarder and explorer to invest that much time. Hoarding can be a thing in this game, since the inventory/weapon system give you many opportunities to spent too much time in the inventory screen. E.g. you can(/have to) rightclick a weapon to unload the ammo left in it, so that players like me end up clearing all those noob-AKs because you want ALL-DA-AMMO for your fancy custom AK.
Further the items are plentyfull and you can always find special, unique custom builds of base weapons (alternative caliber, suppressd variant you normally can't build by yourself, etc.) which makes exploring rewarding. The game gives you a little too many items to sell and therefore money, but the question "which gear to pack for the next area" still make you think twice before grabbing the stat-wise best gun.
These systems combined with the level layout definitely give the game some of the survival elements a modern days "DayZ" or any of his clones desperetaly try to implement.
To people who don't know which game of the STALKER series to get:
This one is the original idea the engine is meant to support, and you feel that. The newest part, "Call of Pripyat", wants to be more open world than the original design based on smaller "area-islands" with loading screens in between, but the scripts often trigger fights before you can reach them and force you to detour through the same areas more often, which feels dull after a time.
So compared to Call of Pripyat, this is the more straight forward game and in my view the better Stalker experience for people new to the series.
I can't speak for the middle child, "Clear sky" as it won't let me play further than the intro level :D
It's hated for being buggy and having a stupid quest/faction design, but i really can't speak for or against it. I know that it's possible to run it with some tweaks, but i didn't feel like investing the time yet. If you can get all 3 games in a bundle, go for that since it is not much more expensive in a sale and you can choose which one fits your long term playstile best.
Technically, all 3 Stalker games are on the same level. The graphics and animations transport the gameplay elements and the mood perfectly, but it's clearly dated. I recommend getting mods/patches or tweak it yourself to extend the field of view, as that hurts modern FPS gamers eyes (except the tunnel-vision cod players). Who wants to go further or really can't stand the brown look, there are enough gameplay and graphic-mods out there to adjust the experience.
Have fun playing !
