Tree of Savior is what you expect. A true successor of the so called Ragnarok Online. For this review, I'll be writing on paragraphs divided by pros and cons. I played through ICBT, so I can tell a lot from my point of view.
Pros:
ToS has a huge amount of options for classes. Large variety of classes and combinations that will most likely suit what kind of class you want best. The adventure is long and grindy, but it's always enjoyable, especially with friends, as you wander around a world masterpiece. The game is very deep too, the level cap is more than 200. The mechanics are mostly Keyboard / Controller based; hitting the enemies are manual. Positioning and tactics matter a lot. Attacks deal in an AoE. It's a step up from Ragnarok's combat mechanics mostly. If you want to go back to the ol' times of MMORPG, ToS is for you.
Cons:
The biggest problem I have with ToS at the current state is poor optimization. It's said that even the high-end users find the performance to be worse than it should be. For low-end users, crashes are very common due to instability. Everyone should have a stable 60 FPS for high-end PC, and 30 FPS for low-end PC.
Also, the story is linear although more variety. You either start from Klaipeda or Orsha, but both are linear in nature.
If you don't want to grind, no, this game is not for you.
Verdict:
7/10. As long as the optimization issue is not fixed, I cannot give this game a high score just yet. I really hope they will fix this up in the near future. It's worth giving a try either way, though :)

S.T.A.L.K.E.R.:SoC is the Dark Souls of the FPS genre. Some will love it, some will hate it. I keep deleting what I'm saying, so I'll just bullet point pros and cons.
PROS:
-Brilliant setting: Chernobyl has been a place I have wanted to visit for a long time. It is essentially a place on earth that has been frozen in time, and the ability to explore it can be extremely immersive at times. Pripyat in particular offers amazing urban combat, allowing you to snipe from windows in high apartment buildings or taking the fight to the irradiated alleyways of the city.
-White-knuckle tension: SoC has the ability to literally keep you on the edge of your seat at times, especially underground areas where light is dim and monsters lurk in the shadows. You will have to memorize enemy movements and behavior to get through certain areas in one piece. Blowouts/emissions will keep you on your toes as well, which are massive releases of radiation that will require you to make your way to shelter as quickly as you can, or die.
-Active modding community: The devs of this game made sure to make the game files accessible from a modding perspective. I'm currently playing through using a mod called "Autumn Aurora" which improves almost all aspects of the game, and ENB, to make the shadows darker and lighting more contrasted. Many other mods exist that enhance the difficulty, add areas, and create entirely new experiences.
-Beautiful visuals: First off, I agree that the game has not aged in the best way, but some aspects of the visuals still look better that some AAA games today, especially the lighting system. Visual mods go a long way in improving the textures, flora and fauna as well. The setting, while bleak and rainy most of the time, will occasionally show off on a sunny day, creating beauty in a dangerous world where death lurks around every corner.
-Fantastic gunplay: SoC is unforgiving at times, but in the majority of cases, it will be due to your own error. To counter this, the game offers great shooting mechanics, including ricochets, bullet trajectory, and penetration. A wide (but not too wide) selection of weaponry allows each gun to have a specific feel and personality, which makes choosing which to pick up and which to drop very important.
-Challenge and difficulty: PLAY ON MASTER. I cannot stress this enough. Difficulty and overcoming it is what makes the STALKER series so great. It makes victory that much more rewarding. Play smart and carefully, and Master difficulty is beatable on a first playthrough.
-Sound: The sound design in SoC is unique and fits the setting like a glove. The beeps of your PDA, the wind rustling in the trees, your geiger counter warning you of nearby radiation, and enemies spewing insults to you in Russian during firefights all add to a wonderful (and terrifying) sense of immersion.
CONS
Story: The STALKER franchise does not rely on it's narrative to tell the story, which to some, may seem like a terrible mistake. It depends on what you look for in games. I believe that the setting tells it's own story, but you may disagree. I love a good story, but in SoC's case I believe that certain gameplay elements make up for the weak storyline. I should also mention that my game is in Russian, which makes comprehension quite difficult for myself, a native English speaker.
Animations: Reload and NPC animations can be a bit strange looking at times. It's entirely possible that the game was created without motion capture due to a lack of resources, which can take you out of the experience at some points. Several mods, however, attempt to improve these faults. A very promising mod called "Gunslinger" is being released soon for STALKER: Call of Pripyat, which vastly improves all animations. Worth taking a look.
Linearity: While the game does offer quite a large area in total to explore, it can sometimes feel linear. Radiation pockets and anomalies keep you mostly on the roads or in towns, cutting quite a bit of forest out from exploring. However, the forests in the real Chernobyl are some of the most irradiated in the world, so it does make sense. Take that as you will.
That's all I can really think of. If you see this game on sale, make sure to grab it while it's cheap. It truly is a wonderful experience overall.

Where do I start with this game? I've played through it twice and am currently on my third play through after beating the trilogy a few years ago. I downloaded the STALKER Complete 2009 mod which I hoped would refresh the game without introducing stupid gameplay imbalances. I was right. It's still one of the greatest and most demanding open-world first person role playing games out there. And I think I would be justified in saying that it on its own rivals the AAA competitors like Fallout 3 or New Vegas. It's just that good.
It plays really nicely, and because it's such an old game it runs smoothly with high anti-aliasing and high frame rates. As a core game you are sort of thrown into the combat with little preparation, but it doesn't take an experienced shooter-player to realize that you need to duck and cover. Leaning is super important, and enemies like to shoot when you move forcing you to play patiently and not go commando. That being said, once you get the formula down, you just sit and pop enemies when they poke their heads out. Pretty standard. The real challenge is fighting monsters which will scare the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you and really put your twitch-shooter skills to the test. Interacting with friendlies and setting out on quests is easy enough, but oftentimes the quests will end in ways you don't expect due to the uncertain nature of everything occurring in the game-world. You plan an ambush with some buddies and only you made it out? That's your fault but you gotta move on.
The Complete 2009 mod really polishes off the game nicely. Textures are still pretty sharp, and the world is brimming with anomalies and enemies. You really notice the subtle touches like rain pouring outside and forcing friendlies to huddle inside next to barrel stoves. The sound is good but definitely dated. I really like having to use directional sound to orient myself and in a game like this that feature really stands out. The day-night cycles are intense and I found myself sleeping through the nights so as to have a daylight advantage in combat.
The story is super intriguing and really enhanced by the dark and radioactive atmosphere. Everything could be dangerous and you gotta be on your game if you want to make it out alive. What's awesome is that you can play this game multiple times and get fairly different experiences in terms of the narrative and your late-game character's attributes. Some people go full ecologist and collect anomalies to enhance their character. Some seek the best guns ever. Some have the best armor. It's all pretty standard for the genre, but it is executed well and provides a player with a large range of choices to make throughout the story.
Addendum: So I beat it after reloading a quick save every 15 minutes because holy ♥♥♥♥ the monolith stalkers really throw everything in the game at you including gunships, mutants, armor piercing ammunition, and their sheer numbers (I killed maybe 40 in the last part of the game?). I don't want to spoil the ending so I won't, but I will address the "incoherence" some people claim the game's story is guilty of. I am pretty sure that the curators that made that claim were either skipping through all the dialogue, or just refuse to acknowledge that a team of devs outside of the United States can make a compelling, unique, and deeply original story. Or maybe game journalists are all ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I think that's most likely.
This game is not appealing to the same crowds that find the Fallout or Metro games appealing, and I think that the reason for that is in the fantasies and idealized situations the game constructs for the player. It really does give you the sensation of being inna woods with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ soviet guns that jam all the time fighting hostile creatures and violently entrepreneurial bandits. You also get the neat sensation of collecting artifacts for science, and doing so under the constant oppression of the military and rival paramilitary factions that seemingly have no scientific aims. While in this debut title, there is no explicit faction-joining for the player, you do participate and witness the war for these radioactive artifacts, and it absolutely informs your player-choices that do in fact yield wildly different endings to the game--bad endings if you're a lazy and stupid player that doesn't read dialogue. I have beaten this game 3 times now I think? I'll never be able to eat ♥♥♥♥♥♥ spam knock-offs again without thinking about my misadventures in the zone scrounging for artifacts, assassinating corrupt military commanders and bandits, and drinking a dozen handles of vodka to make the radiation sickness go away.
If you're intrigued play it and get hooked and maybe you'll pick up Clear Sky and Call of Pripyat which I'll review at some point.

In this game, you stamp passports.  EXCITING!  But don't let the mundane description fool you: the game is a masterpiece in it's own right.
Papers, Please is a testament to how dated graphics and a simplistic core element can be used as a vehicle for a rich experience by implementing the power of choice.  Each person, every randomly generated life you come across, awaits your stamp of Approval or Denial.  Their minor reactions feed the player's psyche to continue the grind, checking papers and comparing photos, cross-referencing lists for potential criminals or fraudulent seals, churning out dozens of people to feed his or her faceless, nameless "Family".
Abusing your power or neglecting your duties don't result in an immediate game over, instead you receive citations in increasing severity based on how problematic the offense was.  Decorated the applicant side of your immigration booth with nonsense?  If your boss sees it, you get fined, but you can always hide the drawings of "Son" underneath official papers during inspections, then put them back up later.
The game rapidly escalates in difficulty, but decreases in reward and intrigue, allowing the player to merge seamlessly from a "game" with a clear carrot-and-stick bait, to an experience where I actually questioned whether or not this was designed as gameification of the career to attract, immerse and train border agents in the process, and exemplify the tribulations and  consequences of those choices.

This game honestly surprised me. I, myself am not a free to play type of person, in fact I think most, 90% of free-to-plays are absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥designed to try and suck money out of me. Not this one, this is up there in some of my favorite f2p games, and yes, I'll admit, this game isn't without it's flaws but it's one game that has semi changed my opinion on Free-to-Play.
Let me start with the good, for a Source Game, an engine of 10+ years, this game looks great, apart from zombies looking like they came out of a low budget B-movie horror flick and the no texture bug which appears on the eyes of some characters (I laugh this one away and think of it as an intended bug for immersion) it's pretty good. In some of the settings, they've hidden away a few graphics options that are experimental such as Lens Flare but is worth enabling. NMRiH really immerses you into the thought that you are a survivor and must get through this with it's graphics, the vanilla maps have been designed very well for immersion in mind. The lighting creates this bleak atmosphere that not many other Survival Horror games create, Left 4 Dead (yes the lighting is still very good but not like NMRiH in any way), DayZ to name a few. It keeps to a certain design framework that really wants to keep you immersed and constantly on alert as every dark corner there may be undead lurking. It emphases the use of Flashlights which are possibly one of the best utilities seen in any game I've played.
Away from the Atmosphere and the Graphics, the combat matches this very well. Ammo for guns is rare, something that really does fit a realistic scenario of such a thing happening and it requires you to make every shot count. Melee combat is interesting too as it has an invisible stamina meter, requiring you to time your swings and make every bit of your energy count. Weapons like Sledgehammers, FUBARs and Shovels drain it more but with the chance of one hit kills and possibly killing multiple zombies, other weapons, like Machetes, Hatchets, don't do as much damage but use little stamina, keeping you on in the fight. That moves me onto the next great thing about this game, the variety of weapons and how they each have a destined purpose. Pistols are great, they're all different and have their own specialties. The Beretta M9 is a 9mm Pistol and the ammo is rather common, it's a 2 hit kill and my favorite pistol due to the sights being better than that of the other 9mm, the Glock 17 which has a larger ammo capacity but worse sights, again in my opinion. Weapons are so varied with it's uses that they're all worth trying to match your game style. Would you like to pick up the M16 or would you rather take a more recyclable approach with a Compound Bow.
Other mechanics in this game away from combat is the ability to become infected and must be warded off with Phlanx Pills (a reference to one of my all time favorite novels by Max Brookes - World War Z) or Gene Therapy, which completely cures you. You can barricade entrances with a claw hammer and some wooden planks, end your teammates (or yourself) to rid them of the burden that may encumber you later in game and more. You can even change your character and his voice. I'm not going to go much more in detail with the other mechanics, these are the best ones, so you'll have to encounter some of the other ones in game yourself.
This section is dedicated to the AI and the Level Design. I'm not gonna lie, the AI really needs patching up, it's ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and needs some work. However it's predictable and unpredictable nature (yes the AI is both) keep you on constant alert. An infected teammate has gone down, where the hell could he be? Well he's glitched out running in circles around where you turned. That's one major issue with the game. Away from AI, the levels are really good. If you're playing slowly, they can sometimes take up to 30 minutes to complete and can be quite the blast if you're last man standing. The maps, each and every one of them are unique and require different objectives and many of them have different paths for different playthroughs. Not major though, but something to change up gameplay each time.
All in all NMRiH is a great F2P game, a slightly cancerous community as I've encountered many annoying little kids in my mere 30 hours of gameplay but overall pretty damn good. 8/10.

The original 1979 Alien movie is one of my favourite movies of all time and because of that I've played pretty much every Alien themed game released, including buying a 2nd hand Atari Jaguar to play Alien vs Predator on that.
For me, none of those games captured the feel of the Alien mythos. Now we finally get the game the Alien universe deserves.
The developers apparently had full access the the original movie resources and it shows, the graphics and audio are spot on.
The story line is interesting and follows on nicely from the movie. I actually sat and played for four or five hours on the first day of play and could have easily done more if real life hadn't pulled me away. There is a palpable feeling of dread and I found myself slowly leaning into my monitor as the tension ramped up and literally jumped in my chair on several occasions. The AI works well and the Alien is fantastic, it really feels like it's a living organism hunting you down if you give your position away.
I wholeheartedly recommend this game whether you''re an Alien fan, a stealth game fan or both.

The Elder Scrolls Online is the only MMORPG based around Bethesda's Elder Scrolls Lore and despite being a first under the flagship of Zenimax Online and having a very rocky start Tamriel Unlimited definitely makes this game the game that it was meant to be.
Gone are the days of needing to subscribe to play and gone are the days of different alliance players being unable to play together, if you see Angry Joe's review on YouTube for this game, I would rarely say this but disregard it. About 90% you can disregard as Tamriel Unlimited fixed many of those negatives it once had at release.
Currently there are two version available for purchase, the regular Tamriel Unlimited and the Gold Edition, I would highly recommend you purchase the Gold Edition as it comes with almost all of the DLC that is essential to making this game feel more like an Elder Scrolls game and it has some nice neat little addons to it too to make your experience more fluid.
Pros and Cons
Pros:
-Solid MMORPG Experience
-Decent Community
-Fun PVP (Cyrodiil Only and when done right)
-Accessible to all skill levels (No Steep Learning Curve)
-All Characters Fully Voice-Acted by Talented Voice Actors
-Immersive Main and Alliance Stories
-Nearly all of the Provinces Represented (Save for Elsweyr - Sorry Khajiits...:()
-Very Easy to make some Good Builds if you just take the 5 mins to look it up
-No Pay to Win formula
-You do not need to Subscribe for the game to feel "whole"
-Can have addons to slightly mod and tailor the game experience to make it easier for you
-All of the typical Elder Scrolls Skills are there, combat and even noncombat (crafting)
Cons:
-Imperial Race is still locked off even with Gold Edition, you'll need to pay an extra $10-$15 to Unlock it -.-
-You need to Pay to have the ability to play with any race in any Alliance (Character Creation)
-Some Side Quests can feel grindy
-Dungeoneering is as expected grindy but if you like that, then it's great
-You can get wrecked at PVP if you didn't build your Character up right but PVP and Cyrodiil are not essential
-Not ALL of Tamriel is available to explore, 35% of Skyrim is available, 50% of Morrowind, 20% of Black Marsh, none of Elsweyr, 40% of Summerset Isles, 10% of Hammerfell but all of High Rock, Valenwood and Cyrodiil* (*If you dare to explore with PVPers lurking about*) is accessible to explore
-If you live in South America you have no dedicated Servers...so have fun with High Ping trying to connect to North American Servers...sorry :(
All in all:
It's a solid MMORPG with a pretty strong population Steam side and a helpful community, the gameplay is fun, combat is fun, questing is fun none of the side quests feel boring and it still has a very strong Elder Scrolls feel to it, for those who are new to MMORPGs coming from ESV: Skyrim or older you may feel like it is not up to par but for those who have played both RPGs and MMORPGs and love the Elder Scrolls Universe this is the game for you. 8/10.

This is not "Skyrim online" or "Skyrim 2", it takes place 1000 years before skyrim. The lore is great, loot is great, quests are great, I can never be bored playing this epic game. I would highly recommend it to any mmo gamer or elder scrolls fan.

‘Transistor’ can only be described as a jazzy composition, seductive and melancholic. I felt as if a tenor sax was played before me.
This performance does not hold any punches. From the get go it launches you into the game. No hand holding, it respects your intelligence as you begin to explore the world.
Gameplay is reminiscent of Supergiant Games’ 'Bastion'. Isometric view and action packed, but what this brings is a more matured and well thought out experience. Aside from the obvious action orientated combat system, it allows for RPG elements to take hold. A plan of action can be devised, by using this new feature the player can plan a method of attack utilizing and maximizing on his carefully customized skills.
The average time to complete this game is around 5 hours. Calculating the cost per minute of entertainment, it would be like buying an average movie ticket (being generous I assumed for a 2 hour length film for $7.96) for each minute one interacts with the game. It comes to a total of $19.90, and that is if you only play it once.
If you need to save money, then wait.
Hell, just watch a play through if you just want to consume the basic story. Though, I think you may get more out of it by actually playing it yourself.
I stand by my purchase, and highly recommend this game.

This game is not Ragnarok Online.  With this statement out of the way, the rest of the review.
+ Beautiful graphics and style.
+ Diverse classes.
+ New IP.  Not a reboot or continuation.
+ Characters can jump on things and up buildings.
- Combat system is what it is.  You will like or dislike it.
x Cannot trade without the use of pay-tokens.  At the time of this review, one is capped to 30 token-enabled trades a month.
x If not using a pay-token, Market/Auction place only allows one item up at a time.  30% tax on sold item.
x Linear progression.
x No open world.  Exploring is done through quest markers- not your own free will.
______
I was greatly looking forward to Tree of Savior for years.  Disappointed to see that the game became a linear coaster.  Even more disappointed seeing that player to player trade, one of the most fundamental features of a MMO, has been required the use of pay tokens.  The reasoning is that this will deter bots from entering the game.  Black Desert Online EU-server has done this, and their worldchat is still flooded with advertisers.  Surprise, surprise, look what is happening.  Surely, in all their infinite wisdom, there must be some smart programmer out there who can create a way to identify and neutralize these botters without infringing a necessary human component of a social experience?  Oh wait, creating a system like that would cost money.  Why spend that?
I still feel this game has a lot of fun for players, but cannot recommend ToS for executing this emerging, bad industry practice.  Price was not a concern for me-- if the game was monthly-sub or buy-to-play, no complaints.  If MMO features are going to be removed, why keep it a MMO?  Why not just make it a co-op game with focus?  The simple answer is, "Will not make as much money as Nexon Cashshop MMO".
I'm confident the game will do well and find its audience.  Numbers will be fantastic when F2P launches.  No crashing and burning like other AAA disasters.  The playing community's culture will grow with the game and create wonderful artwork.  To all who play, especially the younger players; I hope you have as much fun with this as my friends and I did with RO.  Put your smile into the game and make it the best game on the internet.

S.T.A.L.K.E.R.:SoC is the Dark Souls of the FPS genre. Some will love it, some will hate it. I keep deleting what I'm saying, so I'll just bullet point pros and cons.
PROS:
-Brilliant setting: Chernobyl has been a place I have wanted to visit for a long time. It is essentially a place on earth that has been frozen in time, and the ability to explore it can be extremely immersive at times. Pripyat in particular offers amazing urban combat, allowing you to snipe from windows in high apartment buildings or taking the fight to the irradiated alleyways of the city.
-White-knuckle tension: SoC has the ability to literally keep you on the edge of your seat at times, especially underground areas where light is dim and monsters lurk in the shadows. You will have to memorize enemy movements and behavior to get through certain areas in one piece. Blowouts/emissions will keep you on your toes as well, which are massive releases of radiation that will require you to make your way to shelter as quickly as you can, or die.
-Active modding community: The devs of this game made sure to make the game files accessible from a modding perspective. I'm currently playing through using a mod called "Autumn Aurora" which improves almost all aspects of the game, and ENB, to make the shadows darker and lighting more contrasted. Many other mods exist that enhance the difficulty, add areas, and create entirely new experiences.
-Beautiful visuals: First off, I agree that the game has not aged in the best way, but some aspects of the visuals still look better that some AAA games today, especially the lighting system. Visual mods go a long way in improving the textures, flora and fauna as well. The setting, while bleak and rainy most of the time, will occasionally show off on a sunny day, creating beauty in a dangerous world where death lurks around every corner.
-Fantastic gunplay: SoC is unforgiving at times, but in the majority of cases, it will be due to your own error. To counter this, the game offers great shooting mechanics, including ricochets, bullet trajectory, and penetration. A wide (but not too wide) selection of weaponry allows each gun to have a specific feel and personality, which makes choosing which to pick up and which to drop very important.
-Challenge and difficulty: PLAY ON MASTER. I cannot stress this enough. Difficulty and overcoming it is what makes the STALKER series so great. It makes victory that much more rewarding. Play smart and carefully, and Master difficulty is beatable on a first playthrough.
-Sound: The sound design in SoC is unique and fits the setting like a glove. The beeps of your PDA, the wind rustling in the trees, your geiger counter warning you of nearby radiation, and enemies spewing insults to you in Russian during firefights all add to a wonderful (and terrifying) sense of immersion.
CONS
Story: The STALKER franchise does not rely on it's narrative to tell the story, which to some, may seem like a terrible mistake. It depends on what you look for in games. I believe that the setting tells it's own story, but you may disagree. I love a good story, but in SoC's case I believe that certain gameplay elements make up for the weak storyline. I should also mention that my game is in Russian, which makes comprehension quite difficult for myself, a native English speaker.
Animations: Reload and NPC animations can be a bit strange looking at times. It's entirely possible that the game was created without motion capture due to a lack of resources, which can take you out of the experience at some points. Several mods, however, attempt to improve these faults. A very promising mod called "Gunslinger" is being released soon for STALKER: Call of Pripyat, which vastly improves all animations. Worth taking a look.
Linearity: While the game does offer quite a large area in total to explore, it can sometimes feel linear. Radiation pockets and anomalies keep you mostly on the roads or in towns, cutting quite a bit of forest out from exploring. However, the forests in the real Chernobyl are some of the most irradiated in the world, so it does make sense. Take that as you will.
That's all I can really think of. If you see this game on sale, make sure to grab it while it's cheap. It truly is a wonderful experience overall.

Where do I start with this game? I've played through it twice and am currently on my third play through after beating the trilogy a few years ago. I downloaded the STALKER Complete 2009 mod which I hoped would refresh the game without introducing stupid gameplay imbalances. I was right. It's still one of the greatest and most demanding open-world first person role playing games out there. And I think I would be justified in saying that it on its own rivals the AAA competitors like Fallout 3 or New Vegas. It's just that good.
It plays really nicely, and because it's such an old game it runs smoothly with high anti-aliasing and high frame rates. As a core game you are sort of thrown into the combat with little preparation, but it doesn't take an experienced shooter-player to realize that you need to duck and cover. Leaning is super important, and enemies like to shoot when you move forcing you to play patiently and not go commando. That being said, once you get the formula down, you just sit and pop enemies when they poke their heads out. Pretty standard. The real challenge is fighting monsters which will scare the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you and really put your twitch-shooter skills to the test. Interacting with friendlies and setting out on quests is easy enough, but oftentimes the quests will end in ways you don't expect due to the uncertain nature of everything occurring in the game-world. You plan an ambush with some buddies and only you made it out? That's your fault but you gotta move on.
The Complete 2009 mod really polishes off the game nicely. Textures are still pretty sharp, and the world is brimming with anomalies and enemies. You really notice the subtle touches like rain pouring outside and forcing friendlies to huddle inside next to barrel stoves. The sound is good but definitely dated. I really like having to use directional sound to orient myself and in a game like this that feature really stands out. The day-night cycles are intense and I found myself sleeping through the nights so as to have a daylight advantage in combat.
The story is super intriguing and really enhanced by the dark and radioactive atmosphere. Everything could be dangerous and you gotta be on your game if you want to make it out alive. What's awesome is that you can play this game multiple times and get fairly different experiences in terms of the narrative and your late-game character's attributes. Some people go full ecologist and collect anomalies to enhance their character. Some seek the best guns ever. Some have the best armor. It's all pretty standard for the genre, but it is executed well and provides a player with a large range of choices to make throughout the story.
Addendum: So I beat it after reloading a quick save every 15 minutes because holy ♥♥♥♥ the monolith stalkers really throw everything in the game at you including gunships, mutants, armor piercing ammunition, and their sheer numbers (I killed maybe 40 in the last part of the game?). I don't want to spoil the ending so I won't, but I will address the "incoherence" some people claim the game's story is guilty of. I am pretty sure that the curators that made that claim were either skipping through all the dialogue, or just refuse to acknowledge that a team of devs outside of the United States can make a compelling, unique, and deeply original story. Or maybe game journalists are all ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I think that's most likely.
This game is not appealing to the same crowds that find the Fallout or Metro games appealing, and I think that the reason for that is in the fantasies and idealized situations the game constructs for the player. It really does give you the sensation of being inna woods with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ soviet guns that jam all the time fighting hostile creatures and violently entrepreneurial bandits. You also get the neat sensation of collecting artifacts for science, and doing so under the constant oppression of the military and rival paramilitary factions that seemingly have no scientific aims. While in this debut title, there is no explicit faction-joining for the player, you do participate and witness the war for these radioactive artifacts, and it absolutely informs your player-choices that do in fact yield wildly different endings to the game--bad endings if you're a lazy and stupid player that doesn't read dialogue. I have beaten this game 3 times now I think? I'll never be able to eat ♥♥♥♥♥♥ spam knock-offs again without thinking about my misadventures in the zone scrounging for artifacts, assassinating corrupt military commanders and bandits, and drinking a dozen handles of vodka to make the radiation sickness go away.
If you're intrigued play it and get hooked and maybe you'll pick up Clear Sky and Call of Pripyat which I'll review at some point.

In this game, you play as an Immigration Control Officer of a fictional dystopian country.  This means you will be doing tedious stuff like ensuring that the passport and other documents have not expired, that a potential immigrant's work permit passport number matches with his presented passport, that the picture on the passport actually matches the person and other trivialities.   You  do not have the luxury to peruse the papers at your leisure because you have a limited amount of time each day to process immigrants - your daily pay  is based on how many people you accurately serve.
If you want to be good at this game, it will demand that you memorize the *geography* of this fictional world, like which cities belong in the country of Republia, and which districts are in your home country of Arstotzkan.  So if you enjoy filling your head with completely useless trivia, then go for it!  I'd personally spend that time learning real world geography if my inclinations ever took me in that direction (although for censorship/political reasons, the game creators wisely refrained from adding any Real World countries).
The game is a monotonous drone of menial work.  Playing it felt like work to me.  Story mode offers occasional flashes of excitement when you are asked to perform some "cloak & dagger" operations or resolve some moral dillemma, but this happens around 10% of the game and is not enough reward to chore the rest.  The developers could have chosen to add a lot more "custom events" to make the game more engaging, but I guess it was not done due to time/budget constraints, laziness, or possibly a desire to achieve realism.  I guess a border official's life is pretty boring - in game you meet a former border official and he tells you something to the tune of "I'm glad I'm no longer in that business".
In a nutshell: This game is work.  If you want work that badly, then go get a job instead of playing this game.

A great game! Endless fun and chaos! Make sure you have a good and solid team with you!
As mentioned earlier, a good team is vital. A key to a good team (other than not dying 3 seconds after spawning in every time) is communication.
Since there is no HUD you have to ask other players to relay to you what color your name is. GREEN = Full Health, ORANGE = Medium or Bleeding, RED = you're in the danger zone (DAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAANGER ZOOOOOOOOOOOOONE).
Another way to tell what your health status is is by simply looking at your screen and listening to what your character is saying. If your screen is flashing red, then it means you are bleeding and the color on your screen starts fading unless you get a Bandage or First Aid Kit.
It's handy to have a team mate yelling at you to "TAKE THE FU**ING FIRST AID KIT" or when you're infected and they give you a gun to kill yourself with. THAT is when you know they care and an indication you have a team-mate for life (or for as long as you live, which isn't really that long realistically)
PRO TIP: When melee-ing, don't stand too close to the zombie and ALWAYS PRESS 'V' RIGHT AFTER A MELEE ATTACK.
Trust me, it will save your life.

The Elder Scrolls Online is the only MMORPG based around Bethesda's Elder Scrolls Lore and despite being a first under the flagship of Zenimax Online and having a very rocky start Tamriel Unlimited definitely makes this game the game that it was meant to be.
Gone are the days of needing to subscribe to play and gone are the days of different alliance players being unable to play together, if you see Angry Joe's review on YouTube for this game, I would rarely say this but disregard it. About 90% you can disregard as Tamriel Unlimited fixed many of those negatives it once had at release.
Currently there are two version available for purchase, the regular Tamriel Unlimited and the Gold Edition, I would highly recommend you purchase the Gold Edition as it comes with almost all of the DLC that is essential to making this game feel more like an Elder Scrolls game and it has some nice neat little addons to it too to make your experience more fluid.
Pros and Cons
Pros:
-Solid MMORPG Experience
-Decent Community
-Fun PVP (Cyrodiil Only and when done right)
-Accessible to all skill levels (No Steep Learning Curve)
-All Characters Fully Voice-Acted by Talented Voice Actors
-Immersive Main and Alliance Stories
-Nearly all of the Provinces Represented (Save for Elsweyr - Sorry Khajiits...:()
-Very Easy to make some Good Builds if you just take the 5 mins to look it up

The many quest lines have heaps of content and are fully voiced, and you get the feeling that your decisions do matter. They may not be as immersive as the single player Elder Scrolls games, but are definitely better than most MMOs.
The unique method of creating skillsets by mixing classes, armor and weapon types manages to preserve the Elder Scrolls style of "create your own class", while keeping it balanced for an MMO.
There's plenty of things to do for all players depending on your mood. You can do story-based quests, explore the many regions in the world, do solo dungeons, public dungeons, group dungeons, bigger raid dungeons, and fight other players in a three-way war between factions!
I'm loving the game so far. It's pretty much a great MMO with very strong story and lore!

So after playing about 90 Hr of the game i took a break. Now the game has been added to steam so if you already have a "TheHunter" profile you can login and continue your hunt with steam. Don't really understand why we need this on steam but hey, at least is faster for me to launch the game from steam instead of finding the exe file on the computer (You can also do this with non-steam games)
- The Game -
First of all theHunter is an Hunting Simulator. The games delivers huge realistic environments originally based on the islands and surroundings of Washington State in the USA, but which has now expanded to include areas modeled on the Eastern USA, Scandinavia and Germany, and there is a lot of different animals to hunt. From Ducks, Red Fox, Cottontail Rabbit to Bear, Feral Hog Boar, Moose and a lot more. There is about 20 or more animals to hunt which is a lot for an Hunting Simulator. There is 8 Reserves that you can hunt in. And they are big, it can take hours to go across the map. There is also alot of Equipments in the game like Weapons, Sights, Lures, Hunting Aids, Clothing, Hunting Stands, Camper Tent and more.
-The Price-
Is the game free to play? Yes and No. You can play the game without paying a peny. If you only play the free version you only have one gun, and you can only hunt for mule deer. Mule Deer is very easy animal to hunt so it is a perfect hunting target for the newbies.
But if you wanna hunt all the other animals you gonna have to pay for a license. The best value would be to go for the 1 year license that cost at the moment 34.99 USD. But if you want some of the best guns and other useful equipments you have to pay for the "Trailrunner Bundle" which cost about 49.99 USD. Here is the current pricing just to get an idea of the cost.
Basic Memberships
3 Months    - 9.99     USD
6 Months    - 18.99   USD
12 Months  - 34.99   USD (Best value)
Starter Bundles
Wayfarer (3 Months, 2 extra weapons + 5 other items)        -  14,99 USD
Pathfinder (6 Months, 4 extra weapons + 11 other items)     - 31.99 USD
Trailrunner (12 Months, 7 extra weapons + 20 other items)  - 49.99 USD (Best value)
Items included in a membership or bought separately are kept even if your membership expires
-The Multiplayer-
The game future multiplayer which mean that you can set up an server for you friends and go and hunt all together. Is really a lot of fun. You can also set up teams in multiplayer. This can be used for things like unofficial competitions with players on the same server or to allow private communication between a group of players in a free for all game using Chat
-Pros/Cons-
Pros:
- Very realistic game and very good at what i does. I have hunt in real life to and i can say 100% that theHunter is the best and most realistic Hunting Sim per date.
- Great and colorfor environments. Good physic and the animal feel less and I.A and more like a real animal.
- Huge reserves to hunt in.
- Multiplayer
- Missions, Competitions and Achievements ( You can read more about this at
- You can take photo anytime during the hunt. If take a big moose and wanna show it of you can take a picture of it and save it at the gallery that your friends can find on your profile
- In your profile you can take a look at all your Achievements, Skills, Statistics, Gallery, Trophies and you can also add friends that you may meet in the game. So if you wanna see how many animals you got, weight, score, shot distance,
distance travelled, hint duration and longest shot during your last hunt you can find that at your profile
Cons:
- If you do not like hunting then this might not be a game for you at all. This is after all a very realistic hunting game and is not for everyone. This might be one of the reasons why so many dislike this game. Other games like Cabela's games will be easier to play but they are also lees fun. At least for someone who likes hunting.
- The memberships. I don't really mind and i don't think 34,99 USD is a lot for 1 year license compare to normal AAA being 59.99 USD. But i understand that many are scared of this. So my best advice would be to test the game with someone that knows this game and then by the membership if you wanna hunt more. This might be why they added the "Free-to-Play" part.
- Can be very boring overtime if you don't know how hunting works or don't have any friends to play with
Overall will i say it the best hunting game to this date and is a lot of fun for those who like hunt. If you don't like hunting that much you might as well skip this. Hope this helps

Pros:
-Great soundtrack/visuals.
-Very unique class advancement system that I've never seen in another MMO.
-All maps are extremely detailed and beautifully crafted.
-A good balance between questing and grinding. This is great news for people who are looking for that old school grind feel yet may not have the time to be fully committed. It's what WoW+RO feels like.
-Combat feels very fluid, I mean diablo3 fluid. Mobs are blown up and shattered into pieces when they die. It makes you feel very powerful.
Cons:
-Server lag. As of march 31, 2016, the server is very unstable during peak hours and players need to keep switching channels in order to complete quests. However this is subject to change with time.
Controversials - things people have different opinions on, so whether it's pro or con is up to you.
-p2w or not: in cash shop, there's a scroll that adds random stats to your hat. It's not exclusive to cash shop as there's a small chance monsters can drop it. The stats are very minimal at high levels and almost unnoticeable. It's more of a convenience item for leveling alts or new characters and even then it's not amazing. At max level 600, it's going to contribute to less than 0.5% of your overall stats, so whether you think it's p2w or not is up to you.
-no trading for free to play players: this is intended to deal with bots and gold sellers. Yet it's very inconvenient for legitimate f2p players. My take: you can buy tokens from players in order to unlock trading so it's not a big deal really. Besides there's not a lot of things to trade anyway, at least not yet.
Overall, this is one of the most exciting,refreshing MMO experience I've had since 2005. I've been playing this game nonstop. solid 9.5/10.
If your game isn't available yet, either don't have it listed as available or put it in big letters that THE GAME ISN'T REALLY PLAYABLE YET.

So let me get something straight: I do not agree with the many things that are currently in the game. I am not white knighting IMC nor am I giving them a pass for this being Early Access.
I am, however, willing to stick by a game that is fun. Tree of Savior IS a fun game if we're putting aside all the glaring issues that you see in the many reviews here. I would just like to state that many MMORPGs have had rough launches. One game that reminds me of this launch is Diablo 3 if anyone remembers that. Launch was horrendous, riddled with login errors, had terrible end-game and leveling and the actual gear was a mess. Don't even get me started on the ridiculous Auction House. It's essentially the same mistake that Tree of Savior made, they crippled the concept of trading. However, Blizzard addressed the concerns of their playerbase, removed the Auction House, started making slow and steady steps towards a better game. I have been monitoring the official Tree of Savior forums and IMC's responses to the playerbase and I have to say that although there can be a lack of communication, THEY ARE TRYING. They have been fixing issues and working around the clock to deliver a good experience and have definitely been on the right track. It will take time, please be patient with them, but I have to say that all these negative reviews ARE JUSTIFIED. IMC has done this to themselves. They deserve all the negative backlash for their poor design choices, lack of proper foresight and just terrible management of the launch overall. However, I can understand that not all good games start off as such and I am willing to be patient with IMC to see where this game goes.
TL;DR IMC messed up big time and deserve all the negativity, but they are absolutely taking the right steps in communicating, addressing and fixing issues slowly. Step by step, they ARE working towards a better game. Patience is key with this game.
PROS
--------
+ Breath-taking Art
+ Excellent music
+ Highly intuitive and complex class system that really gives you endless customization
+ They rebalanced the leveling process and made it smoother
+ Controller support, mouse support and keyboard controls are smooth
+ IMC is taking proper measures to ensure a stable game
+ Very good fansites that provide plenty of information about classes, items, monsters, etc, including Skill/Stat simulators
+ All the CONS listed below are things that CAN (and most likely will due to the pressure from the playerbase) be fixed
CONS
--------
- Extremely limited Auction House
- Overpriced Token (Premium Subscription)
- No F2P Trading whatsoever, P2P trading limited to 30/month (This is the biggest con by far)

First of all I love this game.  The concept is awesome!  Unfortunately I find it hard to recommend.  It is often described as a medieval RUST.  Having not played RUST I can not say if that is a valid comparison but the reason I have not played RUST is going to be the reason I stop playing Reign of Kings.
In Reign of Kings you find yourself shipwrecked on an island, floating ashore on a tattered raft.  At least this is the implication in the character design screen.  The design of the character has lots of options, is easy to do, and does not take too long to accomplish so a hearty "Well done!" there.  There are no female characters as of yet but hopefully that will come.  After all historicly Queens took over countries as well.
Once on the island you have a few bandages and torches as well as a piece of wood for a weapon/tool.  You stand on the beach of a new world... at least the first time.  There is no random world generator soafter exploring this world you will quickly learn the locations of everything.  Considering the concept of game I do not readily think random worlds are a good possibility, perhaps multiple maps or a random generator that changes the locations of resources?
Regardless from here you must gather and build and climb the tech tree to success!  I have to tell you it is fun if you enjoy these types of games.  There is a unique mechanic here though that changes the gameplay.  This island has a king and this king can and does impose a tax.  The tax is taken automaticly as you gather and hinders your progress.  The tax can be from 0-20% of what you are trying to gather, though only on the most important resources.  If the tax is high those on the server may rise up and overthrow him!  Then establish a new king.  What an AWESOME concept!
There are draw backs though.  There is presently no mechanic that forces structures to be stable... or even possible.  This allows players to build ridiculously high walls, tall one block towers, or bridges in the sky.  This makes it either impossible to protect the "Tax tree" or "Throne" or impossible to get near it depending on how the games is progressing for you.  It allows those who have been on the server to "wall off" resources eliminating the possibility of newer players to EVER progress.
A fix concept is simple though possibly hard to incorporate.  That would be to make things without proper support come crashing to the ground destroying them.  This may force players to actually play the game and make alliances and work together to overthrow a tyrannical king instead of waiting for a relatively empty server and building a skyway to success.
I have also seen players build a wall block ing the tax collection area effectively removing it from all but the strongest/most patient players.  This effectively removes any incentive to be king other then to lower the tax rates on oneself.  Again an easy fix would be to have the area around the "ancient throne" be cursed or unstable and create a "no claim/no build zone" within it.  This would force the walls to be around a much larger area where there is room for seige equipment to give them hell if they are too tyrannical.
The building itself and the tech tree are very well thought out and made.  The placing of block easy enough and a misplaced block is easily picked up and placed proper, though this too leads to a problem.  If an enemy destroys your crest and puts their own up they can effectively steal all your building blocks in a matter of moments.  If you see stations floating in the sky that is exactly what has happened.  :(  A days worth of toil and labor can be destroyed the moment you have to log off for work or sleep and if you are gone more then a day, forget it.  All you have done will be gone.  D:  You will find yourself back to square one with a bunch of levitating work stations as your only benefit for having played before.
How to fix this?  :/  Well historicaly parts of old building were taken to make new buildings.  So this concept makes sense.  However the player disassemblnig a built structure should have to work for it.  Blocks placed by a player inside a claim should be mined out by other players, even if claim is destroyed and a new claim attached.  If done improperly parts of the structure could collapse if made unstable injuring or killing the player mining them up.  Falling stations or resources should be destroyed giving no value to the player trying to take them.  It wasn't always easy to recycle which is why ruins exist today.  I think ruined strongholds would be a neat attraction to the game.  Monuments to those who came before and dangerous sources of materials.  :D
Speaking of material resources, they have a neat system of giving them to you.  You cannot mine as in other games, perhaps the islands water table is too high or the ground to unstable for such.  Instead you have renewing nodes similar to World of Warcraft.  Unfortunately since they are in set locations they very well may become camped by stronger players.  This only becomes a big problem with iron.  While there are rock nodes you can also take rock in smaller quantities from the cliff sides all around so you are able to survive without entering the kililng zone where the nodes are.  Iron you have no such luck, the nodes are the only harvestable sorce of it.  You can steal it however, if that is how you play.  I have often been forced into such unhonorable acts as all my stuff had been stolen many times.
Fix this by having small iron deposits found around the island similar but perhaps not as plentiful as the stone.
Sounds great yes?  So why is it so hard to recommend?
Well unless you come with a group of friends and can ensure someone is on at all times.  Days of play can be erased so very easily by other players.  I am not even talking about hacks as I have not personally encountered any hackers though I do hear about them.  If you have never had the gutwrenching feeling of coming home in real life to find your home robbed, you can get that feeling here.  I have seen really cool players who were playing the game as intended and we were having a great time, come on the next day to find they have to start over because their awesome structure is simply gone.  They have sadly quit because who wants to build over and over day after day to have nothing the next day.  It would be awesome if the stringholds were just that.  Perhaps not inpenitrable but at least hard enough to get into that you can log off for a few hours.
If you have already established a group of friends or are in a guild you will have a ball playing this game!  If you are part of a private server with a group of friends this game will bring you countless hours of enjoyable playtime!  If you are a single player or a casual player that does not spend a lot of time online then this game has nothing for you.  There is no single player mode or creative mode for the game... or at least as of yet.  The casual player has no place in this game and will only find frustration and annoyance as they find themselves simply prey for established players and unable to play at all.  If you like building and creating this game is not presently for you as your efforts will be destroyed by other players, often for no reason at all.
So it is for the groups and guilds that I can completely give it a thumbs up.  The single and creative player may as well look elsewhere.  Unless you are wiling to seek out a guild or server.  :(

Stalker may be the crown-jewel of Slavic post-apocalyptic games, surpassing even Metro 2033. With beautiful environments, a haunting ambient soundtrack, and vicious monsters, Stalker sets a dark tone for this survival-horror shooter. However, you will find that, unlike Metro 2033, humans play as great as threat as the monsters, perhaps even more so depending on how you play. With dozens of weapons, quests, and characters, you will be well prepared to discover all of Chernobyl's secrets. What is more, compared to Western post-apocalyptic games such as Fallout, Stalker possesses a much deeper and more intense story, especially towards the end, when the truth is revealed. Normally I would never recommend mods for a game, but in this case, I believe that Stalker Complete is well worth it, removing/fixing multiple glitches, and thus contributing to a smoother game. Overall, despite the savage nature of the environment, one cannot help but be impressed with how beautifully the developers strung together the story and characters. Overall Score: 10/10

Transistor is breath-taking. Not only is the gameplay fantastic, but the art and music are something to behold even by themselves. Combine it all together with an intriguing story, and you got yourself this wonder of a game.
Here's a quick look video if you want to see the game in action. Or if you prefer to read a more concise review, please continue below.
Let me start with gameplay, the bread and butter about what makes this game so good. You play as Red, and you wield a talking sword who I won't reveal is. But what can this girl and sword do? That's pretty much up to you and the huge number of ways you can customize her. To start, you have 4 abilities you can select between and use like a standard MOBA game. But the neat thing about it is you can put a wide range of different abilities into those slots that all do different things, such a setting a mine, a missile that drags enemies towards you, summon a hound, etc. You can then take it one step further and combine other abilities that modify an existing one. Like your dogs? Then combine it with a charm attack that allows their bark to turn foes to your side. What's that, you want another? Sure, take another split ability on it and have two dogs that charm. Hell, you can even put abilities as passives that grant you amazing buffs. There's a huge number of possibilities that you can do to play the game you want to play, and experimenting is half the fun.
But don't get me wrong. While you may be able to do amazing things, the game is still challenging, and not in a cheap way. Everything comes at a price. If you load one ability to the teeth, your not gonna have enough memory to load in other abilities elsewhere, maybe not even be able to afford a passive. You also get a cool bullet-time mode that you're able to plan out moves and execute them swiftly and precisely. The only downfall is you have to wait awhile before you can do anything else as you recharge. The interesting variety of enemies you come across also make this game stand out, and simply the way you handle them. One enemy will charge at your relentlessly while another lobs grenades at you from a distance. You even have stationary enemies that provides shields or heal their buddies. And combining them all together in different groups adds a great deal of strategy and dynamics to every encounter. Even more so when you have to reach an enemy core before they respawn and you're forced to kill them all over again. Add in limiters that make enemies tougher for more exp, and you can make the game as unforgiving as you want.
Now if that wasn't enough to grab you, then how about the fantastic environments that blend so well with the sci-fi theme? Or how about the the music that sets the mood and tone so well for the game. Or how do fancy the fantastic and dynamic voice acting that reacts to what you do and how you do it? That alone is a feature I really enjoy. Sometimes I just like sitting back and listening as more of the mystery unravels before me. But if you'd rather play the game, you can simply plow right ahead. Even the way you skip cutsceens is well done. You can choose to simply accelerate your bike or boat to head to the next area instead of listening, thus making you feel you're still engrossed in the world.
But now that I sung praises for this game, it still has minor flaws.
*My game crashed as I was heading to another area, and I had to restart the level. The game also froze for a bit when I was in a fight. I have a beast of a computer, so I know my end is not to blame.
*The only thing you can customize in the graphics menu is resolution, which is named resolution accordingly. The game looks fantastic as it is for high-end rigs, but those who may want to skirt by the minimum requirements may not be able to.
*Although I'm really interested about the story, sometimes I get the feeling I still don't understand what I going on when the answer appears to be right before me. The whole game is pretty vague, and the game simply drops you right into the action without warning at all. Personally, I liked that it does these things, but some who like to know everything as it happens may not like this.
That's really all I can think of. I simply enjoy this game immensely, and I highly recommend anyone pick this game up. I feel like it's a steal at $20, and when it goes on sale, then there shouldn't even be a question anymore that you should get it.

Dumb, but fun. Just like a playable Michael Bay movie. If you like explosions, this is your game. If you like a deep story: Move along, nothing to see here.
Long version:
The 3 stages I went through with Just Cause 3:
1. Wohooo, blow it all up. Story is dumb, but who cares.
2. Uh. This is getting really repetitive. Also, what exactly got better since JC2?
3. Ah, screw it. It's fun anyways.
So, first of all: If you have unstable Internet, JC3 will take you out of the game to show you the connection progress to SE, which always has to be connected, except if you're in Steam Offline Mode. The connection would not bother me, as you can tell the game to just stfu and run in offline mode, but this little bugger thinks it's cool to try to reconnect whenever you open the menu, which is kinda necessary because a minimap was too hard to implement it seems.
In 2016, the connection should be made in the background. This is really inexcusably bad design.
Speaking of bad design: The car handling is atrocious. Straights are no problem, but as soon as you get in a curve, the car loses inexplicably much speed. The Handbrake just makes cars twerk their♥♥♥♥♥like they are some pop star and just doesn't feel right. You get used to it, though.
Even worse: Cars seem to not have been a priority since you have a wingsuit which is much faster anyways and not all Islands are connected by roads (in fact, most aren't), which is especially bad considering JC2 had made it better many years ago.
The world is a bit disappointing. I loved the city Islands in JC2 which seemed like real cities. Now, the biggest city is a village with skyscrapers. Also, I missed some details like the nice Ski resort or the desert in JC2. Yes, it's supposed to be mediterranian, but since when does JC give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about realism?
Civilian life is just as underwhelming: No huge Airport (like in JC2), VERY few civilian planes actually flying around and generally the world is a bit lifeless. It's fine though, as nobody wants to be civil in JC.
I really loved the Big Cargo Plane, which actually can transport vehicles (Looking at you, GTA5...). Sadly, there are only around 2 airstrips that actually are big enough for such a huge plane, which is sad.
Blowing up stuff works great, and that's what actually matters.
However, everything looks a bit the same. There are surprises and wow-moments, but nothing really blew my mind in terms of military station design.
The worst thing in the game are the challenges. You need them to get better equipment, but I found them to be too tiresome and too tedious to even consider doing all of them. The fairest challenge is Wingsuiting, but the rest just freaks me out because of the bad car handling, the sometimes quite spastic physics and sometimes just being boring (Fun 1 to 2 times, then it gets repetitive).The challenges are actually the worst thing in the entire game.
However: The game looks great (running on gtx1070, 6600T and 8GB RAM) and I've had a few crashes, but not the big issues you can read about in the reviews.
The story is dumb, but has a bit of wit, which makes it better than the over-the-top cheesy story of JC2.
While the cars handle like♥♥♥♥♥♥ most of them sound really good and relaxing.
I found helicopters to be a bit too weak, tanks, jets or the bavarium wingsuit can do most jobs way better. Also, when you don't have the bavarian wingsuit yet, travelling from one island to another can be really annoying as ships are generally too slow and you can't glide of the large waters.
It's not something great, new, unseen, it's more of JC2. The world is a bit worse, the graphics and the gameplay are a bit better. If you were fed up with JC2 recently, you probably won't want JC3. But if you liked JC2 and wanted something similar, JC3 is your thing. Also: If you want to play a spiderman game, play JC3. It's certainly one of the best spiderman games out there :)

Tree of Savior is one of the most enjoyable MMO's I have ever played. It takes all of the best qualities of its spiritual predecessor Ragnarok Online (tons of unique classes, gorgeous and charming art style, fantastic sound track) and improves upon them greatly while also introducing a vastly improved action based combat system and countless other fun features.
I have played most of the big name MMO's out there, and many of the lesser knows as well. My limited time playing ToS so far has been far more enjoyable to me than any other MMO I can recall. The gameplay itself is imenseley satisfying, and the number of incredibly unique and awesome class skills available in this game is mind-boggling. The variety in skills goes way beyond anything I've ever seen in an MMO. There are classes that can telekenetically throw monsters into walls, guys that can stick monsters onto the end of a spear (like a fork) and use them to pummel other monsters, a centurion class that can allow for your party members to join "formations" with you (allowing you to take control of them all as a unit), necromancers that use the body parts of defeated monsters to create summons and special attacks, and so much more. It really gives you a lot to strive and look forward to as you progress through the game.
Seriously don't listen to the negative reviews complaining about launch week server issues or lack of dev support. It is by no means any worse than the launch week of any other popular MMO, and if you actually look for it you can see that the devs have been doing a wonderful job at keeping the community up to date with their latest developments (GM's have even been responding directly to countless player questions on the announcement section of the forums, as well as announcing progress and fixes in-game via global messages). They even changed their entire launch schedule within a day based on player feedback (ultimately basing their plans around the results of a player poll). Any issues it does have at the moment will without a doubt be a total non-issue in a couple weeks max, so permanently marring the games score based on a few debatably bad days is ridiculous.

Great combat mechanics, decent boss fights, dark and moody soundtrack. Some enemies are a bit lackluster compared to DS1, and the environments don't feel as in-depth either. The addition of more bonfires and instant teleportation at the start also makes you lose some of that sense of adventure after you go through a section once compared to the constant back-and-forth travel of DS1.
There are more weapons though, more armour too. So get your fashion running up because equipment load works differently allowing you to fashion souls much easier. Character gen can still be as messed up as the first (I've seen pure beauty a few times in the game). The lighting is a bit better this time around (And it gets even prettier with ENB graphics mod), the port is soo much smoother (60FPS unmodded), and the animations feel less clunky compared to the first.
Repair mechanic is different. Weapons break easier, but you repair them instantly at a bonfire (Blacksmiths are required for broken equipment). Dodge mechanic is tighter than the first, requiring better timing, but is also not locked to 4 directions when targeting an enemy.
Did I also mention that Online actually works? Because summoning and invading are much easier to do.
Also, get the DLC / season pass. The new areas and equipment are worth it.

Game is unbalanced. Once in a while 1000 ammo is not enough to break through hordes of enemies who just sit there waiting for you. Some other time you can gather 2000 shells with little effort.
So why to play it? Story is quite nice, worth discovering. Scenery is good. It has some nostalgic feeling of world that collapsed - not that much as in Fallout 3 but far more than in Fallout: New Vegas. Occasional appearances of some strange creatures and mystery of artifacts increases the impression.
Buy it, but on sales.

-The concept of a survival medieval player-driven environment is appealing and it is a niche that definitely deserved exploration. The politics-driven, savage medieval open world opens up many options for social interactions that can make this game very interesting with each play experience being unique. Whether you want to RP or simply go through the game with your own play style, the freedom is interesting. This is literally the only thing I can think of that is somewhat decent (Your social experience in this game can be both positive or negative, ultimately making this part subjective anyways.).
-The optimization on this game is poor which leads to constant crashes on many servers, meaning you will be plagued by rollbacks and item losses.
-Official servers are completely unmoderated, free-for-alls. This would be fine if it wasn't for the fact that there are hackers ready and willing to grief you unprovoked. All those high-tier items and blocks you put down on your fortress? You better hope you don't get spotted by the hacker that can just one-shot you and destroy your entire building with a basic hand club.
-The above statement applies to most player servers as well. Hacking may even be more rampant of an issue with player servers.
-Let's say you get past through these service pitfalls and you get to the actual game: You have to contend with the mechanical issues; A combat system that is clunky, laggy, and ultimately unrewarding.  This in combination with severe server optimization issues, despite having decent connection ping and FPS, will often end up with visually stuttering character animations that make combat less about skill and more about sheer annoyance.
-This doesn't even account for the multitude of in-game bugs with VOIP, crests, item crafting, item placing, environment clipping, immersion-breaking ragdoll physics when swimming, and too many other nonsensical things you'll have to compensate for on a regular basis.
-And this last one is purely subjective from my experience and you may feel free to disregard what I am about to say as it is extremely biased, but the players I have experienced in both lawless and rule-bound servers is beyond abhorrent. It is one thing to savage someone's property as it is a part of the game and no one should complain about that, but it's another thing to be absolutely toxic while doing it. This game hosts people with both the kick and the spit in the face after and with (barely functioning, mind you) VOIP, exploring the baseness of some individuals through hearing their toxicity can destroy any and all experiences you may have playing RoK.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If you can still get past all of this and wish to play, I would highly recommend coming into this game with a decent group of friends. This should maximize your experience if you can get past how buggy this game is while mitigating some of the toxic community you'll encounter while playing this game.
In my opinion however, Reign of Kings, while having much potential in it's concepts, falls short of being a good game for the listed reasons which make this game virtually unplayable and ultimately unenjoyable.
Cheers.

Okay - it's not the best Sonic game, but damn, it's far from being the worst. I think it was well worth the wait. Sure the story is a bit short, but they pack a lot of action into the six or so hours it takes to beat. The soundtrack is phenomenal, though that's no surprise for a Sonic game, and the gameplay is solid, especially the avatar stages and Shadow stages. Character customization is fun and cute - more silly than I expected, but good nonetheless. Unfortunately Infinite as a villain is not as interesting as he was hyped up to be, but Eggman makes up for this by being more evil and intimidating than he's been in a long time. Perhaps the best thing about this game though, as a Sonic fan, is that Shadow is back and better than he's been since 2006! He's not just edgy broody man anymore, he has quite a bit of character and shows up in quite a few scenes, in both important roles and to fill out the background. Ultimately, while this game isn't perfect, I highly recommend it for fellow Sonic fans.

Finished Sonic Forces. Here are my thoughts about it:
General atmosphere - 8 out of 10. I really liked the resistance vs the evil empire vibe that the game gives. They got this right from the start, and it made me excited during the game, wondering what was coming next. The avatar character basically is you - you start as a rookie wondering whats going on and looking for a way to get out of the mess, and get more heroic as the game progresses.
Music - 8 out of 10. Some tracks i really liked, some (especially classic sonic ones) i found dull. The good tracks can carry it for me and kept me entertained.
Gameplay - 6 out of 10. On some levels, its more a 5 due to weird platforming behaviour. It doesnt peeve me as much as i can imagine it will do to others, but often it creates a 'fake difficulty' - the game is hard cause its hard to control your character. Sadly, all 3 chars suffer from this. Its playable and therefore I give it a pass, but this could have been optimized more.
Graphics - 8 out of 10. I liked the graphics of many stages, some look pretty wonderful to look at. It made me walk slower just to chew the scenery. A few places could have been fleshed out more.
Difficulty experience - 7 out of 10. Its not too easy, and not too hard. There is many spots where the difficulty feels fake - you die cause you dont know whats coming, and can not react to it other than 'lets do this again since now i know whats coming'. Lots of bottomless pits too adds to that feeling. It doesnt  bother me but im aware other people may consider this a weakness. Bosses... some were easy, some i had to try like 10 times to get pass.
Story - 7 out of 10. Im glad there is a story, and they did their best on it. There is elements i like and love, and then there is the stupid parts and characters who just dont do anything for the story. Unfortunately, not everything in the story is explained, and at the end I still felt confused about some parts. They do several things right, but it has its flaws as well. Still, i felt entertained overall.
Price & Quality balance - 5 out of 10. Get this game if you are a real Sonic fan and dont mind the flaws in the game. For me this is the case and I feel satisfied with the game, although it certainly could have been better. For the more casual platformer fan, I feel the price is too steep. Should wait for a 50% sale.
Overal verdict: I give it a 6.5 for its current price. For the right price, its a 7. Its a game with flaws, but if you can stand these, there is many good parts for you too. And for that, I recommend it.
Pros:
+  Sonic Forces feels like Sonic Generations with a different story, and the addition of a character that you can customize and which fights enemies in a more direct combat style.
+ The general atmosphere, music and graphics are the best parts. Story has its good moments too.
+ Voice acting feels right, especially Infinite, Eggman Tails, Rouge and the Chaotix I feel have good moments.
Cons:
- The cutscenes stutter a bit for me, I feel they could have optimized that more.
- Classic Sonic I find the weakest part by far. Should have been left out of Sonic Forces entirely.
- Weird platforming physics, hard to control your char especially air control in a jump. Sonic Mania does this much better.

This is another time when I wish we had a "Neutral" recommendation rather than "Yes/No". Being a big Aliens fan is the only reason I finished this game as by halfway I was getting very frustrated with it. The graphicl and sound design is phenomenal and it really does look as if you're in the settings of the first film, but the gameplay got rather tedious after several hours.
The game does little to explain to you how things like the crafting system works except for random loading tips, it was hours before I found out that I can actually commit a salvage compenent to an unfinished item and free up an inventory slot, I wonder how much salvage I left behind in the first half of the game. There are way too many button presses needed for the simplest tasks, I supposed they thought it make things more tense but after a while having to press 3-4 buttons instead of 1 just to open a damn door became tedious.
The save system is also a love or hate issue, I'm sure that a lot of time was spent just from going back to save points to avoid frustration from another death wiping out half an hour or more of progress. The save points are inconsistent as well, more diffcult areas have very few while really easy ones have many scattered about.
Then there is the xenomorph AI. For many areas it is fine and some levels have it "tethered" to follow you around like it see through walls. For PC players there is a mod that adjusts it, mostly by breaking the tethering, which did help make the game more tense and less frustrating but it's only doing what the developers should have done in the first place. The game feels more tense when the xenomorph may or may not come after you if you make to much noise, when it hangs around indefinitely it quickly becomes more of an annoyance.

That's not to say the game would be completely without flaws, though: occasionally, the plot drags its feet, and having to replay certain sections multiple times due to the saving system can be annoying.
The Mac port by Feral is also close to perfection: the game ran stable and mostly absolutely smooth on my 2012 rMBP.

I like Dark Souls 2. It improves a lot on Dark Souls 1. Even the online is better and tons of fun. But yet, it feels weaker.
The major issue I have with Dark Souls 2 is that it feels more thinely spread in terms of story. Dark Souls 1 took place in one Kingdom and while some places didn't fit together perfectly it felt well connected. Dark Souls 2 does not. You'll go from Poison Swamp to Fire Castle, or from city to shipyard in almost no time. And each of these areas has a lore that isn't connected to the main lore. So you'll find a swamp king and queen with their own story, but that doesn't have anything to do with the giant fire king you face in the next area.
As for combat, it's better. Miracles are utterly useless after a series of nerfs though, and ranged combat is the only way to get through some areas of the game without having to fight a ton of dudes in heavy armor. Enemy variety is higher, but the bosses aren't as spectacular.
I recommend Dark Souls 2, because it's a great improvement on the first game. But it doesn't feel as polished or as geniuenly creative.

The game is basically What is says on the can, you play as a border guard that does border guardly things, but it's so much more than just that. Are you a lawful citizen, refusing any and all bribes? It's easy to say what you will do when observing as a third party, but when you're in those shoes, you find out exactly the type of person you become under desperate measures.
