You could have just copied Ragnarok Online, with a giant *open* world , where each map is large and has certain monsters that have a set strength where there is no set in stone zone level and dungeons are just another map no different to any other area with mobs, where you can level wherever you like or can without being forced along a linear questline with the premise of kill and get xp in a class system that is fun and makes sense and a combat system that is simple but actually works.
But nah, we only get the cute art style and the great soundtrack. Is that really the only thing they thought was worth taking from RO? Why do we still have sterotypical western MMO tropes seeping into eastern MMOs now as well as every single western MMO? Why do developers STILL think that to make a successful MMO you need some intricate combat system that will never be good, because MMO combat is never good, but it is better to make a boring combat system that works than a boring combat system that doesn't. Most of the classes in Ragnarok played by holding left click, Runescape had a combat system where you left click once and wait until the enemy died for crying out loud, but it worked, and those games were highly successful. And stop forcing sheep hearding, mandatory linear quests for god sake, give players the means to find out how to level on their own.
Anyway, it's basically RO with the entire gameplay system cut out of it to be replaced with ♥♥♥♥♥♥, overused and boring modern MMO tropes that I listed above, plus a very very terrible version of the class system from RO.
The positives
-Art style
-Music
The negatives that I care about
-Ultra clunky keyboard/controller based movement/combat system with practically zero targeting and you feel you have little control over your abilities, highly sensitive to ping, feels horrid when you aren't close to the server. The choice of this movement and combat system in a RO-esque/top down view MMO is utterly bizzare, the fact this isn't point and click like Dofus, Wakfu, RO and other top down games I'll never be able to work out. Why did the developers feel they had to be totally different here, but copy tropes everywhere else?
-Zones are horrifically small and feel totally crowded, made worse by the fact mobs spawn clustered in portions of the already tiny zone rather than randomly placed, your quest area is potentially smaller than the screen.
-Mandatory linear questing. You linearly progress through the zones, the ones you pass through, you won't return to. There is absolutely no open world elements whatsoever, you cannot go anywhere you want when you start the game like you can in RO or many other games for that matter. Even WoW has more choice on where/how you level than this game. This is the worst part that makes the game totally different to RO, terrible and destined to be a failure. The modern obsession with this system is a plague and developers can't seem to work out that if you do this your game dies most of the time. Add this with the tiny zones and you get double the cancer. What if I told you that it is possible to make an MMO without quests, or have them as optional side quests or ways to unlock other things? Well you can and I hope to♥♥♥♥♥♥MMO developers realise this soon.
-Class/skill system is kind of like they wanted to make it similar to RO, but change it so it is unique. Cept it is super stupid because early classes have limited abilities and branch out into new and totally different ones that don't actually complement each other. You have to get bow skills as an archer but then you can eventually get skills for daggers, but when you have daggers, whats the point of the bow skills you just learned. Half the time the old skills are weak and redundant later anyway. I'm not sure why they added 5 billion different classes and grouped them under a mere 4 starting classes. RO had 6, and they branched off into two more, then never branched again, but the starting classes had skills relevant to the classes they turned into, ToS doesn't.
There's more issues but there's no point mentioning them because of the reasons above. And no this isn't a first day rant.

Heres a snipit from Chuminn's review for the Custom Hero
"The newest gameplay style is the Avatar, which is a character you create. The Avatar's gameplay is unexpectedly fun. Think the Modern Sonic gameplay, but without the boost. Instead of a homing attack you have a grappling hook that lets him sweep surfaces and smash into enemies, and instead of a Boost you have a Wispon, a weapon of awesome power. Wispons are the Avatar's main method of defeating enemies. It's not super involved, as some may have already noticed. If your Wispon is Burst, you hold a trigger to shoot a flamethrower. Enemies are often placed in your way so you have something to kill with them, really. But despite the simplicity of the combat, it's actually a lot of fun overall, and very cathartic in the same way that boosting through enemies as Sonic is. The Wispons even have special movement abilities that help the Avatar access alternate routes. You're encouraged to swap your Wispons out because some are more effective on certain levels and certain Red Rings can only be reached by taking advantage of these unique powers. Each Wispon has something going for it, but typically there is a sort of trade-off. My personal favorite is Cube, which freezes enemies and lets you absorb them for free rings, but is very slow for attacking and requires you to stop to use it. The Avatar can be customized with parts earned through completing levels and beating missions, giving you extra incentive to keep playing. The parts and customization options are plenty, and getting something you like is genuinely satisfying."

Finally getting around to playing this one. Got it on sale, it sat in my library for a good few months, cooling down from the hype. Now I'm digging into it to see what all the fuss is about.
This game is likely the only game in the licensed Alien game lineup that accurately portrays the vision of the film; the first (and best) film, released in 1979. It creates an enveloping abmience, with its music, sounds and visuals, along with the story. I haven't yet finished the game but I am pretty far in - chapter 11.
What I will say is that this game ramps up in a solid way - there are some parts that annoyed me with the Alien AI being almost *too* knowning but perhaps that is better than it being too easy.
Some parts of the game are reminding me a bit of Bioshock in outerspace, which is not a bad thing, but just a vibe I'm getting at this stage in the game.
Overall a really solid experience. Not as tense as Outlast or Amnesia, which is a nice change of pace. Things are still startling and jumpy at poitns but I'm not whiteknuckled throughout the entire game, which gives me ample time to explore the very detailed environments that pay homage to the original film.

This isn't one of your Left 4 Dead easy to kill zombies game. You're in a real challenge here.
Guns aren't everywhere. Ammo isn't everywhere. Supplies aren't everywhere. Medkits aren't everywhere. You can get infected and die with only Antibiotics to slow it down. You have to move fast, avoid contact and conserve your ammo, if you're lucky to find. You can either move fast, help your team and get all your teammates to safety, or you can stand in the corner like an idiot and get killed while only 1 of you will try to win.
Gameplay is hard, challenging, rewarding, teamwork is required, you WILL feel stress and possibly fear.
10/10 would get bitten again.

TL;DR AT THE BOTTOM
A good game with potential to be great, Reign of Kings offers an engaging medievel survival experience with a fair amount of depth already while its still in alpha. The game when fully fleshed out, has the potential imo to provide hours upon hours of fun akin to the type of experiences you would find in rust/dayz type communites albeit with less ♥♥♥♥ery. Thats not to say that this game has some flaws (which are to be expected in alpha) so for the sake of lists and lists alone (You know you like pros and cons bullet points in our reviews, you know you do!) I shall provide a brief list of Pros and Cons from MY perspective.
PROS
-Best Character Creation menu EVER!!! (I would seriously pay 5 bucks for a dlc that let me use the same system in this game on ANY game with character creation. Now the reason why I like it is very polarizing but I'll just state it simply; You can make your guy look ♥♥♥♥ing wierd beyond imagination. Remember 2K15's Face Scan Glitch? Picture that but the WHOLE body is your playground, if you haven't seen pictures of what Im talking about just google it and thank me later)
-SUPER SMALL DL for how much stuff is already in the game, when I first dl'ed it was under 1gb (its more or exactly 1gb due to patches last time i checked)
-Fairly Responsive Dev Team (Had one night where we saw 2 patches within a few hours of each other, they were extremly similar in what they fixed but it still shows they are earnest in their attempts to find all the kinks and what not)
-Potential for an awesome RP experience (I suggest private or whitelisted servers, public servers it is nigh impossible to engage in rp or lite rp without sustaining small to severe raids up to having your whole base, blocks and all taken)
-Potential for awesome PVP (Right now the game consists of several classes of swords axes warhammers bows crossbows javelins and varies other trinkets to maim and dismember your prey whether youre going for the kill or just to break his legs so you can rope him up easily and take him to your happy shack, and yes you will make a happy shack as I like to call it this game, filled with all the torture devices you can need for catching a leatherclad theif nicking your♥♥♥♥♥♥ Also you can parry and feint and use 3 different types of strike for each melee weapon. SOMEWHAT similar to M&B or Chivalry)
-Potential for amazing buildings (Has no upper limit to building as far as I know, built a tower on one server so high we timed it at 33 seconds to impact when jumping from the top. You can on rp servers mostly, build large complex towns through proper coordination and what not.)
-Fairly engaging soundtrack (The soundtrack is very similar at somepoints to Skyrim the only problem being it plays sporadically at what seems to be random intervals, sometimes I hear music every 30 mins, sometimes its 10, sometimes it 2 hours etc.)
CONS
-Public servers can become riddled with hackers and griefers and even community servers that are not password protected or require you to be whitelisted can fall prey to these jackasses.
-Limited material and structures to build with. (7 Tiers of material to make your base out of ranging anywhere from thatch,wood, reinforced iron, and stone being the highest tier currently. Also unless you rotate stairs or ramps there is no way to round out structures without resorting to the previous mentioned method, which is time consuming and often fatal if you are building high up. The game has half a dozen or so different lights, lanterns, lamps, candles, and torches to choose from when lighting up your humble viking raiding camp or peaceful cooking village. There are a handful of crafting stations each with there own set of upgrades that can produce anything from crests to claim land, steel armor for your warriors to defend their holy god emperor king lord, all manner of weapons, lockpicks, ropes, shackles, whips, trebuchets etc. The torture stations they have in the game are fairly limited so far but extremley rewarding when you do manage to throw someone in one, they consist of fun toys like guillotines, pillorys, gallows etc. There is A LOT of stuff for such a small DL and for an early release as well so I won't list them all.)
-Unbalanced PVP (Right now most servers consist of midget fetus monsters with t rex arms running around with weapons twice the size of them kneecapping everyone of normal stature and just being an all around menace because, although the headshots are easier to score on these berserker offspring of the midget king napoleon, thats ONLY if you can hit the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. Not to mention hitboxes are horrible in this game compounded with lag and the to be expected bugs from alpha makes most matches a toss up, even if you're decked out in steel you can find yourself beaten to death and dismemberd by man in a thong wielding a deer leg.)
-Server rollbacks/crashes can set your charcter back 2 mins or a few hours, I've had friends say it set them back by a full day but I cannot confirm that)
-Game in its current state can become somewhat repetitive without engaging PVP/RP (After 50 hours in and being the king on a server where we built a nigh impenetrable gate, I found myself envying the peasants me and my men tortured and harassed for so long, manually collecting taxes or leading werewolfs or bears into their open houses, making them fight in death pits etc, because I was trapped in this iron fortress which is really just a giant guy made of stone who appears to be knighting another giant guy made of stone, while the wretched little curs were free to roam the countryside picking flax and flowers or blowing obnoxiously on their wretched horns or flutes, I had to always be on my guard leaving my fortress for as King you were always a target. So I switched servers and started and savage camp with my friends where we only wore wooden armor and used javelins and bows and shouted incomprehensible phrases at passerby before savagely...well savaging them. I suggest whenever you're feeling tired with the game to switch servers or just rebuild your base under a theme like "vikings, or traveling merchants, or slavers" whatever! just to keep you in the game until the devs start pumping out the really good stuff
-The land is extremly small, to run from one end to the other takes about 7 mins so if you're coming from jogging simulator I mean DayZ then you might be put off or find this to your liking, hopefully they expand and add more stactic objects and possibly NPCS to interact with. Maybe a safe zone to do trading who knows.)
TL;DR
This game has the potential to thrust itself firmly into the upper echelons of survival base building type games, but that all depends on the devs and their ability to push out fun and challenging new content and get rid of the hackers while also allowing a way for players to moderately their own communities without need of an Admin on 24/7. They also need to desperately update the admin panel because as it stands right now with explosive kegs being disabled, admin have no reliable way of removing objects or blocks placed down to grief someone other then using a trebuchet like a normal player. With all that being said this purchase should give you a few hundred hours if you're into medievel♥♥♥♥♥♥ torture, slavery, and base building survival genres.

As a longtime Sonic fan I've been waiting for this game for a good while. No doubt Forces had to live up to some very high expectations - the game was marketed to hell and back, what with all the trailers, a Hooters promotion, and even a tie-in prologue comic done by Ian Flynn and ABT of the Sonic the Hedgehog comic series. As a result, there is some disappointment to be had in saying that this may not have met everyone's expectations, but I can say it is overall a solid experience.
Sonic Forces, much like Generations, Unleashed, and Colors before it, is a straightforward (literally) action platformer with an emphasis on speed, collectables and tearing through waves of enemies. There's some platforming to break up these segments, but a fair amount of your time is going to be spent tearing through levels and crushing foes like a madman. This is the "Modern Sonic" portion of the gamplay, and those familiar with previous games will feel at home here. Sonic feels fine for the most part, but his jump does feel noticeably more awkward compared to previous titles, and the biggest offense is the changing of his boost physics. He gains serious momentum and airtime if he jumps while boosting, allowing a player to bypass some more strenous portions of the already bite-sized levels by jumping and pushing boost. It's not a gamebreaker, but it's admittedly painful to see that his physics were not toned down to function within the constraints of the level proper.
"Classic Sonic" also makes his return from Generations. For those unfamiliar, Classic Sonic was a gameplay style based on the Genesis titles. Classic Sonic has more of an emphasis on tighter platforming, but the physics are very noticeably different from those of the Genesis titles, so if you're a newcomer to the Classic Sonic gameplay, I would not go in expecting a 1:1 Genesis similarity. He doesn't really have proper acceleration or slope physics, he's far tighter. The levels themselves aren't amazing, but they're a fair amount of fun, and even a little challenging at times too. For those coming from Generations you'll note his rolling physics are actually significantly improved. He properly gains momentum when rolling, whether from a spindash or not. On the opposite end, his actual running momentum is noticeably worse. Overall I think he plays fine but he could stand to play better. For those coming from Mania, you may be pleased to know he has the Drop Dash.
The newest gameplay style is the Avatar, which is a character you create. The Avatar's gameplay is unexpectedly fun. Think the Modern Sonic gameplay, but without the boost. Instead of a homing attack you have a grappling hook that lets him sweep surfaces and smash into enemies, and instead of a Boost you have a Wispon, a weapon of awesome power. Wispons are the Avatar's main method of defeating enemies. It's not super involved, as some may have already noticed. If your Wispon is Burst, you hold a trigger to shoot a flamethrower. Enemies are often placed in your way so you have something to kill with them, really. But despite the simplicity of the combat, it's actually a lot of fun overall, and very cathartic in the same way that boosting through enemies as Sonic is. The Wispons even have special movement abilities that help the Avatar access alternate routes. You're encouraged to swap your Wispons out because some are more effective on certain levels and certain Red Rings can only be reached by taking advantage of these unique powers. Each Wispon has something going for it, but typically there is a sort of trade-off. My personal favorite is Cube, which freezes enemies and lets you absorb them for free rings, but is very slow for attacking and requires you to stop to use it. The Avatar can be customized with parts earned through completing levels and beating missions, giving you extra incentive to keep playing. The parts and customization options are plenty, and getting something you like is genuinely satisfying.
The levels are fun and do provide a genuine challenge later on, for those worrying that they may be too easy. Despite initial impressions, they're actually far less linear than many may have actually assumed. Even the most linear of levels has at least one or two extra pathways to take, typically leading to a Red Ring or other shiny trinket. To mix things up further there are a few Tag Team levels, where you take control of both Sonic and the Avatar. These play perfectly fine and are handled really well, and there's a lot of cool moments that come with it. Overall they ARE more linear than those of Colors or Generations, but they still manage to provide a lot of fun and energy.
They aren't quite as varied, aesthetically-speaking, as I'd have liked however. You go through about 7 different locations in the game, over 30 levels each (bosses included). Unfortunately half of them are either cities or Eggman bases. Metropolis for example is absolutely gorgeous looking, but on the opposite end the final Eggman levels are sort of a mishmash of design elements and colors which do little to please my eyes. What they lack in variety is made up for in sheer spectacle, which is where the modern games have always shined, really. This spectacle is undoubtedly helped by the power of HEDGEHOG ENGINE 2, which makes the game look absolutely gorgeous. From the first level you are treated to giant death worms hopping in and out of an ocean of sand in Green Hill, and things only get crazier from there. There's some mid-level cutscenes and actions to mix things up a little, and they look wonderful as well, I almost confused them for CGI cutscenes.
All of this is tied together by a story that isn't the most well-written, but damn if it isn't just a lot of fun. The story is full of fun moments with either your OC or Sonic himself (or both of you together) and anyone who is looking to appease their inner child will certainly find such happiness here. It's not a paragon of depth, and it doesn't quite hit strides as dark as Sonic Adventure 2, but it manages to be an enjoyable story that hits a good balance between not being overly convoluted or grim, and not being super simplistic and light. It's very relaxing fun overall, but if you are the sort of person looking for a story with far more substance, then I'd have to look elsewhere.
The music is a mishmash of genres - Classic Sonic's tunes are Genesis-esque beats. The Avatar has vocal, dancepop-esque tracks with lots of electronic influences. Modern Sonic's themes are mostly rock tunes, with a leading synth instrument. Just like with the rest of the game I feel the music is very hit-or-miss for some people. Many may be put off by the varying musical styles and the heavy DnB/dance/electronic influences in the Avatar's themes, or the instruments used in Classic Sonic's themes. I enjoyed most of it, but it's best you listen to the soundtrack yourself and form an opinion.
My big complaints don't lie with the level design, or the way anyone feels, it's that the game is too short. The Modern Sonic stages are far shorter than in Gens, and same applies to Avatar. Just when I'm all revved up and ready to win, the experience is over. The levels are thankfully a lot of fun to go through however, and SEGA likely knew this because they added tons challenges to entice you to keep playing. If you like collectables and being the best, you'll be here for a while.
+ Fast, fun gameplay
+ Tons of customization options
+ Enjoyable narrative
+ Visually fantastic
- Lack of content
- Short levels
-/+ More streamlined level design
- You like Sonic
- You liked Colors
- You enjoyed Classic Sonic's gameplay in Gens
- You prefer bite-sized adventures
- You don't mind Boost or replaying levels
It's not an amazing game, but it's far from a terrible one either. Look into it with an open mind, and if you enjoyed Sonic's previous offerings, there's little to hate here.

I bought this game because I heard it was a Sonic game for Sonic fans, that of which I am. The sad part is, and while I was having fun in the moment and enjoyed the cheesiness of it (I even liked Infinite), in retrospect I couldn't really say the game is good. The game feels very unpolished. Cutscenes would glitch out all together and become masses of green static forcing me to restart the game, audio would skip and bug while desyncing from visual cues, Classic Sonic stages would lag out like crazy, making them very hard to complete without getting hit. I haven't experienced any crashing, though, and I'm pretty sure the Switch version doesn't have any of these issues, making it the better port.
The stages are very short as well. I wouldn't really classify the entire game as short since there are so many collectables and stage revisits, but it begins to feel very samey when you visit Green Hill Zone for the 4th time. I do believe the avatar stages are actually implemented quite well though, they don't feel as short as the Sonic stages and all the weapons are fun. The avatar is great, I have no complaints with it and it feels like there was a lot of effort placed into making your character feel unique. The game looks gorgeous too, one of the best-looking Sonic games. But past that you have for the majority of the game: "hold right and jump to win" stages that don't offer a lot of challenge, and there are no lives. And then there are times where the game throws a brick wall of difficulty in your path before becoming super easy again, it's inconsistent.
Don't get me wrong, I really wanted to enjoy this game as I had high hopes for it. It's not truly awful, but for $40 you're getting a game that has only as much appeal as any other mediocre Sonic game (Unleashed, Lost World etc.). If you really want it, wait for a price drop. I think, speaking as one, Sonic fans should enjoy the game overall, but it's not $40 worth of enjoyment.

If you enjoy challenging games, this is one you should give a shot. It can be played in so many different ways, and only gets more fun with experience. It will definitely be difficult when played for the first time, but the beauty of Dark Souls is that the player will learn and adapt to the challenges they face. It is a game that will punish the player for their mistakes, but greatly reward them for paying close attention. It isn't a game that's hard just for the sake of it. You CAN make it an easy game if you analyze the things that are making it difficult and approach them differently than you had been, and this is why I absolutely love this series. Dark Souls II is a major step up from the first game, in both graphics and gameplay.
I would highly recommend this series in general.

I've never experienced anything like this before in a game.
The graphics are truly beautiful. It's the grimy, late 1970s sci-fi world of Ridley Scott's Alien in breathtaking detail...
I started to wonder: How... How did they do this?
The answer is that Fox gave the developers everything from the production archives. This piece goes into it:
There's also voice acting from cast members of the original movie. If you're listening and thinking, "That sounds like the real Sigourney Weaver or Sam Skerritt, etc." it's actually them.
The game definitely has issues, but it's enjoyable overall.
The main problem is the very long length of the game. I played it on normal difficultly until about half way through, then I switched to novice mode. If you find yourself saying, "Screw this," turn the difficulty down.
Even on the lowest difficulty, it's still hard. I looked at the achievement badges on Steam and only 16.8% of players finish the game on any difficulty setting!
Re: the ending, that's another issue with the game. Anyway...
I found myself wanting to appreciate the incredible visuals and layers of sound more without worrying about something killing me. This was much more possible with the difficulty turned down.

As terrifying as the alien is, I think the androids are worse. I don't want to say anything else except that, on my first encounter, my reaction was something like, "Oh no, no, no. AHHHHHHH!!!"

- There are different factions that you can join and unlock in this game, unlocking different strategies to get more gems and profit.

The STALKER games have a reputation for being tough, and it’s well-deserved -- this is probably the most challenging single-player game I’ve played. Both the open world and the AI are very unforgiving. There are constant dangers not just from the wide variety of enemies but also from high levels of radiation and strange spatial anomalies. The Zone is a large place and during the course of the game you get to visit a diverse range of environments and encounter many weird malevolent forces. The combat is always demanding and requires a good deal of strategic thinking given that you have to deal with other health-depleting factors at the same time. The story, although it does suffer from the usual lack of focus as a result of non-linear gameplay and some uninspiring side quests, is still reasonably strong and engaging. Graphically it’s quite impressive, although I should point out that I installed the STALKER Complete 2009 mod from the get-go, which (as I understand it) improves on the vanilla game in this area. It’s true that there are some annoying bugs, but they didn’t dampen my enjoyment of the game too much. And even though the weapons and armour deteriorate (a feature I’m not overly fond of) the speed with which this occurs is more realistic than in many RPGs so it didn’t bug me too much. Overall the game scores very highly for its outstanding atmosphere, which is one of the most engrossing, and idiosyncratic, that I’ve encountered. Highly recommended. 4/5

For a "paperwork simulator," "Papers, Please" is one of those rare games that redfines what a video game is -- and what it can be. It has rightly received heaps of mainstream praise for its unique portrayal of a bleak dystopian border checkpoint rife with moral dilemmas and political undertones (Do you help the woman without proper credentials pass through the gate to join her husband and get your pay docked? Or do you turn a blind eye so you can spend your earnings on your son's birthday present? Do you join the revolution, or stuff your coffers as an emotionless bureaucrat?), and for its game design, which manages to tell a compelling story from the vantage point of a clerk's desk -- a feat in itself (game designers take note: THIS is how you can tell a rich story strictly through gameplay).
The graphics are an 8-bit marvel and the sound design is better than you'd expect, but it's the personality of "Papers, Please" that really shines, infusing mundane busy-work with life-or-death drama that is both humorous and tragic. I simply can't recommend this enough. One of the best games of 2013, hands-down.

Short review from the Second Closed Beta.
This is just a generic MMORPG.
Some expected it to bring the old Ragnarok Online formula back to the table, having a very big open world map with multiple areas for various level ranges, whitout questlines to guide how and where you explore or grind. Giving the players freedom to choose how they play with each of their characters, and having a lot of different experiences for everyone.
However it did not, it follows the current common MMORPG formula of having a questline that constantly guides you from area to area until you explore the whole world map in a set order of areas, damage and experience formulas that penalty you for trying to deviate from norm, maps filled with quest-related sandbag monsters spawning in fixed spots next to the quests and no variety on how you advance in the game based on what class/playstyle you use.
This game's controls are very good though, the combat feels nice and the classes, from what I experienced with a friend, are very unique and fun to play. So if you want a generic MMORPG, this game may be a good coice because it's fresh and it has good combat.
The reason for the negative review is because even if the game is ok for a generic MMORPG, It was implied it would do something different than generic MMORPGs. Having many, MANY similarities with Ragnarok online, such as art style and team members, and promising stuff like freedom of choice and lots of variety almost felt like they promised it would bring back everything ragnarok did right. It did not, the only similarity with ragnarok is it's looks, and that's a bad thing, not because it's not what they "supposedly promised" but because ragnarok was a good and unique game.
To me this game is a waste of potential and a big disappointment. If they had the same content, but applied it differently it would be a much better, unique game.

If you have been craving that "GRIND-IT-OUT" let me mindlessly kill these massive mobs and finish BARE QUESTS kind of game, This game is EXACTLY for you.
Yes, I know there have been server lags, but that is simply ONE con to the MANY pros this game brings
(CREATIVITY / GENERAL OVERVIEW)
This game feels good, the combat is great and the amount of classes / HYBRIDS you can make is ridiculous!
I've been looking for a game like this in a long time. If you were a fan of Maplestory you'll probabaly like this game.
When you unlock a new skill, you feel the wonder, the excitement of trying it out and seeing what other class skills you can mix to make crazy COMBOS. (Playing with friends is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED imo) For example, having the Peltasta Class (Swordsmen) Provoking all enemies around + the Wizard's AOE skills helps demolish mobs in a party.
When i'm playing this game not only am I grinding it out with one character, I get excited to try other classes and see what those jobs branch out to-- and the WORLD IS HUGE! The World feels big and maps have regions, and continents and so and so forth (You get the idea) BIG WORLD, LOTS OF QUESTS, LOTS OF GRINDING AND BOSS FIGHTS
(QUESTING / EXPLORING)
There are literally thousands of things to do in this game and they reward you for doing the little things, like exploring and collecting all the material items-- that you can exhange for some permanent boosts to your character (Just little things like +100HP for example) and everything you do feels deserved. It can be long, but that's what I'm looking for in a game. A F2P Game that I can lose myself in for hours upon hours. Be sure to talk to EVERY NPC! Usually any NPC out in the wild gives about 2-4 quests alone, lots of EXP to help you get along and stay standard / overleveled against mobs. As I said before the map is very big, and with that means more regions, NPS, quests.
(ITEMS / GEAR)
Items draws are good, things are good right now I defintely don't feel a P2W aspect at all to this game. However you can buy hourly experience scrolls using money, but it won't make much difference (It's only +30%). You can get great gear already by finishing up quests. And from my experience already it seems that you can get the "PAID GEAR" by going to the marketplace for dishing out some HARD EARNED SILVER. So if you really like to grind GET READY!
(DESIGN / GRAPHICS)
The UI is very clean (Almost reminds me of some LEVEL 5 games UI-- S/O to Ni No Kuni, etc etc). Has the anime ispired characters look down. Wish they wouldve gave more customization with it but eventually there will be more head accessories / costumes that you can wear to distinct yourself from the others. It has a nice blend of 2D / 3D models and unique class skills that gives it the proper atmospheric feel they are trying to convey to you. Overall, very clean, accessible, and should be able to run on MOST COMPUTERS. Even my computer is low-end and I run things smoothly 40-50 FPS. (Low-End Mode helps A LOT! And i dont see much of a graphical difference)
OVERALL: 9 out of 10
Now don't bash me for giving out the score just because the servers at launch were bad! I want to raise awareness for this game because it's very good! Everything is smooth, fair, and you get a quality game that I'd say is worth $60+ EASY as a F2P! Love this game, I can see the potential and after launch theres only room for growth-- which will then swallow my wallet because  COZZMETICCKKKS

Well, Sonic Forces is finally here, and what a ride it's been.
I should preface this by saying that this is by no means a perfect game. There are certainly valid criticisms to be leveled against it, and I plan on addressing those.
That said, I think this is a good, but flawed game, and I had fun with it.
STORY:
Might as well get the story out of the way first and foremost. This part will no doubt be divisive for a lot of people, but as someone who grew up with the Adventure games, I've always liked when Sonic dips a little bit into the serious side of things, which this game definitely does. Despite this however, it still maintains an overall sense of playfulness with its narrative, and in that sense almost feels like a 80s-90s action B-movie. It's wacky, over the top, and doesn't always make sense, but it's a fun ride. Outside of a few infuriatingly unanswered questions, this story is the most in-depth and involved since Unleashed, and I am personally a fan of that.
GAMEPLAY:
Let's start with Modern Sonic. Once again, we return to the Boost formula, and at the best of times, it is just as exhilerating as it was in Generations. That said, the decision to remove Sonic's wall jump and drift abilities strikes me as an odd one, since their addition would mitigate some level design issues the game has. While not quite as linear as I had expected them to be (there's only a handful of levels I would really say are bad in that aspect), the levels aren't quite as fantastic as they were in Generations, and the inclusion of these elements would have certainly helped in that regard. The physics in this game, particularly in regards to jumping, also leave a bit to be desired. In some of the more precision-platforming moments, it's quite easy to overshoot or undershoot your jumps. These moments are few and far between, at least in the main stages, but it's something worth addressing nonetheless. Despite all this though, he is still fun to play, and has some great moments.
Classic Sonic plays like Classic Sonic. There really isn't too much to say about him. While not as dead-on as Mania was, he feels a lot closer to his Genesis counterpart than he did in Generations, and while there aren't too many great opportunities that capitalize on it, the drop dash from Mania is a welcome addition. In terms of level design, however, Classic Sonic feels like the weakest of the three. Not to say the levels are necessarily bad per se, but compared to both Generations and now Mania, they are nowhere near the level of quality we've gotten out of the chubby blue ball of spines as of late.
And then there's the Avatar character, probably the most interesting aspect of this game. Their gameplay style is, at its core level, derrived from Modern Sonic. However, the lack of a boost function leads to their levels generally being a bit more open than Sonic's. I honestly might have had more fun with the Avatar than I did with either Sonics, and customizing them to your liking is every bit as rewarding as you would expect it. The us of the color powers via Wispons is also a lot of fun, and leads to both interesting combat scenarios and fun platforming mechanics. The issues with jumping I mentioned prior, however, are still present in the Avatar, possibly to an even greater extent since not every species has a double jump by default. But, as is the case with Modern Sonic, there aren't too many times where it becomes a problem for you, and as such remains more of a minor inconvenience than anything.
MISC:
In addition to the main story levels, there are also extra levels and secret levels, and I will not sugarcoat it, they are not good. The levels are short and blocky (oftentimes made of LITERAL BLOCKS), and the central gimmick each revolves around wears thin pretty quickly. These are where the issues with jumping really come into play, as these levels don't seem to be designed in a way that accomidates the issue. Thankfully, they are optional, so you are not forced into playing them unless you really want some additional loot.
The bosses in this game aren't really great either. They lack the variety and interesting mechanics games like Generations and even Colors had, and on top of a truly terrible final boss, the lower tier bosses just aren't as fun as they could be.
The mission objectives, on the other hand, are really compelling and offer a lot of replay value. The game features daily missions that give you limited bonuses in game, as well as set objectives that you can complete at any time. These missions all reward you with costume parts for your Avatar, and it is surprisingly satisfying to obtain these. In addition, there are also SOS levels, which change the way you play through a given level in a number of ways, and also yield their own rewards via certain mission objectives. I've found myself going "just one more mission" a number of times, it's just that rewarding.
CONCLUSION:
Overall, despite some definite problems, Sonic Forces is a good game. Not a great game mind you, but a good one. The Avatar mechanic is compelling and keeps me coming back for more, and despite some issues, this game has some stand-out levels and systems in place that are well worth the humble price of admission.

Alien : Isolation...Finally i got this game! Now after many playtroughts , i think it is time to review this game. Alien Isolation is a horror- survivor- game ( with some action elements )  developed by Creative Assembly and based on the Alien franchise. It was published by Sega , and originally released for PC , Playstation 3 , Playstation 4 , Xbox 360 and Xbox One
The game's Story is set 15 years after the events of the first Alien film. You play with Amanda Ripley , the daughter of Ellen Ripley. Amanda's goal is to investigate the disappearance of her mother.
Gameplay
Unlike previous video games based on the Alien franchise , Alien Isolation focuses on Stealth and survival horror gameplay , and the game requires the player to avoid a single Alien over the course of the game with the help of different gadgets. Now these gadgets are introduced with the game's crafting system , because most of these useful items needs to be crafted before you can use them. there are some really useful items , and some really un-useful ones. There are Molotov-Coctails , Noise makers , EMP grenades , Med-Kits and a lot more. These gadgets can be used againts  the Alien , also againts human enemies and againts Working Joes. The gameplay is satisfiying , really focusing on hard stealth ..for the most part. After the 9th mission ( iam not certain if it is the 9th mission ) you'll aquire a Flamethrower , wich can be used to completly shake off  the alien. Tough , the flamethrower can be emptied in no time , and ammunition is not easy to find. So it doesnt takes away from the experience :)
Also , the game's Alien A.I is really advanced. it was done really well! it learns every time when it encounters you , so you cant use the same tactic againts the alien every time , because it will change Hunting strategy! This is an amazing thing!
Graphics
The Graphics of this game is amazing! IT LOOKS SWEET AS DAMN. I played it on Ultra graphics and i can say without a doubt , that the game has amazing graphics. But the game's style is even more amazing. Its style resembles the first Alien movie. Like the original Alien film , Alien : Isolation features a lo-fi , '70s vision of what the future would look like. And this game nales this vision. i love it to death.
Characters
There aren't so much characters that you will meet ( at least , low ammount of friendly characters ) on your adventure.
You play with the Daughter of Ellen Ripley , Amanda Ripley. I personally loved Amanda , she is amazing. And i also loved her voice actor. They made her a really likeable character. You'll also have two teammates aboard the station , Samuels and Taylor. Taylor is pretty undeveloped character , and you wont really know much about her. Samuels is also mysterious , but as you progress through the game , you'll learn more and more things about this guy. He is a cool character. There is also Marshall ( a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ) and Ricardo , who i also really liked.
In overall i think this game is really amazing. lets see the positives and the negative things about this game.
Positive :
-Amazing Style
-Fantastic Graphics!
-Really great plot
-The A.I of the Alien is great! .. for the most part xD
-Amanda is AMAZING
-Cool DLCs.
- As an Alien fan , its a plus point that this game wasnt screwed up!
- Sevastopol Station is devastating when it comes to the look!
-Atmosphere is superb!
-*BIT SPOILERS AHEAD* The Hive Part
Negatives :
-some characters are uninteresting , and just come-in and die
-Cliffhanger ending

This game surprised me. Initially, when I first looked into this game, it seemed a boring and monotonous game with little to do except stamp a passport. Instead, it's well designed and involves more then just seeing if the pictures match. Matching photos is fine, but this game goes far deeper with various details on the passport and various other elements, like IDs and tickets, that must be matched and discrepancies checked for. You must also 'interrogate' people who seem to be missing information or have (seemingly inaccurate information) on their documents. You also must deal with daily changes to official protocol on who should be allowed through your checkpoint, as well as juggling documentation on your desk.
You must also make sure you pass enough people through efficiently in order to get paid enough to support your family, and you must budget things like food, heating, and medicine, to keep everyone healthy and happy, at the end of each day.
This game did not initially seem to have alot of good gameplay but the clock mechanism, and daily budgeting, produce a fun and challenging experience. A great game requiring good observation skills (I once let a male through, who had Female marked on their passport, oops). Good game, good price, great gameplay. Yet another example of how you don't need cutting-edge photorealistic graphics and physics modeling to make a game good.
No other game could make the experience of stamping passports all day this interesting. This game is indeed a dystopian document thriller, and it does not disappoint.

In light of the recent bunch of entirely useless negative reviews of this game, I will try to write an actual useful negative review. I'll try to stay light on the spoilers in the main review, but I'm pretty sure the comments will be spoileriffic if there is any discussions on the points I make.
If you don't like idle clickers that have slow periods (start of the game is one of them), don't play this game. This statement is more about taste in games than quality.
If you do like idle clickers, and can handle slow periods, then this game should be enjoyable for a while, regardless of the flaws and issues this game has.
The Good :
This game has a clear progression, and there are lots of choices to be made. The background art evokes the old pixelated rpg style, which means it can be a soft trigger for nostalgia. It can be a pretty good distraction between sessions of more intensive games, or just running while you are watching a show.
The Bad :
While you do have a lot of choices, most of them are just plain wrong (for the objective of progression, which is the goal of the game), and until you become adept at evaluating them correctly, it is very easy to make the wrong choice. While this game was on kongregate, it was directly linked to a chat community, where feedback on your choices was easy to find. On steam, you have to actively look for the community, which means that a significant portion of players who find this game through steam will most likely head down a deadend path without knowing it, at least until they go looking for the community.
The information flow could be better. I mean, sure, you do get stats like "coins per seconds" and percentages on buildings, but once you get a bit into the game, you will start running into upgrades with no actual info on how weak or strong they are. First example I can think of is Druidic Vocabulary in the Druid faction (although it becomes important a bit further into the game).
There is also an issue of misleading/confusing wording. While I do understand that the game developers aren't native English speakers (I'm not either, btw), they do have a beta-tester community and a game community (which is a fairly active and vocal community on kongregate) to give them feedback on wording and clarity in the game.
My end recommendation would be :
1. Don't get this game if you don't like the specific genre
2. If you like the genre, treat this game as a distraction, not as the focus of the day. This will make the flaws less apparent and less important.
For the average gamer, I would end up on not recommending this game, but if you are really into the genre, you could definitely have fun with this game, as long as you are able to forgive a few flaws/issues.

What differentiates realm grinder from other games of this same type is the depth of the gameplay. Other idle games feel like terribly disguised skinner boxes that you just plink time in to get bigger numbers for no reason other than a hollow sense of accomplishment. Realm grinder is still one of these technically, but it actually respects your time put in and gives you strategy and interesting features to play around with to make it feel more than what it actually is.
The most important part about realm grinder and what other games of this type do wrong is the speed of "restarting". I see so many idle games where you get to the point where you have to "restart" your run to sacrifice all your progress to get a tiny bonus to push past the progress wall the game puts in front of you. Usually though, the bonus is so small that it's basically the excruciating grind you had to do for multiple days to get up to that point all over again only 5% faster. Realm Grinder almost always give you a massive boost to your production upon resetting your run, making the strategy of getting the most out of each run the main part of the game, not catching back up to where you were a few hours ago.
But what else does it have to offer? The race system allows you to choose a specialization each run, adding a sense of strategic depth due to the variety of each playable alignment. Good races focus more on the active parts of the game, while evil focuses on idling and being more passive. Later on you unlock neutral races, research, prestige factions, lineages, additional spells, reincarnations, ascension, and more- so there is always a new layer of the game being added on so you have something new to focus on.
In short, if there is any idle game you try out- do this one. This is the only incremental clicker type game I can actually feel confident calling a "game", the others just feel like passive time sinks. I've put 4 months or so into playing this so far, at time of writing am at R68, and I'm loving it still even if there are some slow parts. There is so much to do and discuss at each step of the game that even the less interesting parts of the game still feel like an adventure rather than a long slog.

ToS just doesn't capture what I loved so much about Ragnarok Online.
What made RO great for me? The openess of the world and the freedom to build gear sets for specific dungeons. And why was that desireable? Because the economy thrived on rare drops found only from specific mobs in specific places. Being able to gear towards +wind elemental damage and +damage to fish and water type monsters would allow you to farm Bib so much faster and efficiently than those who had genereic gear. Collecting drops which had a 1 in 10,000 chance became much more freequent when you had approreate gear - which in turn allowed you to finance more gear sets and higher upgrades on your armor.
I didn't catch any of that in ToS. Maybe there is more of that towards the end game but if there is; why do you have to play through so much of the world just to get there? None of the world seemed reusable in ToS. Once you out-leveled a zone, there didn't seem to ever be a reason to go back.
The way ToS has designed their class pathing, gear, item drops and player economy just seems more restrictive and more generic than RO. I'd have to even say their '80 different' classes is a bit of an overstatement. So many of the classes you only take for one tier as it serves as nothing more than a stepping stone to get to the higher classes.

I've never experienced anything like this before in a game.
The graphics are truly beautiful. It's the grimy, late 1970s sci-fi world of Ridley Scott's Alien in breathtaking detail...
I started to wonder: How... How did they do this?
The answer is that Fox gave the developers everything from the production archives. This piece goes into it:
There's also voice acting from cast members of the original movie. If you're listening and thinking, "That sounds like the real Sigourney Weaver or Sam Skerritt, etc." it's actually them.
The game definitely has issues, but it's enjoyable overall.
The main problem is the very long length of the game. I played it on normal difficultly until about half way through, then I switched to novice mode. If you find yourself saying, "Screw this," turn the difficulty down.
Even on the lowest difficulty, it's still hard. I looked at the achievement badges on Steam and only 16.8% of players finish the game on any difficulty setting!
Re: the ending, that's another issue with the game. Anyway...
I found myself wanting to appreciate the incredible visuals and layers of sound more without worrying about something killing me. This was much more possible with the difficulty turned down.

As terrifying as the alien is, I think the androids are worse. I don't want to say anything else except that, on my first encounter, my reaction was something like, "Oh no, no, no. AHHHHHHH!!!"
Play this game, it's worth your time.

Alien : Isolation...Finally i got this game! Now after many playtroughts , i think it is time to review this game. Alien Isolation is a horror- survivor- game ( with some action elements )  developed by Creative Assembly and based on the Alien franchise. It was published by Sega , and originally released for PC , Playstation 3 , Playstation 4 , Xbox 360 and Xbox One
The game's Story is set 15 years after the events of the first Alien film. You play with Amanda Ripley , the daughter of Ellen Ripley. Amanda's goal is to investigate the disappearance of her mother.
Gameplay
Unlike previous video games based on the Alien franchise , Alien Isolation focuses on Stealth and survival horror gameplay , and the game requires the player to avoid a single Alien over the course of the game with the help of different gadgets. Now these gadgets are introduced with the game's crafting system , because most of these useful items needs to be crafted before you can use them. there are some really useful items , and some really un-useful ones. There are Molotov-Coctails , Noise makers , EMP grenades , Med-Kits and a lot more. These gadgets can be used againts  the Alien , also againts human enemies and againts Working Joes. The gameplay is satisfiying , really focusing on hard stealth ..for the most part. After the 9th mission ( iam not certain if it is the 9th mission ) you'll aquire a Flamethrower , wich can be used to completly shake off  the alien. Tough , the flamethrower can be emptied in no time , and ammunition is not easy to find. So it doesnt takes away from the experience :)
Also , the game's Alien A.I is really advanced. it was done really well! it learns every time when it encounters you , so you cant use the same tactic againts the alien every time , because it will change Hunting strategy! This is an amazing thing!
Graphics
The Graphics of this game is amazing! IT LOOKS SWEET AS DAMN. I played it on Ultra graphics and i can say without a doubt , that the game has amazing graphics. But the game's style is even more amazing. Its style resembles the first Alien movie. Like the original Alien film , Alien : Isolation features a lo-fi , '70s vision of what the future would look like. And this game nales this vision. i love it to death.
Characters
There aren't so much characters that you will meet ( at least , low ammount of friendly characters ) on your adventure.
You play with the Daughter of Ellen Ripley , Amanda Ripley. I personally loved Amanda , she is amazing. And i also loved her voice actor. They made her a really likeable character. You'll also have two teammates aboard the station , Samuels and Taylor. Taylor is pretty undeveloped character , and you wont really know much about her. Samuels is also mysterious , but as you progress through the game , you'll learn more and more things about this guy. He is a cool character. There is also Marshall ( a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ) and Ricardo , who i also really liked.
In overall i think this game is really amazing. lets see the positives and the negative things about this game.
Positive :
-Amazing Style
-Fantastic Graphics!
-Really great plot
-The A.I of the Alien is great! .. for the most part xD
-Amanda is AMAZING
-Cool DLCs.
- As an Alien fan , its a plus point that this game wasnt screwed up!
- Sevastopol Station is devastating when it comes to the look!
-Atmosphere is superb!
-*BIT SPOILERS AHEAD* The Hive Part
Negatives :
-some characters are uninteresting , and just come-in and die
-Cliffhanger ending
In overall , i find Alien Isolation to be an amazing game! i would give it a 9/10! it was an amazing horror experience!

This game surprised me. Initially, when I first looked into this game, it seemed a boring and monotonous game with little to do except stamp a passport. Instead, it's well designed and involves more then just seeing if the pictures match. Matching photos is fine, but this game goes far deeper with various details on the passport and various other elements, like IDs and tickets, that must be matched and discrepancies checked for. You must also 'interrogate' people who seem to be missing information or have (seemingly inaccurate information) on their documents. You also must deal with daily changes to official protocol on who should be allowed through your checkpoint, as well as juggling documentation on your desk.
You must also make sure you pass enough people through efficiently in order to get paid enough to support your family, and you must budget things like food, heating, and medicine, to keep everyone healthy and happy, at the end of each day.
This game did not initially seem to have alot of good gameplay but the clock mechanism, and daily budgeting, produce a fun and challenging experience. A great game requiring good observation skills (I once let a male through, who had Female marked on their passport, oops). Good game, good price, great gameplay. Yet another example of how you don't need cutting-edge photorealistic graphics and physics modeling to make a game good.
No other game could make the experience of stamping passports all day this interesting. This game is indeed a dystopian document thriller, and it does not disappoint.

Papers, Please is bleak, mechanical and harsh. You run the border checkpoint into the glorious country of Arstotzka, and your job is to let authorized individuals in, and keep any undesirables out. While I do work at Kongregate (the publisher of this game), I also have been playing Realm Grinder for years. As someone who has played tons of idle games, written articles about them, and spoken at game conferences on their design, I feel confident saying this is one of the top 3 idle games out there in terms of mechanics and depth. The game just keeps going and the dev team (of just two brothers!) is very active with new features.
It starts feeling like a Cookie Clicker clone with a few new features (like choosing Good or Evil and races within those), but before long a lot more complexity arises. Then, each time you feel like you're getting to a point that you have seen everything and might start getting bored, the game unfolds some new mechanic that gives you more to chew on. It's not as pretty as many of the newer mobile idle games are, and there's precious little animation, but if you're looking for a deep idle game to sink your teeth into you can't do much better than Realm Grinder.
Also, I recommend checking out the extremely large and detailed wiki if at any point you're feeling stuck. There are some really clever and interesting strategies that the community has developed (various combos and timing) that can help a lot. And perhaps you'll even find a way to improve on them. :)

I reccommend this idle game to anyone who is willing to dump a considerable amount of hours into this game.

So 4 years would mean a nice lengthy game with a big story and lots to follow and a ton of things to do... and is this what Forces is? not really. They tried actually going for a story this time so we can start with that
After running through Green Hill, Sonic is informed the city is under attack by Eggman, Sonic arrives to save the day but is quickly stopped by Chaos from Sonic Adventure, Shadow the Hedgehog, Metal Sonic and Zavok from Sonic Lost World, which btw they're not the real villains, they're just effects from the phantom ruby, so no, Shadow isn't evil again. As Sonic fights these 4, a new villain appears called Infinite, who has the powers of the phantom ruby from Sonic Mania. Infinite effortlessly takes down Sonic and imprisons him in Eggman's base, the Death Egg. While Sonic is imprisoned, Dr Eggman conquers the world (after 26 years jfc took his ♥♥♥♥ing time) and Knuckles the Echidna forms an alliance called 'the Resistance' (...really trying to rip off Star Wars here aren't you?). Soon after, the avatar you create joins the resistance and frees Sonic from the Death Egg. While this is happening, Tails meets Classic Sonic who's just arrived from the events of the final boss in Sonic Mania and they both set out to find modern Sonic. Meanwhile, modern Sonic has just suddenly decided he's had enough being in prison so he defeats Zavok and frees himself, luckily he bumps into the avatar and they go back to Earth. Sonic then meets Infinite and fights him and this time actually wins, later on the avatar, Sonic and classic Sonic all unite and figure out a plan to stop Eggman and Infinite. And really from there you just do several missions until the final few missions where the avatar needs to use the Phantom Ruby to make the sun vanish before it destroys Earth. Then after that, Sonic and the avatar destroy Infinite, who retreats and is... nowhere to be seen after that. Then classic Sonic, modern Sonic and the avatar all fight Eggman and his "Death Egg Robot" which looks nothing like the Death Egg Robot you probably remember. Then Mania Sonic goes back to his dimension, Modern Sonic goes to fix the world they live in and the avatar just... walks away. The story overall is just... meh. Isn't too confusing like SA2 or lacking like Generations was, which is a good improvement but... why is everything so mediocre? there's no build up to a big story, there's nothing amazing about the story, it tries to be but it ends up not being so good. What I don't like is how they never explain where the phantom ruby came from... was it Mania Sonic? was it always there? its just odd. Also... if Mania Sonic is from a different dimension but they recognise him, does this mean classic Sonic in Generations was from a different dimension? or by 'dimension' do they mean the past? also why is Silver here? stuff like this is never explained which can be annoying. However, there is a free Shadow DLC which explains Infinite's origin story which is literally... Shadow beat up Infinite, roasts him and ♥♥♥♥s off... and boom. Infinite is now the ultimate edgelord. Yay. Infinite and Black Doom team up?
The gameplay is split into 3 different styles... modern, classic and the new avatar. Modern Sonic controls... better than Generations, he's no longer a tank, but his gameplay is so automated and cinematic, there's literally a video of The Completionist just looking away from the TV screen, holding X on his controller and Sonic got through half of the level. The drift no longer exists as any turn you make is automated. So... he controls better when you actually have control of him, but there also isn't any control... although I swear 2D platforming is weird in this game, you have the double jump which does nothing and doesn't even respond sometimes when you try to do it. And I die on simple platforming segments when it should really just be a piece of cake. There's no flow to him and he feels like a tank in 2D meanwhile in 3D he's just a cutscene.
Classic Sonic... jesus christ, what the ♥♥♥♥ happened? not only does he feel nothing like how he did in Sonic Mania, but he feels worse than Generations, he's so slow, there's no speed and he's just thrown into the game and you're expected to be like "oh, okay" when no, it makes no ♥♥♥♥ing sense. His levels are so boring and the level design is♥♥♥♥♥♥ that goes for all 3 gameplay styles, the level design is boring and easy, but its also difficult as ♥♥♥♥ because you can't control anyone properly.
The Avatar... he's the only one who feels normal in this game, but he also suffers the same♥♥♥♥♥♥as Sonic, stupid 3D automated cutscenes, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 2D level design. There's different wispon things you can get to progress through a level differently but why would I want to do that? remember in Generations, specifically Seaside Hill where you could either go on the kart racing path or the turtle path? and on the  turtle path there's different paths on that too, there's even 1 which allows you to go on the kart racing path but you free run it, THAT is how levels should be. Not... "oh equip this gun to do stuff you could do in all the previous games" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
Tag team... well, its a cutscene. Nothing more.
The game plays itself for you, you watch a cutscene explaining the story, you sit back and watch the level be completed for you while you listen to Sonic's friends explain the story some more, wait 3 hours and there you go. Sonic Forces. I mean there's things in the game which are good, I want to like Sonic Forces, but its such a ♥♥♥♥ up compared to Generations and Unleashed that I honestly can't enjoy anything in this game. Not even the music. How do you ♥♥♥♥ up Sonic music? the only other Sonic game to have♥♥♥♥♥♥music is Sonic Boom, but even then the music wasn't exactly obnoxious, it was just boring. In this game, every classic Sonic piece annoys me, every modern Sonic piece is forgettable and the avatar ones... they're okay, but also forgettable. The only things I really remember are the Shadow themes playing during the DLC (except one of them is ripped straight out of Shadow the Hedgehog) and the main theme, Fist Bump.
For a game that was worked on for 4 years... this game isn't good. Its not bad either, its just... meh. Can I recommend it? yes and no. Don't buy this at full price, wait for the winter sale or something, or get a friend to gift it to you, but you'd probably be the biggest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ever if your friend wasted money on this game for you. If you want a good 2D Sonic game, play Mania. Thats the best Sonic game in over 10 years. If you want a 3D game... play Adventure 1, Adventure 2, Heroes, Unleashed, Generations... but not this.
And after watching the somecallmejohnny review I can honestly say... we need new people, fans of 3D sonic games to come in and create a game that will actually be good. Let the fans balance it out between Adventure and Boost to win. Or... instead of only appealing to Classic/Modern fans, let the Adventure/Heroes fans have a turn, tag team? without the boost this could easily become Heroes-like gameplay. Modern Sonic can be adventure 1/2 Sonic and as for classic Sonic? stop bringing him back into 3D games, it doesn't work. He controls like♥♥♥♥♥♥ he's not fun, nobody plays him in Generations, nobody will play him in Forces, just leave it.

I don't know if there's such thing as a pre-review but if not, I'm going to invent it for the anticipation I've felt with this title since Sega first announced it. First of all as a writer and one who revels in a strong female lead, Ronald Shusett and Dan O'Bannon's screen play for the movie Alien is a classic gem despite what some may thing of its violent and graphic nature. Competing against such horror staples as Halloween (another strong female lead helmed by Jamie Lee Curtis) it managed to forge it's own unique fan base in the wake of movies like Star Wars and Battlestar Galactica. Thanks in large part to the team they assembled including the cast and crew of the Nostromo, director Ridley Scott and of course visionaries like H.R. Giger, Ronald Shusett and Dan O'Bannon. I should know. I wasn't of age to see the movie when it was released but my parents bought me the Heavy Metal comic version based directly from the movie script. So I got to read the movie in comic form long before I could legally see it. By the way, the same thing happened with the initial release of The Terminator. I remember my parents waking my brother and I to let us know what incredible movies they'd just seen never realizing that these movies were genre defining masterpieces of their time launching the careers of both the talented Sigourney Weaver and Arnold Schwartzenegger not to mention the cult following of other cast members who were already a mix of Shakespearian stage actors to tried and true live stage performers. Ironically both Aliens and The Terminator had involvement by Roger Corman laureate James Cameron who would go on to break box office records.
So here I am nearly forty years later to visit the ill fated voyage of the Nostromo and her crew all thanks to modern technology that I and my best friend Scott Maple used to fantasize about when we were young. How right we were. I mean of George Lucas could see it, why couldn't we? The truth is that we all did, those of use who were lucky enough to be part of that wonderful generation as those who are seeing the beginnings of the Quantum computing, nervous system based biomagnetic haptic interface and virual reality generation will likely see.
So when I heard that SEGA was doing an Alien spinoff where so many had tread, I wondered what they could do for it. Did they really get it? The protective child bearing Mother of the planet Earth facing off against a gene stealing mimic who'd spawn offspring via the host's digestive system? Sega did get it as the once again the female lead once again surfaced and all of us guys who'd been rooting for her all along once again got the chance to prove our confidence in the opposite sex. Our faith in our Mothers and sisters alike as much as our Fathers and brothers. Sega it seemed got the point according to the marketing hype and graphics presenting Ellen Ripley's surviving daughter as the hero. Keep in mind that I haven't even played the game yet. This is important because the narrative is the strong point of this game and retaining Ellen Ripley's place in the story is an important statement because chances are, this game is of important significance because it is likely the first game ever to be competitive with actual Hollywood writing in terms of impact and character presence. If Neil Blomkamp can keep the strong female presence of Ellen Ripley while retaining the James Deanish appeal and wisdom of Dwayne Hicks (played by Michael Biehn), then we have another movie installment of the franchise following Aliens. After that installment only Sega could match the Hollywood writing present and give us another interesting movie in the Alien genre barring that of director Ridley Scott and his current Alien: Covenant project. So I've indivateced that I see the Alien franchise as being important and taking the fact that its writing is also very important. After all. Ellen Ripley and Sigourney Weaver showed us that Women characters could not only be smart and technically savvy, but could carry a movie lead against an almost supernatural nemesis winning out in the end. Something that up until the likes of Raquel Welch and Jane Fonda had been impossible. This is the importance of the franchise that Sega has so masterly handled understanding the importance of the genre. Its a message from the people of the world that we believe that Women are capable of so much that history might have denied them. Help us. Please.
Please note that I'll review this after I've played this but the importance of what Sega has undertaken cannot be ignored much as what Ridley Scott and James Cameron have accomplished in similar regards. Neil, are you capable of meeting the importance of such a calling?

While I do work at Kongregate (the publisher of this game), I also have been playing Realm Grinder for years. As someone who has played tons of idle games, written articles about them, and spoken at game conferences on their design, I feel confident saying this is one of the top 3 idle games out there in terms of mechanics and depth. The game just keeps going and the dev team (of just two brothers!) is very active with new features.
It starts feeling like a Cookie Clicker clone with a few new features (like choosing Good or Evil and races within those), but before long a lot more complexity arises. Then, each time you feel like you're getting to a point that you have seen everything and might start getting bored, the game unfolds some new mechanic that gives you more to chew on. It's not as pretty as many of the newer mobile idle games are, and there's precious little animation, but if you're looking for a deep idle game to sink your teeth into you can't do much better than Realm Grinder.
Also, I recommend checking out the extremely large and detailed wiki if at any point you're feeling stuck. There are some really clever and interesting strategies that the community has developed (various combos and timing) that can help a lot. And perhaps you'll even find a way to improve on them. :)

Still really conflicted on this game. After giving it a full playthrough and then a few hours of sidequesting, it's hard for me to decide if it's mediocre or just okay.
Elephant in the room: Yes, the game is littered with a lot of mundane, overly linear level design. Classic Sonic's level design is a little better, but his physics are so ♥♥♥♥ing awkward that he ends up being the worst to play as. It's not Sonic 4 levels of bad, but it's not as smooth as Generations.
Modern Sonic doesn't feel as smooth or fast as Generations, but still feels okay save for the homing attack sometimes being picky about when it wants to work.
Custom Hero is kinda weird. I hate how it's not only the only character who can uses Wisps (unless you count the white Wisps which do nothing but add to Modern Sonic's boost meter), but they're tied to "Wispons". You pick a Wispon and it lets you use a certain attack, but also only lets you use one Wisp. So if you pick the Lightning Wispon, you can only use Lightning Wisps, and etc., which kills the fun of how Colors lets you use Wisps immediately when you find them. Generations and Lost World just barely used Wisps, and even they utilized them better than this.
The game is over in about four hours, but there's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of side content in the form of S ranks, extra rings, and bonus stages, but the gameplay just isn't fun or compelling enough to make it feel fulfilling.
I could tell going in that the story would be stupid as heck, but I was hoping it'd at least be some dumb fun, and I hardly even got that. It's a very MGS5 style of storytelling where the bulk of it is "LET'S GO OVER THERE AND DO SOMETHING THAT VAGUELY HELPS US SOMEHOW" instead of it being meaningful and substantial beginning to end. Hell, even Sonic Adventure 2, as poorly written as it was, handled its plot progression better.
The only reason I bought this game for at launch was because I'm a damn Sonic loyalist. If you're really curious or interested, give it a shot when it comes down to about $10. Otherwise, you'd be better off spending your money on two copies of Mania, one for you and one for your friend. It arguably has about the same amount of content and it's objectively way better and more refined.

Thus, the battles are probably the most boring part of the game. And since this is, you know, an RTS, that just shouldn't be. They just drag on forvever, and they have such little spirit. They aren't exicitng, and that's a hard thing to screw up in a war game.
Anyways, don't let the pretty graphics and trailer footage fool you; the game really isn't that great, and while I did get a few dozen hours of so-so gameplay out of it, it wasn't worth the $60 price tag (plus you need an extra $15 to play as the Spartans). So, unless you can get it on sale, I would just buy Total War: Atilla if I were you. Or, even better yet, get the original Rome: Total War--a vastly better game.

Sonic Forces may just be the most controversial game of the year, subject to tons of complaints over both stuff tiny and big, some will get to know this as the only game that is worse than 06.
I am here to say this isn't true, at all.
Sonic Forces is certainly more geared to the artistic people of this era, with notable time being plced in aesthetics and sound rather than gameplay, however, this does not mean gameplay is utter trash, unlike what others have said.
There are many things I like about the gameplay, Sonic feels fast, he kicks off at pace rather than a slow crawl and more akin to adventure, a boost isn't needed to keep up your speed. He can also double jump, recreated in a better form straight from Colours and he can Boost Jump, which unlike Generations, keeps up your momentum but shrinks your jump height.
Level design is concerning at the least, it is, as people say, a long selection of pretty halls and neat passages. Each place in atmosphere feels unique and special and everything looks stunning, not a bit of terrain is left doing nothing. But, the level design is at the very least appaulling where I am (Level 11), the passages can feel same-y and sure, you may be whirring in all sorts of nice slopes but it's still uncomplicated, challenge less paths, and I am playing on HARD.
Yes.
HARD.
And it is easy. I have collected more % of the red rings in Forces in my first run than I have ever done in gen, I have never felt challenged in the levels, but maybe, this will change, it still has alot of time to redeem itself in that forte, and I am holding my horses before saying what everyone else says.
The bosses (Of which I have been through two) are really fun, much more challenging, sure, I haven't died on any, but I have been fighting for my life for extended periods on both of them.
The graphics, as aforementioned, are stunning. Each bit is alive, each QTE is beautifully made with state of the art animation and visuals, in the first Avatar level you are already feeling like you are Bond or in some sort of epic action movie. And when it's not QTEs, it is a glorious walking- I mean running simulator. Standing still you will see the many things the Hedgehog Engine 2 will offer, especially in later installments of the series. Picturesque lighting, Dynasty Warriors level of characters and animated objects, epic scenes which span for miles.
The music is a killer soundtrack, a soundtrack of the age, remixes of old tunes rehashed into wonderful electronic mixes and arrangements, with a couple guest appearances from the great atmospheric London Symphony Orchestra, each piece wonderfully reflects the scene it's used in just perfectly, a great piece for each amazingly animated cinematic.
The story is the best bit, most people say it's all over the place. And to be honest it is, but that doesn't mean it's bad, it is as Knuckle's rightly claims, war and war isn't in one place. The story feels like stories, intertwining into one great big epic detailing an epic struggle, battles are made strong by a great shift from appauling voice acting in older games to amazing, strong voice acting here. Battles feel straight out of DBZ and character development can be strong with unfamiliar or new elements.
I think it deserved my 35 quid, it's much better than most games that come out today in the triple A market, not for it's gameplay, but for it's state of the art graphics and audio, alongside amazing stories. All in all I am happy, even if it does feel a bit like Sonic And The Secret Rings.
8/10
