The Elder Scrolls Online is a great game. It took two years - or something like that - but it is, now.
I started playing a year ago, and even though I was really hyped and impatient to play it, I found it difficult to play it for longer than two months. I was fun to play it, but not enough to get me addicted. Then I came back, and I stayed longer, because the game had become better. And, something like three or four months ago, I came back for the third time with One Tamriel, and since then, I am playing a lot.
The fact that you can travel anywhere, anytime, without having to think about levels is great. There is a sensation of freedom in that, especially for a player like me who likes to travel & discover.
Another great thing : the crafting. It took me a lot of time to get into it, but now, I really enjoy crafting. Since poison came, Alchemy is extremely interesting, provisionning too, and I am starting seriously to work with woodworking. The interesting thing is that each type of crafting works differently (except the woodworking-blacksmithing-clothing trio) and it is quite pleasant to figure out how each crafting works.
The best thing about TESO - or ESO, like everyone else seems to call it - is probably the fact that is is constantly changing - for the best. And I'm not talking about DLCs. I am currently just playing with the basic version, and I can still enjoy a lot of changes. Moreover, Housing is coming in early 2017 :D (and for everyone! I was convinced that it was going to be a DLC, It made my day when I learned that it was going to be free!).
On the other hand, yes, the game has some defaults. I would say that sometimes, especially in group, combat is a bit boring. Strange thing, because on my solo account, I enjoy fighting, but in group, my impression is that the bosses are too hard to kill... ...and doesn't do enough damage. So sometimes (not all the time, it is still fun to play with friends), figting a boss is just a dull affair.
I hope my review was useful. Since I am a french speaker, you'll excuse me for any mistake :)

Lots of people are comparing this game to Ragnarok Online (RO), but Tree of Savior is actually more similar to another famous IMC game, Granado Espada (GE). The same group of people worked on all three games, and it shows.
While its art and class design is meant to invoke RO, the teams system, item shop, megaphones, EXP cards, map design, audio, and even costumes are basically copied from GE.
The Good:
Visually beautiful
Large map with many zones and assets
Very content rich for a brand new MMO
Music by the legendary soundTemP and friends (same composers for RO and GE)
Nostalgia.
The Bad:
Too much stuff locked behind microtransactions. Without a paid token, there are heavy restrictions on trading.
Bots and gold sellers. Every game has a few, but it's an all-out infestation here. IMC isn't even trying to stop them.
Iffy controls. The keyboard system is not accurate or fast enough for PVP, and the mouse system is not as fluid or responsive as say, Diablo 3.
Unpolished. Problems with hitboxes, bugged quests, invisible walls, etc.
Unsuitable music. The throbbing techno was an good choice for the grimy world of GE, but not here. The RO soundtrack alternated between light ambiance and memorable themes, which would've suited ToS better.
The Misunderstood:
Questing may seem linear at first, but becomes more open world later on. The map progression system is identical to GE, but not fully open world like RO.
Grindy for a modern day MMO. Roughly as grindy as GE, but thankfully nowhere as grindy as RO. Some people like this, some people don't.
The class system feels overwhelming at first, but it's designed to create highly specialized characters that provide a niche service to parties or the entire community (crafting, upgrading, etc). This is similar to RO, and indeed many skill concepts in ToS are borrowed from RO/GE. But due to the grinding, there needs to be easier/cheaper ways to reset characters.
Conclusion:
As with RO and GE, Tree of Savior was created by a talented team with big ambitions, powerful artistic vision, but poor quality control. These are the type of creative folks who have great ideas, but don't know how to package or deliver their product professionally. This has resulted in rough launches and patchwork gameplay (especially questing) during the early days of all three games.
That being said, RO and GE both went on to be very successful MMOs. If there is one thing that could doom ToS, it's the excessive restrictions for non-premium players.
Despite its shortcomings, the game is clearly a labor of love with much content to explore. If out of nothing but nostalgia, I would still recommend giving Tree of Savior a try.

NOTE: This is a pre-Scholar of the First Sin (SotFS = V1.10, DX9) review. A lot may have changed, I will update once I play it.
I certainly enjoyed this game a lot, a real lot. It was improved over the original (Dark Souls Prepare to Die Edition, namely) in every single way. However there were a few key differences that I did not enjoy, and some things that I just flat out preferred in the original over the sequel, not because it was better in the original, but because thats what I just flat out prefer.
PROS:
+ Mechanics improved
+ Stat mangement made significantly more interesting, stats are no longer black and white.
+ PvP is MUCH improved.
+ The game performs SIGNIFICANTLY better than the original.
CONS:
- Weapons variety and reasonabiliy of options seems lessened over the original, despite entirely new categories of weapons being introduced.
- PvP lag is significant during invasions, I don't know why but half the time I get "lag killed" (hit out of range, die randomly from an attack I haven't experienced yet).
- It seems significantly easier to level up, which almost becomes a secondary concern until VERY late in the game (beyond level 120). Leveling requirements don't seem to require souls along what seemed to be an almost exponential scale anymore, and following scaling much closer to a linear increase of requirements. While this is NOT a true negative, it removes some of the sense of accomplishment you get from leveling up (it becomes almost trivial).
OF NOTE:
> The game can be played on an even higher difficulty level, see the Victory stone in the wiki.
> My Dark Souls PTDE armor set (custom armor configuration) is one of my all time favorites, I was not able to find an equivalently enjoyable set in DS2, which makes me more BIASED towards DS1 slightly. However, the plot was what sealed the deal in terms of which game I prefer.
*SPOILER ALERT*
- Because the story builds off the original storyline, as essentially a repeat of events happening later on down the timeline, I found I liked the more epic "first time occurence" of the first games storyline. This detracted from the narrative experience in my opinion.
*END SPOILER*
That said, Dark Souls 1 player or not, I still recommend this game, you should play it (all the way through, not rushing) if you played the first, even if you are skeptical, and you should play it if you haven't. Demon's Souls players go either way. I would say its less of a sequel and more of a continuation.

Tree of Savior is a game that hearkens back to Ragnarok Online, and for better or for worse, it succeeds. The biggest problem, however, is ToS is attempting to become like a game that was successful in a market that no longer exists in the way it did over a decade ago.
Pros:
+ Beautiful art style. From other players, to bosses, to the environment, Tree of Savior is absolutely beautiful.
+ The soundtrack is fantastic, no part of the game has a music track that doesn't thrill or relax you.
Cons:
- Grind. Grind, grind, grind. Tree of Savior expects you to grind, and you will grind. Once you get out of what I consider the 'tutorial' around level 80, you're expected to do nothing but grind monsters for levels with the occasional few quests, sparsely spread out every few levels.
- An enormous spread of class choices and branching classes...and only certain ones are useful. If you happened to not pick one of those and planned your path beforehand, you're♥♥♥♥♥♥out of luck. And because leveling takes so long once you reach the triple digits, you're better off just sticking with your subpar class.
- No real content outside of grinding. Dungeons are pointless, as grinding in regular zones is much faster and easier. Crafting is an afterthought. I can't speak for whatever endgame there is, because it would take me months upon months to reach level cap through mindless grinding.
- Just like Ragnarok Online, expect bots. LOTS of bots.
I looked forward to this game ever since it was announced, and to say I was disappointed that it was nothing but a poor carbon copy of Ragnarok Online's gameplay is an understatement. The game is beautiful, and I could stand around and simply stare at the environment for hours...which I'm expected to do, as I stand with a group in a corridor and spam skills to kill monsters that respawn.
tl;dr ToS is a game with art from 2015 and gameplay from 2005. Unless you love grinding, avoid.

I watched all the movies, given that the latter ones are not that great, I still love the entire world and the style and the idea it self. I was so excited for this game, I have been following pre-release videos and what not, and eventually bought it.
Just upon opening the menu and even the intro sequences you get an amazing Alien-ish feeling and this sort of 80s atmosphere that continues once you start playing, the environments are amazing! You truly feel like you got yourself onto the set of Alien! Amazing! The sound effects and the overall ambience is also quite good, especially with headphones. And I even like the graphics, and I am not a demanding person when it comes to game gfx.
But that is, unfortunately, where the positives end. The game is literally unfair. And not that it would be difficult, I played many difficult games and I have never, ever been so frustrated like I am with Alien:Isolation. The save points are crazy far apart from each other, this would be ok if it wasn't for the extremely frustrating Alien AI. Most of the time the flamethrower does nothing to it, hiding in "closets" and what not is extremely boring after a short while, human AI that makes noise and draws the Alien out is not getting attacked instead I am getting attacked, I had moments in which the Alien fell through the floor and appeared behind me, times in which the alien would duplicate and times in which it would burst through a closed (locked-down) door like it has a noclip.
I cannot count the amount of unfair deaths I had during my 10 hours of playtime, but what I can say is that I eventually stopped having any fun and just closed the game. As a longtime Sonic fan, I was both excited and worried for the next installment. No, it doesn't live up to Mania, but as a boost Sonic it's rather fun. Yes, the stages are short, but they look great and I enjoy speeding through them. There are moments where you can slow down and find optional routes, as well. The controls for the game are fine, they maybe could be a bit better though. Dodging left and right sends you all the way to either side no matter where you are on the path, which threw me off at first. I really enjoy the new avatar system and I like the grappling hook, though it could've been implemented better. Using the flamethrower to toast enemies at high speeds as the Avatar never gets old. I don't care much for QTEs, but these are extremely hard to mess up. Classic Sonic controls well, but there really isn't much reason for him to be here since Modern Sonic and the Avatar stages already switch between 3D and 2D gameplay. The story is as silly and over dramtic as Sonic storylines usually are. This dramatic new villian definitely gives me Sonic Adventure vibes, and so does the music. The music in this game is absotluetly fantastic, I've had some songs stuck in my head all day after playing. The bossfights are definitely the weakest part of the game, but I don't find them offensive. Overall, for the price I have found this game to be well worth it, I am definitely enjoying my time with the game.
TL;DR
As long as you aren't expecting it to blow your mind and you enjoy boost Sonic, you will have a good time. Nice Adventure vibes. Music is amazing.

A Disappointing game which had potential.
The idea of an Avatar is great and the customisation is fairly decent, but it's let down by mediocre level design and controls.
The levels themselves are fairly linear for both the Avatar and Modern Sonic, which isn't a large problem on its own, but becomes one when the levels are extremely short. Within the first 15 stages I repeatedly found myself expecting more from the level but instead seeing an end goal. The stage lengths never went above 2 minutes, and if it did it was because I was scouring for red rings (which drastically reduces the speed in this game). The stages therefore don't provide you with any challenge throughout the level or add any real variety, this is exacerbated with the QTEs which whilst nice at times, don't provide challenge or penalties for failure.
The controls are significantly worse than in Sonic Generations. Turning right or left, double jumping, using certain wispons (lightning whip) or the Avatar's grappling hook will grind you to a halt. Since the Avatar doesn't have a boost, it can't rectify the problem of maintaining speed. The Avatar's Wispons don't give you any real changes to movement to help maintain speed in general use. They could've granted different benefits to movement which could chain as attacks, but instead they're just a button to instantly wipe out enemies. Missed opportunity in my opinion.
Modern and Classic Sonic also suffer from the control issues and becomes obvious when in 3D sections, trying to circle around just does not work. There was a portion of a stage where I had to climb some platforms in 3D and the controls were just so poor it took me about 30 seconds just to do so.
From my brief moments, the music in this game was very solid and great to listen to. I wouldn't take the story seriously even though the game wants you to, but that's part of the fun.
Overall its an okay game for some mindless fun, but I wouldn't recommend it unless it was significantly discounted.
As for the PC Port, the game ran okay maxed out at 60fps on a GTX1060, but noticed some significant hitching/stutter at times, especially as Classic Sonic. It also does not support Ultrawide resolutions, so may need a mod to get that working.

This game is a wonderful way to spend time. I mean if you don't really feel like waiting for the Left 4 Dead series to go on sale, but you just want to kill zombies, get this game. Sometimes it's hard finding a room that isn't mission-oriented, but you will find one. A little bit of help for those new to the game. Some servers will allow you to pick your equipment.
I'll do this in steps (by memory, I haven't played in months.)
1. type !guns
2. pick your preferred weapon group (pistols, rifles, shotguns, automatics, etc etc.)**
** = you really want a semi-automatic weapon as you'll run out of rounds loaded in your weapon quick and not do much damage to the infected and end up reloading a lot. a weapon like the Winchester rifle is my preferred weapon, as it penetrates the military zombies' helmets with its .357 rounds, and if you reload once every 2 shots.
3. Grab medical supplies: Pills, gene therapy shot, bandages, first aid kit. These are essential.
3a. Pills and the gene therapy shot stave off the infection if you are infected.
3b. Bandages keep you from bleeding out.
3c. First aid kit heals your hitpoints.
Once you have everything, toss your ammo (The !guns servers usually have unlimited ammo so you don't need it taking up your inventory.)
By the time you're done the round will have started. Get close (Yes I said close) to the infected and fire. Aim for the head and stay calm. Panic firing will get you killed. Also, step backwards every time you fire and hit the reload key. Use shove if a zombie gets too close and don't ever... EVER use a melee weapon. Getting too close to a zombie usually lets them bite you. As does getting surrounded. Just find a nice spot with your Winchester, aim. Fire. reload. repeat.
And most of all, have fun.

Reign of Kings is a really, really fun game. I have spent non-stop-grinding hours playing this. The PVP and building system is great. The combat system is very similar to Chivalry. If you are one of those who are in favor of a game that's in medieval times and likes to build and conquer land, this is definitely a game for you. Although the good times rival the bad, in the gap of good times, you'll run into very frustrating, mind wrecking, and depressing situations. An example of that would be your own base being conquered, which can mean that you've lost the entirety of your hours spent into making a fortress, and depending on how many friends you play with makes a big difference. I've devoted 30 hours of gathering resource just myself and tried to build a base that I can call home and feel safe while logged out (in this game, when you log out, your character packs a sleeping bag right where you decide to log off and go to sleep, in other words, your character never leaves the server), but in the end, I have lost it all. This is, in my experience, the most painful and headaching situation and it is inevitable, even if your base may seem like it's indestructable. It is a PvP/KoS game, so there's really nothing the losing side can do about it. Aside from my little story telling of my experience in the game, the game itself has a lot of potential. I'm very surprised that the bugs and glitches are at minimal, making the game very enjoyable and have to worry less. Hackers still exist (they'll always exist), but a week that I've spent in this game, it does not seem like I have ran into any of them.
Anyhow, if this game is intriguing to any of you, grab it and give it a go! You won't regret it! Good luck!

Originally, I was going to review it after I beat it the second time as soon as SEGA had fixed the issure with AMD Phenom II CPUs that don't support the SSE 1.4 Instructionset. However, I am still waiting on that and decided to change my mind. So here's my review for Sonic Forces, and I'm possibly going to be a bit blunt on it. I'm not a Sonic Fan, but I do want to keep up to date with what SEGA's mascot has been doing when I get the chance.
The story goes that Dr. Eggman has defeated Sonic, and took over the world, or at least most of the world. A resistance was formed and are battling against Eggman's army. Also Tails became a chicken and can't do anything without Sonic, EVEN THOUGH He did do something without Sonic around during the Adventure games. That's a plothole.
You have three characters this time around. Modern Sonic with all of his boosting greatness, Classic Sonic for Genesis-ish platforming, and your own custom character armed with a Wispon and is somewhat a chicken him/herself.
Modern Sonic's Levels are as that as Colors/Generations. You have a Boost gauge which is refilled by either defeating enemies, or grabbing Wisps in Wisp capsules. Oodly enough, he forgot how to drift, and learned how to jump in mid air... sort of. However, it seems that most of his levels are mostly automated, as if I'm watching the game and not playing it myself. Not just that, they are so easy as well, only a couple of Modern Sonic levels near the end of the game I only had trouble with. The levels are also pretty shorter than that of Sonic Generations and Sonic Adventure 2. He also has problems turning while running, especially if you are using Boost. He still uses Homing attack, which is mostly for mid air enemies, springs, and those hanging things.
The Custom Character's levels are as short as Modern Sonic's levels, but you don't have Boost. Instead you use a Wispon, and some sort of grappling hook gadget your character has for some reason. The wispons are an interesting mechanic to the game, and wish to utilize them more, but it's possible to beat the levels without. using the Wispon even once. The Rent an Avatar mechanic, which is used with any level for your custom character, allows you to switch out with another player's custom character and vice versa at anytime during the level. Sadly, it's very underutilized on Pc because every player keeps getting the same custom characters, who look base and has the default Burst Wispon, everytime. This is possibly a bug. Some levels, like Most of Modern Sonic's levels, seem to be a bit automated. and all of the levels, except a couple of them, are too easy to beat. Still though, I find the Custom Character levels more enjoyable, despite some automated areas, and all of the 2D sections.
The Tag Levels, which you play as both Modern Sonic and the Custom Character, are the only levels that don't have 2D sections on them. and I like it. Pretty much for a ll of these levels, Sonic and the custom character will automatically have a time where they use Double Boost. However, it's a QTE, or else they'll stumble for a little bit.These levels are pretty short and are too easy to beat, except for one level.
Classic Sonic's levels are pretty much what you'd expect from a classic Sonic game. The game uses a 2D perspective and focuses on Classic Sonic, as if the game was 2D itself. However, unlike Sonic Generations, Sonic's running speed has been limited, and the only way to gain more speed than running is by rolling. Sonic's running speed limit has not been used since Sonic 1, so I actually have no issues with this. Though a bit harder, these levels are still easy, except that one level way late in the game. The only addition I've seen in Classic Sonic's controls is the Drop Dash, which was introduced in Sonic Mania.
Though the only challenging things I find in the Missions are the time limit ones, other than that, the missions in the Mission list are easy. You can also do daily missions ahead of time to gain a sweet bonus for completing the Daily Missions. this gives you a bonus to your score at the end of each stage. However, it's very possible to get an S Rank without it, seeing that it's easy to get S Ranks for some reason.
The Custom Character is very customizable, especially when you first make him/her. With a few race options, and Wispons/Clothes you unlocked, you can make your custom character your own. I managed to put my cat into the game, so it's not that bad, except for the clothing options. as most of the body parts could be possible to wear alongside some things, but you can't for some reason, for example - A skirt with a shirt. So far, the only outfit that I know of that has both a shirt and pants is that of the Persona 5 outfit.
The music doesn't disappoint. However, their attempt to try and emulate the Genesis music instruments needs more work as it really doesn't sound that much like the genesis music from the classic games.
Lastly, I already said it, but the game itself is mostly easy, with most of the levels too easy and seems too automatic, which makes the game less fun. However, the levels that aren't so automatic are more fun than the ones that are.

While this game looks nice enough, it fails in almost all other aspects. There are loads of classes, but you cant try them all and test them out, because there is no viable options to reset them. Controls in this game are extremely clunky. You can change some of them, but you cant really target already charged attack with mouse, and to aim it you have to press multiple keys on keyboard at the same time.

I will still play this game for time being, but i really cant recommend it to new players. If you really want to try it, wait 1 month for free to play.

The TLDR: This game is even more epic than it looks and nowhere near as daunting as the video makes it seem.
The Detail:
Watching the video for this game doesn't really convey its scope. I looked at it several times before a friend of mine picked me up a copy because he wanted to test the multiplayer.
First thoughts: I can't believe this game is listed as early access, because it feels remarkably finished and seamless. It isn't until you've been playing for 20 hours or so that you'll start to notice where they are probably planning advancements. Examples: Almost every technology has several upgrade levels, but there is really only one viable level of mining machine. Some materials (both raw and manufactured) seem to only have one or two uses (examples: wood, or iron rods) while others seem to have hundreds of uses. Some things are incredibly automatable, while others are almost painfully manual (example, there is no early or mid-game automation for collecting wood - you have to chop trees by hand).
The endgame content is amazing. I'll just leave that there, except to say that Power Armor works the way it should - not just as a defense but as a tool into which you can insert many gadgets.
Building your factories will seem daunting at first, creating very wide areas you need to defend. The enemies get stronger as your polution rises, meaning you're on the clock from the first powerplant or miner you set up.
Which brings me to balance. These guys have done an incredible job balancing the game so that it feel pressured and dangerous without being under constant threat and having to continually run your perimeter guarding your land.
I'll probably add to the review later, but if there is one thing to take away from this review, it's this: Factorio is massively more balanced, full of content, challenging, and intuitive than most finished games from the big houses - and I fully expect them to continue adding balance and content in the future. If you're looking for a good builder game, you just found it.

To provide context, while my "Time Played" only says about 20+ hours right now, I've been playing this game since the late 10.x alpha iterations. Probably hundreds of hours over a dozen or so playthroughs. That said, I love this game just as much now as I did when I first started.
Pros
-Resource gathering that makes sense: You want to build a coal-powered drill? Just as you would think in real-life, you need iron to make it, and coal to run it. For the sake of simplicity, not every single component imaginable has to be crafted for something, but the gathering and subsequent crafting does make a certain amount of sense.
-Pollution/Biter Evolution: The increase in pollution as you build up your base comes at the cost of angering the local wildlife. It also causes them to improve their attack capabilities and numbers, providing an enemy that gradually improves even as you get better at killing them.
-Moddability: The devs themselves had stated how much they support the modding community, and they built the game to reflect that. You simply copy and paste mods into the Mod folder, then enable/disable them in-game. So easy.
-Production: You feel a real sense of accomplishment when you design, lay-out, and finish building a segment of your factory. Nothing compares to that feeling when you "flip the switch" and watch the resources flow through just the way you anticipated, resulting in the finished product you wanted. Of course, just the opposite happens if you find out you made a mistake.
-So many more...I could go on and on, but play it for yourself to see!
Cons
-Multiplayer: It works, and I've played several multiplayer games. However, the process you go through harks back to ye olde multiplayer days when you connected via IP. Nothing wrong with that, but it requires the use of a program like Hamachi if you are operating behind a router. Devs have said they are working on this though.
-Resource Settings: Your early game settings HEAVILY influence how your game will go. Make a small starting area, and you will likely be mobbed before you have a chance to build much. Make your starting area too large, and you won't see a whole lot of alien activity at all until late-game. In addition, for those who want a more "survival" feel with fewer resources nearby and requiring more "spreading out" with trains and such, the game has a hard time striking a healthy balance. You either end up with more resources than you'd like, or far fewer than you need. The RSO mod helps to fix this though.
-Addictive: Not really a con, but hey, consider yourself warned. I sat down for the first time on this game and didn't even realize how much time had passed until it was 3 AM.
-A few other things come to mind, but nothing major and all can be addressed with mods or the devs have already said they are working on it.
Finally, the devs are very active on the Factorio forums and subreddit. Check out those for help or advice. NegativeRoot, Arumba, and ColonelWill (among others) also have some great Factorio videos and tutorials out there on YouTube and Twitch. I highly recommend checking their stuff out for ideas and workarounds.

Waited four years for something I could sum up as a "meh" experience. I set my bar pretty low, though. So I'm not too disappointed. This game is a lot like Colors. The 3D sections are extremely linear and arbitrary, but there is some fun to be had in the 2D sections. Ironically, Classic Sonic's levels seemed to have more depth to them compared to the Modern ones, which is a complete flip flop from Generations.
The music is, on average, above average. But its not knock-my♥♥♥♥♥out of my seat amazing like S3&K, Mania, Gens, Unleashed or Colors. Still some good stuff in the mix, though.
The story is one the game's strongest points, but its still has rushed pacing, exposition slideshows, violates basic storytelling rules like "show, don't tell," and all the mystery surrounding Infinite doesn't have a huge reveal plot twist like we were expecting. Very, VERY anti-climatic.
The "boost to win" criticism is BS when talking about Generations. But with this game I'd be inclined to agree on that front. Modern's stages completely scrap any semblance of platforming for straight lines of boringness, then switching it up to 2D after these bland 3D segments. There are a few modern stages where the 3D stages aren't entirely trash. Death Egg was a good example, with a few multiple paths scattered around. However, the stages are just really short.
All in all, if you're looking for a good platformer, I'd have to give this a pass. If you're a sonic fan however, I can see you getting a bit of enjoyment out of this. Its a step above Lost World in terms of overall quality...But thats not saying much.

I feel like the crappy reviews this game has are there for a reason, but having straight up beat the game, tried out all the wispons, beat the Shadow campaign, all the things, I think this is a good step for the Sonic franchise, and here's my reasons why.
1. 3d stages are back in the generations style. I mean, these are short levels. I played on hard, and honestly I only ever died because I tried to do something stupid and definitely impossible over and over (The crappy double jump birds get gave me some weird ideas about platforming). I honestly had fun, and the best ones were definitely sonic with avatar. The new avatar's abilities are cool, but I'd ditch them all for the quick dash Sonic has, so it was really cool to have both. The reaction based fast paced 3d levels are fun here too, though not as extensive as Generations' levels. I want more of those.
2. 2d Sonic phased out. There were only a few 2d sonic levels, and I like 2d sonic, but he has a place now. Mania was all about 2d Sonic. He has a place, it's not like generations, it's time to give all the focus to 3d.
3. Bringing back some old bad guys. I was disappointed when the only ones that had boss fights were Metal Sonic and the fat guy from Lost Worlds, but this is promising. I hope at some point we can see crazy hybrids of boss fights.
4. Story takes a back seat. There's a bad guy. He's bad. Go stop him. That's all you need. In this one, there was even a minor plot twist at the end. I mean, it was small but nice nontheless.
5. The supporting cast is back! Boom seemed like we were phasing out a lot of them, but Chaotix, Silver, small knuckles, and the 3d sonic game villains have made a return, and that was cool to see. We also had control over Shadow, which is a small thing, but it did give me a little longer with modern Sonic.
Of course, there are problems, and most of them have to do with the tiny levels and avatar. We didn't really need that guy, a chao garden might have been better in terms of rpg elements and character creation. He got in the way, wasn't as fast as sonic, and killed a crap ton of bad guys with like no effort. The whispons were fun to move around with, but in a boss battle, it felt less involved than it might if it was sonic hitting things like normal.
I mean, I'd say buy it. It's short but fun. Not maybe the best boost style Sonic game, but dang it, it is one, and that's enough to tide me over until we can get a full length one again.

This game is pretty much fun. It's like you combine GTA with a grapple hook and a wingsuit.
But although the wingsuit is a pretty good upgrade - if you compare this game to Just Cause 2 - I really miss the big skyscraper cities from the former game. Just Cause 3 only consists of small and big villages and that will get pretty boring after a while.
PRO's:
+ The wingsuit is awesome
+ I've always liked the grapple hook
+ Lot of fun missions, challenges and stuff
+ The map is huge.
CON's:
- All villages are almost the same. No big cities!
- Vehicle control is terrible (which is not a big issue as I always use the wingsuit or parachute).
- Will probably get boring before you finished the story.
Conclusion: I recommend this game, but buy it when it's on sale. It's not really worth the full €50.-, but it's totally worth it when it's 75% off!

Alien Isolation is like a vacation in hell. From one hand, you have sights of breathtaking beauty to see, but on the other hand, you're being chased by an unkillable entity of pure evil.
Key aspects:
+ The game is a visual masterpiece. The lighting and textures exceed most contemporary games, aiming for realism.
+ Driven from the previous: the game is extremely well optimized, allowing you to run with maximized settings even on mediocre systems.
+ There's a strong sense of authenticity compared to the Alien and Prometheus movies. Also the level design is wonderful and beckons to explore.
+ You're being kept in a state of constant danger. The game won't pause if you hack a door, read messages from computers or even when you save your progress.
+ Alien's AI is completely unpredictable.
+ Fun crafting system and items that sparkle with originality.
+ Gripping story with a very interesting protagonist.
+ The game was surprisingly long, it took me over 53 hours to complete the main story.
+ There are some scenes that look and feel completely unique. For example you get to go outside of the space station with all the immersion that comes with it. Or that one level which takes you to a hostile windy planet.
Verdict:
10/10
A game that truly plays with your mental capacities. There were times when I just couldn't force myself to get up from under a table. Yet at the same time it was so beautifully executed and so addictive. Alien Isolation is amongst my favorite games, that I've played in my entire life.
Update:
Gave it the "I feel reluctant to come out from under the table" Award on Steam Awards.

If you're a fan of the previous Boost Style Sonic games, especially Sonic Colours, like I am, then you're gonna like this a lot.
The environments are beautiful, the story is rich with many characters, and the level design is also good. Not on par with Sonic Generations but definitely as good as Sonic Colours. Yes, there are some linear parts but all sonic games have them, but Sonic Forces does provide interesting pathways for you to go through. The earlier levels are quite linear but as you go through the game it gets a lot better. Plus what adds to the replayability is the custom character's Wispons, which also provide alternates path for the character. The boss fights are also very fun to play and challenging, you're gonna have a good time beating all the bosses in the game.
Speaking of custom character, i'm not really into making oc's and customizing, but the game provides you so many extra accessories for completing extra tasks and getting higher ranks and levels, I found myself going back to the custom character's room to see what's new and what fits my liking. I think that's a huge thing for people who are into character customization.
Modern Sonics levels are also pretty fun to play through, although I should mention that the drift is now removed so sonic team have taken a step backwards in terms of controls for Modern Sonic. But the level design is very fun, again, it has linear sections but later in the game the level design really picks up.
Now let's talk about the elephant in the room, Classic Sonic. I was skeptical about classic sonic going into the game like many others, but I gotta say, it's not that bad and I was quite pleasantly surprised. The levels have many multiple pathways and the controls and physics are better than Generations. That being said, it's no where near as good as Sonic Mania but I think that was bound to happen.
The game does tend to crash on startup sometimes but I think Sonic Team has patched that with the new update as it's been less frequent today. The game does lag sometimes as well, and i'm gonna blame that a bit on optimisation and ofcourse Denuvo, it could've been better. This game had a 4 year development period.
So overall, I enjoyed the game from the start and I'd definitely recommend it to Sonic fans but also casual platforming fans. My only complaint is that Sega should fix the crashing and lag issues with some patches and Modern Sonic's controls could have been better.
My score for the game is 8.5/10

Modern Sonic: Control isn't as great as Generations, but playing on them felt a lot better due to 2D segments not stopping movement completely. A lot of Sonic's stages were pretty linear, but it does get pretty crazy later on in the game. His boss fights were the most fun.
Avatar: I probably enjoyed his stages the most due to it being very different and new to the series. Playing as him forces you to replay some stages a lot and using the correct Wispon to beat it faster or to get all the Red Rings.
Classic Sonic: All of his stages are just completely bad. I was never a fan of his stages in Generations, and they're worse here. I think the only good stage was the Death Egg one. They added drop dash, it's great, but all he gets is a barrier, and it plays like a really boring 2D Sonic game.
The game is very enjoyable, but it definitely has its flaws, especially gimping most of Sonic's controllability to having most of it being automatic. But they did improve my gripes about Generations. It doesn't balance out, but I didn't hate it. This game is definitely a budget game, but with what they had and did. They did well in it. For once, I honestly feel like majority of the stages in this game have a lot of replayability without me hating it. Generations had me only wanting to replay a few stages because it was fun, but this game knocked the ball out of the park with a lot of stages. They're unfortuantely short, but they aren't close to being bad. The avatar stages surprised me, I was skeptical at first, but then his stages got a lot tedius in a good way. It gave me variety of ways to complete the stage. The only main gripe I have about this game is that Classic Sonic was just slapped into the game with no real purpose. Most of, if not all, his stages have no soul or heart. It's almost as if the devs did not care for him to be in the game. Even I didn't want him the game. It felt like a chore almost all the time I had to play his stages. Luckily they weren't hard at all, but I definitely would not replay his stages for fun. If I were to rate this game without any of Classic Sonic's trace in the game. It would honestly be at least an 8 out of 10.
Sega, I thank you for this budget Sonic title. Now, I hope you have the funds to finally produce us the AAA Sonic games again.
Also the music in this game is beautiful. Except Classic Sonic's.

Ok, I'm a big Sonic fan, have been a fan from the start, and know that not alot people like the newer games, but I'm open to opinions which is cool. I have to say, seeing the first trailer to this and finding out you could make your own character for the Sonic World, I was a little bit uneasy to say the least. But now playing a hour of this, has put me at ease:
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay in Sonic Forces is pretty smooth, Modern Sonic stages are built like the Sonic Unleashed Day levels, which to me is perfect since the speed you do around the place is fast paced, plus the flipping to 2D platform is nicely done. Classic Soinic is what you expect of Classic Soinc, 2D platforming from start to end and in my opinion is a nice slow paced change to the speed. The Custom Character is pretty awesome, unlocking different gadget guns that have different traits, and the ability to swing on a zipwire is a nice feature. Score: 5/5
STORY:
The story of Sonic Forces is building up well in my eyes. Eggman taking over the world and Sonic and gang building a Resisitance, to me takes me back to the SATAM Sonic cartoons if you're familiar to them. The voice acting and how the characters move and act is good, even the little radio chatter is nice, got to say, Sonic still has his cool attitude in this one, just like the others before. Score 5/5
CINEMATICS:
This is where I stumble a little in this subject, starting the game the Opening Intro was buggy to begin and I couldn't figure out why, but soon found that if you put the game in Big Picture Mode on Steam and then in the in-game options put the framerate to unlocked, the Intro played without any stuttering coming out of Eggman's mouth. So yeah, there was that, but the cinematics look sharp, clean and no stutter in sight. Score 4/5
OVERALL:
Overall in my opinion, this is up with the good Sonic's, if you loved Unleashed, Colours, Generations, then you'll love this one. If you still feel a little worried about if it's good, bad, or just don't know what to think after Sonic Boom (Cough), then don't worry, take a deep breath, pick up the controller and play. I'm having a real fun time with this one, and hope that the fun doesn't stop. Overall Score 4.5/5
